1"""Chain handlers — one per state transition. 

2 

3Each handler: 

4 * Takes ``(story, app_config, software_factory_root, *, dry_run=False)``. 

5 * Returns a ``HandlerResult`` carrying the next state, an opaque payload, 

6 and an optional error. 

7 * Is responsible for ALL side effects of its transition: LLM calls, 

8 GitHub API calls, filesystem writes, DB writes. 

9 * In ``dry_run=True`` mode, MUST NOT make any LLM calls, MUST NOT touch 

10 GitHub, MUST NOT write to the app repo. The deterministic fixture 

11 payload exercises the downstream state shape. 

12 

13The orchestrator (``factory/chain/orchestrator.py``) decides which handler 

14to invoke based on the story's current state. 

15""" 

16

88def _writing_worktree( 

89 app_config: AppConfig, 

90 software_factory_root: Path, 

91 story: StoryRecord, 

92) -> Path: 

93 """Resolve (and lazily create) the per-story worktree the chain writes 

94 into. 

95 

96 All "writing" handlers — those that run a sandbox, commit, or push — 

97 must use this instead of ``resolve_app_repo_path``. The source repo 

98 at ``app_repo_path`` is the operator's checkout and is treated as 

99 read-only by the chain; each in-flight story gets its own private 

100 worktree under ``state/worktrees/`` so multiple sandboxes can run 

101 in parallel without racing on a shared working tree. 

102 

103 Read-only callsites (context-prelude scans) keep using 

104 ``resolve_app_repo_path`` because they don't mutate state. 

105 """ 

106 import subprocess 

107 

108 from factory.app_config import resolve_app_repo_path 

109 

110 source_repo = resolve_app_repo_path(app_config, software_factory_root) 

111 wt = ensure_worktree_for_story( 

112 source_repo, 

113 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

114 app=story.app, 

115 story_id=story.github_issue_number, 

116 slug=story.slug, 

117 base_branch=app_config.default_branch or "main", 

118 ) 

119 

120 # Refresh the worktree against the CURRENT base before the writing handler 

121 # runs. ensure_worktree_for_story's reuse path returns a worktree cut from 

122 # an OLD base; when a fix merges to main while a story is mid-flight (e.g. a 

123 # sibling un-breaks the test suite), that in-flight story's dev run keeps 

124 # testing against the stale base and can never go green — the dev churns on 

125 # a failure it cannot fix. The PR-open path already re-merges base at PR 

126 # time (see _open_pr_for_story); do the same here so every dev/writing 

127 # attempt sees since-merged fixes. Best-effort and NON-destructive: `git 

128 # merge` preserves uncommitted WIP that doesn't overlap the merged files, 

129 # and on ANY conflict/dirty-overlap we abort and proceed on the current 

130 # base (never silently clobber the dev's in-progress work). 

131 base = app_config.default_branch or "main" 

132 try: 

133 subprocess.run( 

134 ["git", "fetch", "origin", base], 

135 cwd=str(wt), 

136 check=False, 

137 capture_output=True, 

138 timeout=60, 

139 ) 

140 merged = subprocess.run( 

141 ["git", "merge", "--no-edit", f"origin/{base}"], 

142 cwd=str(wt), 

143 capture_output=True, 

144 text=True, 

145 timeout=120, 

146 ) 

147 if merged.returncode != 0: 

148 subprocess.run( 

149 ["git", "merge", "--abort"], 

150 cwd=str(wt), 

151 check=False, 

152 capture_output=True, 

153 timeout=60, 

154 ) 

155 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError): 

156 pass # base refresh is best-effort; never block the writing handler 

157 finally: 

158 # CRITICAL: if the merge timed out or the process was killed mid-merge, 

159 # the except above skips the return-code abort and leaves the worktree 

160 # with MERGE_HEAD + an unmerged index. A later `git add -A` + commit in 

161 # a writing handler would then bake unresolved conflict markers into a 

162 # real commit and push them (silent corruption, worse than a stale 

163 # base). Guarantee no in-progress merge is ever left behind, however 

164 # the merge call exited. 

165 _abort_inflight_merge(wt) 

166 return wt 

167 

168 

169def _abort_inflight_merge(worktree: Path) -> None: 

170 """Best-effort: clear a left-in-progress merge (MERGE_HEAD present) so no 

171 downstream ``git add -A`` + commit can bake conflict markers into a real 

172 commit. Idempotent — a no-op when no merge is in progress.""" 

173 import subprocess 

174 

175 try: 

176 head = subprocess.run( 

177 ["git", "rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "MERGE_HEAD"], 

178 cwd=str(worktree), 

179 capture_output=True, 

180 timeout=15, 

181 ) 

182 if head.returncode == 0: 

183 subprocess.run( 

184 ["git", "merge", "--abort"], 

185 cwd=str(worktree), 

186 check=False, 

187 capture_output=True, 

188 timeout=30, 

189 ) 

190 except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError): 

191 pass 

192

199_MIGRATION_COLUMNS: dict[str, str] = { 

200 # column_name -> SQL type (idempotent ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN if missing). 

201 "sm_result_json": "TEXT", 

202 "last_rejection_reason": "TEXT", 

203 # Docs-chain support. Default ``"tdd"`` keeps pre-existing stories on the 

204 # historical pipeline; new docs-scope stories opt in via PM's child_story 

205 # output (``chain_kind: "docs"``). 

206 "chain_kind": "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'tdd'", 

207 # JSONL of prior dev sandbox attempts (one entry per chain-level retry): 

208 # ``[{attempt, ts, test_output_tail, files_touched, summary}, ...]``. 

209 # Fed forward into the next dev invocation's initial message so the LLM 

210 # sees what it already tried and what failed. 

211 "dev_attempts_json": "TEXT", 

212 # WS4.2 resume-from-checkpoint marker (see StoryRecord.dev_step_checkpoint). 

213 # Nullable TEXT; pre-existing stories gain it as NULL and are unaffected. 

214 "dev_step_checkpoint": "TEXT", 

215 # Item 4 — harness precheck flag. Bool, default 0 (False). SQLite 

216 # stores bool as 0/1 INTEGER; the SQLModel layer coerces on read. 

217 "harness_precheck_passed": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

218 # Hard convergence guard counter. INTEGER default 0; pre-existing stories 

219 # gain it on next visit and start counting from their next reviewer pass. 

220 "reviewer_cycles": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

221 # Review-cycle history (last 4 cycles) — reviewer finality memory + dev's 

222 # "already addressed" digest. See StoryRecord.reviewer_history_json. 

223 "reviewer_history_json": "TEXT", 

224 # WS1.2 independent acceptance oracle. ``acceptance_test_ref`` is the stored 

225 # test path; ``acceptance_expected`` (INTEGER 0/1) is the required/blocking 

226 # source of truth (set at spawn regardless of authoring success). Pre-WS1.2 

227 # stories gain both on next visit: expected defaults 0 so they are never 

228 # retroactively blocked. 

229 "acceptance_test_ref": "TEXT", 

230 "acceptance_expected": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

231 # WS1.1 per-story budget circuit breaker. Aggregate accumulators the 

232 # pre-dispatch breaker reads; without these ALTERs an existing factory.db 

233 # (predating the breaker) raises ``no such column: total_attempts`` on the 

234 # first orchestrator read. Pre-existing stories start at 0 and accrue from 

235 # their next dispatch, so none are retroactively tripped. 

236 "total_attempts": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

237 "total_spend_usd": "REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

238 # WS1.1 advance-decay high-water mark (see StoryRecord.max_progress_ordinal). 

239 # Pre-existing stories start at 0 and register their progress on next visit; 

240 # a story mid-flight simply gets its first decay when it next advances to a 

241 # state above its (freshly-recorded) mark — never retroactively tripped. 

242 "max_progress_ordinal": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

243 # Dependency-deferral cap counter (see StoryRecord.dependency_defer_count). 

244 # Pre-existing rows gain it as 0 and start counting from their next stalled 

245 # deferral — none is retroactively parked. 

246 "dependency_defer_count": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

247 # S4 (019 fail-silent audit) — see StoryRecord.pr_create_retries. 

248 # Pre-existing rows gain it as 0; none is retroactively parked. 

249 "pr_create_retries": "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0", 

250}

253def _ensure_story_columns(eng: Any) -> None: 

254 """Idempotently add Phase 3 columns to the ``stories`` table if missing. 

255 

256 SQLModel.metadata.create_all() only creates tables that don't exist; it 

257 won't add new columns to an existing table. For dev we don't need full 

258 Alembic — just an ``ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`` for the small set of new 

259 columns Phase 3 introduces. Adding a column twice raises; we suppress 

260 that specific failure. 

261 """ 

262 from sqlalchemy import text 

263 

264 from factory.observability.schema import stories_migration_columns 

265 

266 # Use the MERGED column set, not this module's dict alone: the observability 

267 # layer migrates the same table from its own list, and the two had drifted 

268 # apart. Which columns a live factory.db gained used to depend on which 

269 # engine opened it first. 

270 with eng.begin() as conn: 

271 rows = conn.execute(text("PRAGMA table_info(stories)")).fetchall() 

272 existing = {r[1] for r in rows} 

273 for col, sqltype in stories_migration_columns(): 

274 if col in existing: 

275 continue 

276 conn.execute(text(f"ALTER TABLE stories ADD COLUMN {col} {sqltype}")) 

277 

278 

279def _engine(db_path: Path) -> Any: 

280 db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) 

281 eng = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{db_path}", echo=False) 

282 SQLModel.metadata.create_all(eng) 

283 _ensure_story_columns(eng) 

284 return eng

287def persist_story(story: StoryRecord, db_path: Path) -> StoryRecord: 

288 """Insert-or-update ``story`` in ``state/factory.db.stories``.""" 

289 eng = _engine(db_path) 

290 from datetime import UTC, datetime 

291 

292 story.updated_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() 

293 with Session(eng) as session: 

294 session.add(story) 

295 session.commit() 

296 session.refresh(story) 

297 return story

300def get_story(story_id: int, db_path: Path) -> StoryRecord | None: 

301 eng = _engine(db_path) 

302 with Session(eng) as session: 

303 return session.get(StoryRecord, story_id)

306def stories_in_flight(app: str, db_path: Path) -> list[StoryRecord]: 

307 """Return every story whose state is not terminal. 

308 

309 Phase 5 adds DEPLOY_PENDING as an active state (the orchestrator drives 

310 it to DEPLOYED or BLOCKED_DEPLOY_FAILED). DEPLOYED and 

311 BLOCKED_DEPLOY_FAILED are terminal — the chain stops driving once a PR 

312 has been deployed (or its deploy has failed and waits for human 

313 intervention). 

314 """ 

315 eng = _engine(db_path) 

316 with Session(eng) as session: 

317 rows = session.exec(select(StoryRecord).where(StoryRecord.app == app)).all() 

318 # Terminal: PR_OPEN through READY_FOR_MERGE (the auto-merge worker drives 

319 # these by polling, not the orchestrator tick), DEPLOYED, and the two 

320 # blocked states. 

321 terminal = { 

322 StoryState.PR_OPEN.value, 

323 StoryState.CI_PENDING.value, 

324 StoryState.CI_GREEN.value, 

325 StoryState.READY_FOR_MERGE.value, 

326 StoryState.DEPLOYED.value, 

327 StoryState.BLOCKED_TESTS_NEED_CLARIFICATION.value, 

328 StoryState.BLOCKED_DEPLOY_FAILED.value, 

329 # Dual-draft loser: terminal, so its worktree is prunable and it never 

330 # counts as in-flight. 

331 StoryState.SUPERSEDED_BY_SIBLING.value, 

332 # Operator-closed: terminal, worktree prunable, never in-flight. 

333 StoryState.CLOSED_BY_OPERATOR.value, 

334 } 

335 # DEPLOY_PENDING is INTENTIONALLY in-flight so the orchestrator's 

336 # _DISPATCH picks it up for handle_deploy. 

337 return [r for r in rows if r.state not in terminal] 

338

345# A4 whole-DIRECTION budget for the single-story collapse (operator decision 

346# 2026-08-09). Deliberately NOT pm_sync's per-slice ceilings: those exist to 

347# keep each slice inside ONE dev pass's comfort zone, and applying a per-slice 

348# cap (modified_files <= 2) to a SUM refuses any 3-slice split where each 

349# slice touches one file — i.e. the exact direction-120 shape the collapse 

350# was built for. These are sized to what one dev sandbox run can do: the 

351# sandbox allows 600 iterations per story (runner.sandbox_run), so 400 leaves 

352# retry headroom; the file counts allow ~1.5-3x the per-slice caps because a 

353# split duplicates per-slice overhead (tests, plumbing) that a single story 

354# pays once. A direction over THESE budgets keeps its split and is flagged 

355# for the operator to cut into sibling directions. 

356A4_MAX_NEW_FILES_PER_DIRECTION = 8 

357A4_MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_DIRECTION = 6 

358A4_MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_DIRECTION = 400

361_SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+")

364def _slug_of(text: str) -> str: 

365 s = _SLUG_RE.sub("-", text.strip().lower()).strip("-") 

366 return (s[:60] or "story").strip("-") or "story"

369def _author_acceptance_oracle( 

370 story: StoryRecord, 

371 direction: Direction, 

372 app_config: AppConfig, 

373 software_factory_root: Path, 

374 *, 

375 dry_run: bool, 

376 db_path: Path, 

377) -> None: 

378 """WS1.2: author the independent acceptance oracle for a freshly-spawned 

379 story (best-effort, never raises — must not fail story spawn). 

380 

381 Authored here (spawn time, before dev runs) from the SPEC ONLY and stored 

382 outside the dev worktree — see ``factory.chain.acceptance``. author_... 

383 sets ``story.acceptance_expected`` (the required/blocking flag) even when 

384 authoring itself fails, so a flaked author BLOCKS rather than silently 

385 ships; the tick self-heal re-authors it later. 

386 """ 

387 try: 

388 from factory.chain.acceptance import author_acceptance_test 

389 

390 author_acceptance_test( 

391 story, 

392 direction, 

393 app_config, 

394 software_factory_root, 

395 dry_run=dry_run, 

396 db_path=db_path, 

397 ) 

398 except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - oracle authoring must never fail spawn 

399 _logger.warning( 

400 "acceptance oracle authoring raised for story %s (%s): %r — " 

401 "acceptance_expected governs blocking; tick self-heal will retry", 

402 getattr(story, "id", None), 

403 story.slug, 

404 exc, 

405 )

408def handle_stories_spawned( 

409 direction: Direction, 

410 pm_result: dict[str, Any], 

411 app_config: AppConfig, 

412 software_factory_root: Path, 

413 *, 

414 dry_run: bool = False, 

415 db_path: Path | None = None, 

416 github_client: Any = None, 

417) -> list[StoryRecord]: 

418 """For each ``child_story`` in ``pm_result``, create a StoryRecord, optionally 

419 open the GH issue, and write the story file shell to the app repo (if any). 

420 

421 In dry-run mode: 

422 * No GH issue is created; ``github_issue_number`` is ``None``. 

423 * No file is written to the app repo; ``story_file_path`` is a 

424 plausible placeholder under ``stories/0-<slug>.md``. 

425 

426 Phase 7 — dual-draft branch: 

427 * If ``should_spawn_dual_draft(direction, pm_result)`` returns True 

428 (``(explore)`` tag OR PM confidence < 0.6), the chain produces 

429 TWO interpretations and spawns two StoryRecords (one per 

430 interpretation) instead of consuming ``pm_result.child_stories`` 

431 verbatim. Each story carries the ``alt-a`` / ``alt-b`` suffix in 

432 its slug + branch so downstream draft PRs are distinguishable. 

433 """ 

434 from factory.chain.dual_draft import ( 

435 link_alternatives, 

436 produce_interpretations, 

437 should_spawn_dual_draft, 

438 ) 

439 

440 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

441 out: list[StoryRecord] = [] 

442 

443 # Phase 7: dual-draft branch — spawn two interpretation stories, 

444 # regardless of how many child_stories the PM emitted. 

445 if should_spawn_dual_draft(direction, pm_result): 

446 interpretations = produce_interpretations( 

447 direction, 

448 pm_result, 

449 dry_run=dry_run, 

450 ) 

451 # Pick scope from the first child_story if present; otherwise 

452 # default to ``backend`` (most common case for ambiguous asks). 

453 first_child = (pm_result.get("child_stories") or [{}])[0] 

454 scope = str(first_child.get("scope") or "backend") 

455 # ``chain_kind`` is inherited from the first child story since 

456 # dual-draft produces two interpretations of the same underlying 

457 # work item; the variant doesn't change per-interpretation. 

458 chain_kind = str(first_child.get("chain_kind") or "tdd") 

459 

460 for interp in interpretations: 

461 slug_base = _slug_of(interp.title or direction.title or "story") 

462 # ALWAYS preserve the dual-draft interpretation suffix (``-alt-a`` / 

463 # ``-alt-b``). The entire loser-cleanup mechanism identifies siblings 

464 # via a trailing ``-alt-*`` (``dual_draft._DRAFT_ALT_SLUG_RE``). The 

465 # old ``f"{base}-{id}"[:60]`` truncated the SUFFIX off for long 

466 # titles — both siblings collapsed to the same 60-char slug with NO 

467 # ``-alt-*``, so ``_draft_alt_suffix`` returned None, sibling 

468 # detection failed silently, and BOTH interpretations merged (the 

469 # dir 010 over-fire, 2026-07-21). Reserve room for the suffix by 

470 # truncating the BASE, so ``-alt-a``/``-alt-b`` always survives. 

471 _alt = f"-{interp.interpretation_id}" 

472 slug = (slug_base[: max(1, 60 - len(_alt))].strip("-") + _alt) or "story" 

473 title = f"{interp.title}"[:200] 

474 issue_number: int | None = None 

475 story_file_path = f"stories/0-{slug}.md" 

476 if not dry_run and github_client is not None: 

477 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

478 body = ( 

479 f"{interp.body}\n\n" 

480 f"_Direction: `{direction.id}-{direction.slug}` " 

481 f"(tracker: #{direction.state.get('tracker_issue', '?')})._\n" 

482 f"\n_Interpretation: `{interp.interpretation_id}` — " 

483 f"{interp.key_assumption_diff}_\n" 

484 ) 

485 issue = repo.create_issue( 

486 title=title, 

487 body=body, 

488 labels=["story", f"scope/{scope}", "draft-alternative"], 

489 ) 

490 issue_number = int(issue.number) 

491 story_file_path = f"stories/{issue_number}-{slug}.md" 

492 

493 # Dual-draft path: use the first child's points as a hint 

494 # (interpretations share the same underlying work item). 

495 dd_points_raw = first_child.get("points") 

496 try: 

497 dd_points = int(dd_points_raw) if dd_points_raw is not None else 3 

498 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

499 dd_points = 3 

500 from factory.observability.estimator import ( 

501 estimate_story_seconds as _est_secs_dd, 

502 ) 

503 

504 dd_estimated_seconds = _est_secs_dd(db_path=db, points=dd_points, chain_kind=chain_kind) 

505 story = StoryRecord( 

506 direction_id=direction.id or direction.slug, 

507 app=direction.app, 

508 title=title, 

509 slug=slug, 

510 scope=scope, 

511 state=StoryState.STORY_CREATED.value, 

512 chain_kind=chain_kind, 

513 github_issue_number=issue_number, 

514 github_branch=f"story/{issue_number or 0}-{slug}", 

515 story_file_path=story_file_path, 

516 points=dd_points, 

517 estimated_seconds=dd_estimated_seconds, 

518 ) 

519 # Dry-run is a pure preview: build the would-be StoryRecord for 

520 # the returned list but never persist it or author its oracle — 

521 # a persisted dry-run story is a live dispatchable artifact (the 

522 # 2026-07-20 self-tick incident: a "safe" preview spawned rebuild 

523 # stories that the tick then executed). 

524 if not dry_run: 

525 persist_story(story, db) 

526 _author_acceptance_oracle( 

527 story, 

528 direction, 

529 app_config, 

530 software_factory_root, 

531 dry_run=dry_run, 

532 db_path=db, 

533 ) 

534 out.append(story) 

535 

536 # Post the comparison comment on the tracker (real-run only). 

537 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and len(out) >= 2: 

538 try: 

539 link_alternatives( 

540 out[0], 

541 out[1], 

542 interpretations, 

543 direction, 

544 github_client, 

545 app_repo=app_config.repo, 

546 ) 

547 except Exception: 

548 # Never fail the spawn on a comparison-comment hiccup. 

549 pass 

550 return out 

551 

552 # EBS: compute baselines lazily so the very first story spawn after a 

553 # cold start still gets a usable ``estimated_seconds`` (None when no 

554 # samples yet — the Monte Carlo simulator gates on N>=5 to keep cold 

555 # starts from emitting bogus ETAs). 

556 from factory.observability.estimator import estimate_story_seconds 

557 

558 child_stories = pm_result.get("child_stories") or [] 

559 

560 # A4 (operator decision 2026-08-09, per-app flag 

561 # ``gates.single_story_per_ac_direction``): an AC-carrying direction 

562 # spawns exactly ONE story. The acceptance oracle grades EVERY story 

563 # against the DIRECTION's criteria (``_author_acceptance_oracle`` → 

564 # ``list(direction.acceptance)``) — deliberately: scoping the oracle to 

565 # what PM/SM says a story covers would let the chain grade its own 

566 # descoping, a false-green channel. Under that rule a multi-story split is 

567 # structurally broken, not merely wasteful: the first sibling to merge 

568 # satisfies the direction, and every LATER sibling grades green-at-base → 

569 # ``oracle_not_discriminating`` → operator waiver. Observed live 

570 # 2026-08-09: direction 120 spawned 3 slices; story 179 implemented every 

571 # criterion in 22.7 min and siblings 180/181 had to be superseded by hand. 

572 # 

573 # The collapse REFUSES to fire when the children's summed size estimates 

574 # exceed the per-story ceilings PM's re-prompt loop enforces per slice 

575 # (``pm_sync.MAX_*_PER_STORY``) — silently merging N validated slices 

576 # into one over-budget story would trade a visible waiver for an 

577 # invisible budget burn (a timed-out dev run records $0). An oversized 

578 # AC-carrying direction keeps its split and emits 

579 # ``direction_not_single_story_sized``: it needs splitting into sibling 

580 # DIRECTIONS by the operator, which no spawn-time choice can do safely. 

581 # Directions WITHOUT acceptance criteria keep multi-story splits; the 

582 # dual-draft branch above already spawns exactly two competing alternates 

583 # (each stamped with the full-coverage mandate) and is untouched. 

584 from factory.chain.acceptance import acceptance_expected_for 

585 

586 if ( 

587 len(child_stories) > 1 

588 and app_config.gates.single_story_per_ac_direction 

589 and acceptance_expected_for(app_config, direction) 

590 ): 

591 estimate_keys = ( 

592 "estimated_new_files", 

593 "estimated_modified_files", 

594 "estimated_sandbox_iterations", 

595 ) 

596 

597 def _summed(key: str) -> int | None: 

598 """Sum ``key`` over all children; ``None`` when ANY child omits it. 

599 

600 Polarity matters: in pm_sync a missing estimate is a soft warning 

601 that KEEPS the split (safe); here summing missing-as-zero would 

602 COLLAPSE the one direction whose size is unknown (adversarial 

603 replay over the 48 held-out directions: the only collapse 

604 candidate was the pm.md anti-example D007, precisely because its 

605 children carry no estimates). Unknown size ⇒ refuse. 

606 """ 

607 total = 0 

608 for c in child_stories: 

609 try: 

610 total += max(0, int(c.get(key))) 

611 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

612 return None 

613 return total 

614 

615 maybe_sums = {k: _summed(k) for k in estimate_keys} 

616 sums: dict[str, int] = {k: v for k, v in maybe_sums.items() if v is not None} 

617 estimates_complete = len(sums) == len(estimate_keys) 

618 fits = ( 

619 estimates_complete 

620 and sums["estimated_new_files"] <= A4_MAX_NEW_FILES_PER_DIRECTION 

621 and sums["estimated_modified_files"] <= A4_MAX_MODIFIED_FILES_PER_DIRECTION 

622 and sums["estimated_sandbox_iterations"] <= A4_MAX_ITERATIONS_PER_DIRECTION 

623 ) 

624 

625 if not dry_run: # dry-run is a pure preview — write no telemetry 

626 try: 

627 from factory.manager.signals import write_event 

628 

629 write_event( 

630 "chain_steps", 

631 { 

632 "event": ( 

633 "story_split_collapsed" 

634 if fits 

635 else "direction_not_single_story_sized" 

636 ), 

637 "app": direction.app, 

638 "direction_id": direction.id or direction.slug, 

639 "pm_child_count": len(child_stories), 

640 "summed_estimates": sums, 

641 "dropped_titles": ( 

642 [str(c.get("title") or "") for c in child_stories[1:]] 

643 if fits 

644 else [] 

645 ), 

646 "estimates_complete": estimates_complete, 

647 "reason": ( 

648 "acceptance oracle grades direction criteria; " 

649 "one story per AC-carrying direction" 

650 if fits 

651 else ( 

652 "summed slice estimates exceed the whole-" 

653 "direction budget — this direction cannot be " 

654 "one story and, under direction-scoped " 

655 "acceptance grading, cannot safely be many; " 

656 "split it into sibling directions" 

657 if estimates_complete 

658 else "one or more slices carry no size " 

659 "estimates — size unknown, refusing to " 

660 "collapse into a single unbounded story" 

661 ) 

662 ), 

663 }, 

664 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

665 ) 

666 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - telemetry only, never fail spawn 

667 pass 

668 

669 if fits: 

670 merged_rationale = "\n\n".join( 

671 str(c.get("rationale") or "").strip() 

672 for c in child_stories 

673 if str(c.get("rationale") or "").strip() 

674 ) 

675 # Scope: the modal implementation scope. ``docs``/``test`` never 

676 # win — an AC-carrying direction is by definition graded on app 

677 # behaviour, and three personas consume scope (module-doc pointer, 

678 # task_scope, the commit title), so inheriting whatever slice the 

679 # PM happened to list first is a coin flip on a load-bearing value. 

680 impl_scopes = [ 

681 str(c.get("scope") or "").strip() 

682 for c in child_stories 

683 if str(c.get("scope") or "").strip() not in ("", "docs", "test") 

684 ] 

685 # Deterministic tie-break: by count, then alphabetically — 

686 # ``max(set(...), key=count)`` varies with PYTHONHASHSEED on ties, 

687 # and one-backend-one-frontend ties are the common shape. 

688 scope = ( 

689 sorted(set(impl_scopes), key=lambda s: (-impl_scopes.count(s), s))[0] 

690 if impl_scopes 

691 else "backend" 

692 ) 

693 # Points: the SUM (the one story does all the slices' work), 

694 # snapped up to the next Fibonacci value so EBS baselines keyed on 

695 # (persona, points) aren't poisoned by a 2-point label on 3 slices 

696 # of work. 

697 raw_points = 0 

698 for c in child_stories: 

699 try: 

700 raw_points += int(c.get("points")) 

701 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

702 pass 

703 points = next((f for f in (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13) if f >= raw_points), 13) 

704 collapsed: dict[str, Any] = { 

705 # The direction's own title, not the first slice's — a story 

706 # named "happy-path smoke test" under-describes work the 

707 # oracle grades against every criterion. 

708 "title": direction.title or child_stories[0].get("title") or "story", 

709 "scope": scope, 

710 # NEVER inherited: an AC-carrying direction cannot be a docs 

711 # story (the docs chain has no dev and skips the very gates 

712 # the oracle rides on — it would wedge unmergeably). 

713 "chain_kind": "tdd", 

714 "points": points, 

715 "rationale": merged_rationale 

716 or "Single story covering every acceptance criterion of the direction.", 

717 **{k: v for k, v in sums.items()}, 

718 } 

719 child_stories = [collapsed] 

720 

721 for child in child_stories: 

722 slug = _slug_of(child.get("title") or "story") 

723 title = str(child.get("title") or "Untitled story")[:200] 

724 scope = str(child.get("scope") or "backend") 

725 # ``chain_kind`` decides which chain variant drives this story. 

726 # PM emits ``"docs"`` for documentation-only deliverables (the new 

727 # docs chain) and ``"tdd"`` (default) for everything else. 

728 chain_kind = str(child.get("chain_kind") or "tdd") 

729 # EBS: Fibonacci difficulty points from PM; default to 3 (median). 

730 points_raw = child.get("points") 

731 try: 

732 points = int(points_raw) if points_raw is not None else 3 

733 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

734 points = 3 

735 estimated_seconds = estimate_story_seconds(db_path=db, points=points, chain_kind=chain_kind) 

736 issue_number = None 

737 story_file_path = f"stories/0-{slug}.md" 

738 

739 if not dry_run and github_client is not None: 

740 # Real-run: open GH issue, then story_file_path uses the issue number. 

741 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

742 body = ( 

743 f"{child.get('rationale') or ''}\n\n" 

744 f"_Direction: `{direction.id}-{direction.slug}` " 

745 f"(tracker: #{direction.state.get('tracker_issue', '?')})._\n" 

746 ) 

747 issue = repo.create_issue( 

748 title=title, 

749 body=body, 

750 labels=["story", f"scope/{scope}"], 

751 ) 

752 issue_number = int(issue.number) 

753 story_file_path = f"stories/{issue_number}-{slug}.md" 

754 

755 story = StoryRecord( 

756 direction_id=direction.id or direction.slug, 

757 app=direction.app, 

758 title=title, 

759 slug=slug, 

760 scope=scope, 

761 state=StoryState.STORY_CREATED.value, 

762 chain_kind=chain_kind, 

763 github_issue_number=issue_number, 

764 github_branch=f"story/{issue_number or 0}-{slug}", 

765 story_file_path=story_file_path, 

766 points=points, 

767 estimated_seconds=estimated_seconds, 

768 ) 

769 # Dry-run is a pure preview: never persist the story or author its 

770 # oracle (see the dual-draft branch above and the 2026-07-20 incident). 

771 if not dry_run: 

772 persist_story(story, db) 

773 _author_acceptance_oracle( 

774 story, 

775 direction, 

776 app_config, 

777 software_factory_root, 

778 dry_run=dry_run, 

779 db_path=db, 

780 ) 

781 out.append(story) 

782 return out 

783 

784 

785# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

786# sm (Scrum Master) 

787# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

788 

789 

790# Matches a story filename like "0-my-slug.md" or "42-some-thing.md" — the 

791# leading numeric prefix is the issue number (0 = "no issue yet" placeholder). 

792_STORY_FILENAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+)-(.+\.md)$") 

793 

794 

795def _substitute_issue_number_in_path( 

796 target_path_rel: str, 

797 *, 

798 issue_number: int | None, 

799 slug: str, 

800) -> str: 

801 """Substitute the leading ``\\d+-`` prefix in the story filename with the 

802 real ``issue_number`` when known. 

803 

804 Robust to any directory prefix on ``target_path_rel`` (the path's 

805 ``parent`` is preserved verbatim). If ``issue_number`` is None, the path 

806 is returned unchanged. If the filename doesn't carry a numeric prefix at 

807 all, we fall back to ``stories/<issue_number>-<slug>.md`` so the chain 

808 still finds the file by convention. 

809 """ 

810 if issue_number is None: 

811 return target_path_rel 

812 path = Path(target_path_rel) 

813 m = _STORY_FILENAME_RE.match(path.name) 

814 if m is not None: 

815 # Only substitute when the existing prefix is the "no issue yet" 

816 # placeholder (``0``). A real issue number that disagrees with the 

817 # story's ``github_issue_number`` is left alone — this is more likely 

818 # a chain bug (split story?) than the SM's intent. 

819 if m.group(1) == "0": 

820 new_name = f"{issue_number}-{m.group(2)}" 

821 return str(path.with_name(new_name)) 

822 return target_path_rel 

823 # No numeric prefix; conventionalize. 

824 return f"stories/{issue_number}-{slug}.md" 

825 

826 

827def _dry_run_sm( 

828 story: StoryRecord, direction: Direction | None, software_factory_root: Path 

829) -> dict[str, Any]: 

830 """Deterministic Scrum-Master result for dry-run mode. 

831 

832 Produces a BMAD-format story file embedding: 

833 * the direction's flow.md verbatim if present 

834 * the direction's api_spec.md verbatim if present 

835 * acceptance criteria verbatim 

836 * pointers to context/current-state.md and context/modules/<scope>.md. 

837 """ 

838 flow_text = "" 

839 api_text = "" 

840 acceptance_lines: list[str] = [] 

841 if direction is not None: 

842 if direction.has_flow: 

843 try: 

844 flow_text = (direction.dir_path / "flow.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip() 

845 except FileNotFoundError: 

846 flow_text = "" 

847 if direction.has_api_spec: 

848 try: 

849 api_text = (direction.dir_path / "api_spec.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip() 

850 except FileNotFoundError: 

851 api_text = "" 

852 acceptance_lines = list(direction.acceptance) 

853 

854 ac_block = ( 

855 "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {ac}" for i, ac in enumerate(acceptance_lines)) 

856 if acceptance_lines 

857 else "1. (no explicit acceptance criteria — see Dev Notes)" 

858 ) 

859 

860 dev_notes_parts = [ 

861 "- Story carries verbatim embeds of user-supplied artifacts below.", 

862 f"- Read context/current-state.md and context/modules/{story.scope}.md before " 

863 "implementing.", 

864 "[Source: context/current-state.md]", 

865 f"[Source: context/modules/{story.scope}.md]", 

866 ] 

867 if flow_text: 

868 dev_notes_parts.append("\n#### Flow (verbatim from direction)\n\n" + flow_text) 

869 if api_text: 

870 dev_notes_parts.append("\n#### API spec (verbatim from direction)\n\n" + api_text) 

871 dev_notes_parts.append("\n#### Acceptance criteria (verbatim from direction)\n\n" + ac_block) 

872 dev_notes = "\n".join(dev_notes_parts) 

873 

874 file_content = ( 

875 f"# Story 1.1: {story.title}\n\n" 

876 "Status: ready-for-dev\n\n" 

877 "## Story\n\n" 

878 f"As a user, I want {story.title.lower()}, so that the documented outcome holds.\n\n" 

879 "## Acceptance Criteria\n\n" 

880 f"{ac_block}\n\n" 

881 "## Tasks / Subtasks\n\n" 

882 "- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #1)\n" 

883 " - [ ] Subtask 1.1\n\n" 

884 "## Dev Notes\n\n" 

885 f"{dev_notes}\n\n" 

886 "### References\n\n" 

887 f"- [Source: context/modules/{story.scope}.md]\n" 

888 "- [Source: context/current-state.md]\n\n" 

889 "## Dev Agent Record\n\n" 

890 "### Agent Model Used\n\n" 

891 "(populated by dev)\n\n" 

892 "### File List\n\n" 

893 "## Senior Developer Review\n\n" 

894 "## Review Follow-ups\n" 

895 ) 

896 

897 return { 

898 "stories": [ 

899 { 

900 "title": story.title, 

901 "slug": story.slug, 

902 "scope": story.scope, 

903 "file_content": file_content, 

904 "target_path": story.story_file_path 

905 or f"stories/{story.github_issue_number or 0}-{story.slug}.md", 

906 } 

907 ], 

908 "summary": f"Dry-run SM story for {story.slug!r}.", 

909 } 

910 

911 

912_SM_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = { 

913 "type": "object", 

914 "required": ["stories", "summary"], 

915 "properties": { 

916 "stories": { 

917 "type": "array", 

918 "items": { 

919 "type": "object", 

920 "required": ["title", "slug", "scope", "file_content", "target_path"], 

921 "properties": { 

922 "title": {"type": "string"}, 

923 "slug": {"type": "string"}, 

924 "scope": {"type": "string"}, 

925 "file_content": {"type": "string"}, 

926 "target_path": {"type": "string"}, 

927 }, 

928 }, 

929 }, 

930 "summary": {"type": "string"}, 

931 }, 

932} 

933 

934 

935#: Marker opening the code-appended block below. Also the idempotence guard — 

936#: a re-run of SM over an already-stamped file must not stack the block twice. 

937_FULL_COVERAGE_MARKER = "<!-- factory:dual-draft-full-coverage -->" 

938 

939 

940def _with_full_coverage_mandate( 

941 file_content: str, story: StoryRecord, direction: Any, *, ac_single_story: bool = False 

942) -> str: 

943 """Stamp a story file with every direction AC when the oracle grades them all. 

944 

945 Fires for a dual-draft alternate (always — PR #268), and, when 

946 ``ac_single_story`` is True, for the only story of an AC-carrying 

947 direction (A4, 2026-08-09): in both shapes the acceptance oracle grades 

948 the story against the whole direction and no sibling exists to pick up a 

949 deferred criterion. 

950 

951 The prompt above tells SM that ``alt-a``/``alt-b`` are COMPETING attempts at 

952 the whole direction. This is the same statement enforced in CODE, because a 

953 prompt is a request and this invariant is load-bearing: 

954 

955 * ``explore: true`` directions spawn two alternates; measured over the 

956 sacrifice ledger, 23 such pairs resolved 23 ``deployed`` / 

957 20 ``superseded_by_sibling``. One ships, one is closed. There is no third 

958 story. 

959 * The acceptance oracle grades every story against the DIRECTION's criteria 

960 (``_author_acceptance_oracle`` → ``list(direction.acceptance)``), never 

961 the story's. 

962 

963 So an alternate that defers a criterion is graded on work nobody was asked 

964 to do. Observed live 2026-08-08 on sacrifice story 173 (direction 117): SM 

965 wrote "token lifecycle ... is out of scope for this narrow-read story; it 

966 belongs to sibling stories that implement token model and consumption" — no 

967 such sibling exists, dev faithfully built only the guard, and the story was 

968 unmergeable before dev's first line of code. 

969 

970 Appending rather than validating-and-rejecting is deliberate: a reject loop 

971 costs another SM call and can fail three times and terminally block, which 

972 trades a late block for an earlier one. This makes the requirement present 

973 in the artifact dev actually reads, with no extra LLM spend and no new 

974 failure mode. Non-alternate stories of a MULTI-story split are returned 

975 untouched — a genuine split (only possible when no oracle grades it, or 

976 the A4 collapse refused an oversized direction) SHOULD scope each story 

977 narrowly. 

978 """ 

979 # Lazy, like every other ``dual_draft`` use in this module — keeps the 

980 # import graph minimal for tests that import handlers without the chain. 

981 from factory.chain.dual_draft import _draft_alt_suffix 

982 

983 is_alternate = _draft_alt_suffix(story.slug or "") is not None 

984 if not is_alternate and not ac_single_story: 

985 return file_content 

986 acceptance = list(getattr(direction, "acceptance", None) or []) 

987 if not acceptance: 

988 return file_content 

989 if _FULL_COVERAGE_MARKER in file_content: 

990 return file_content 

991 criteria = "\n".join(f"- [ ] {ac}" for ac in acceptance) 

992 if is_alternate: 

993 heading = "## Required coverage — this is a COMPETING alternate" 

994 framing = ( 

995 "This story is one of two rival attempts at the whole direction " 

996 "(`narrow read` / `broad read`). Exactly one ships; the other is closed " 

997 "as `superseded_by_sibling`. **There is no sibling story that will " 

998 "implement anything deferred here**, and the acceptance oracle grades " 

999 "this story against every criterion below." 

1000 ) 

1001 else: 

1002 heading = "## Required coverage — the acceptance oracle grades the whole direction" 

1003 framing = ( 

1004 "This story is the direction's ONLY story. An independent acceptance " 

1005 "oracle grades it at merge time against every criterion below — never " 

1006 "against a subset the story text declares in scope. **No sibling story " 

1007 "exists or will be created**, so anything deferred here is built by " 

1008 "nobody and the story is then graded against it and blocked." 

1009 ) 

1010 return ( 

1011 f"{file_content.rstrip()}\n\n" 

1012 f"{_FULL_COVERAGE_MARKER}\n" 

1013 f"{heading}\n\n" 

1014 f"{framing}\n\n" 

1015 "Implement ALL of them:\n\n" 

1016 f"{criteria}\n\n" 

1017 "Anything above that the body of this story describes as out of scope, " 

1018 "deferred, or belonging to another story is an ERROR in the story text — " 

1019 "the criteria here win.\n" 

1020 ) 

1021 

1022 

1023def handle_sm( 

1024 story: StoryRecord, 

1025 app_config: AppConfig, 

1026 software_factory_root: Path, 

1027 *, 

1028 dry_run: bool = False, 

1029 db_path: Path | None = None, 

1030 fixture: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

1031) -> HandlerResult: 

1032 """Run the Scrum-Master persona; write the BMAD story file to disk. 

1033 

1034 In dry-run mode: deterministic fixture story is composed from the 

1035 direction's flow.md / api_spec.md / acceptance criteria (if any). The 

1036 story file is written to ``apps/<app>/stories/<issue|0>-<slug>.md``. 

1037 In real-run mode: invokes ``text_run("sm", ...)`` with the SM persona 

1038 prompt + context prelude + PM result + Direction. The chain writes the 

1039 file content from the SM result. 

1040 """ 

1041 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

1042 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_SM_STARTED).value 

1043 persist_story(story, db) 

1044 

1045 direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

1046 

1047 if fixture is not None: 

1048 result = fixture 

1049 elif dry_run: 

1050 result = _dry_run_sm(story, direction, software_factory_root) 

1051 else: 

1052 from factory.app_config import resolve_app_repo_path 

1053 from factory.context.loader import compose_context_prelude 

1054 from factory.directions.parser import get_direction_chain 

1055 from factory.runner import text_run 

1056 

1057 persona = "sm" 

1058 persona_prompt = _read_persona_prompt(persona) 

1059 chain = ( 

1060 get_direction_chain(direction, software_factory_root) if direction is not None else None 

1061 ) 

1062 prelude = compose_context_prelude( 

1063 persona=persona, 

1064 app_repo_path=resolve_app_repo_path(app_config, software_factory_root), 

1065 task_scope=story.scope, 

1066 direction_chain=chain, 

1067 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

1068 ) 

1069 flow_text = "" 

1070 api_text = "" 

1071 direction_body = "" 

1072 pm_block = "" 

1073 if direction is not None: 

1074 direction_body = direction.raw_body 

1075 if direction.has_flow: 

1076 try: 

1077 flow_text = (direction.dir_path / "flow.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8") 

1078 except FileNotFoundError: 

1079 flow_text = "" 

1080 if direction.has_api_spec: 

1081 try: 

1082 api_text = (direction.dir_path / "api_spec.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8") 

1083 except FileNotFoundError: 

1084 api_text = "" 

1085 pm_result = direction.state.get("pm_result") or {} 

1086 try: 

1087 pm_block = json.dumps(pm_result, indent=2) 

1088 except TypeError: 

1089 pm_block = "(pm_result not JSON-serializable)" 

1090 

1091 full_prompt = ( 

1092 f"{persona_prompt.rstrip()}\n\n" 

1093 "---\n\n" 

1094 "## Context\n\n" 

1095 f"{prelude.rstrip()}\n\n" 

1096 "## PM result\n\n" 

1097 f"```json\n{pm_block}\n```\n\n" 

1098 "## Direction\n\n" 

1099 f"{direction_body.rstrip()}\n\n" 

1100 f"### flow.md\n\n{flow_text.rstrip() if flow_text else '(none)'}\n\n" 

1101 f"### api_spec.md\n\n{api_text.rstrip() if api_text else '(none)'}\n\n" 

1102 "## YOUR ASSIGNMENT — exactly ONE story file\n\n" 

1103 "This invocation prepares the story file for exactly ONE StoryRecord\n" 

1104 "(the chain runs you once per record). The PM result's child_stories\n" 

1105 "above are decomposition CONTEXT — scope boundaries and sequencing —\n" 

1106 "NOT a list of files to emit. If this record is the direction's ONLY\n" 

1107 "story, any sibling or sequencing references in that context are\n" 

1108 "VOID: no sibling exists or will exist, so nothing may be deferred\n" 

1109 "to one. Your `stories` array MUST contain\n" 

1110 "EXACTLY ONE entry, with `slug` set EXACTLY to the value below\n" 

1111 "(verbatim — the chain matches on it and refuses to write on\n" 

1112 "mismatch). If this record is one interpretation of a dual-draft\n" 

1113 "pair (title suffixed 'narrow read'/'broad read'), scope the story\n" 

1114 "content to THAT interpretation.\n\n" 

1115 "### Dual-draft alternates are COMPETING, not COMPLEMENTARY\n\n" 

1116 "'narrow read' and 'broad read' are two rival attempts at the WHOLE\n" 

1117 "direction. Exactly one of them ships; the other is closed as\n" 

1118 "`superseded_by_sibling`. They are NOT a decomposition, and the\n" 

1119 "other alternate is NOT a follow-up that will finish your work.\n\n" 

1120 "Therefore EVERY alternate MUST cover EVERY acceptance criterion\n" 

1121 "in the direction. The narrow/broad axis is how much you do BEYOND\n" 

1122 "the criteria (narrow: nothing beyond; broad: adjacent rough edges\n" 

1123 "too) — it is NEVER which criteria you cover.\n\n" 

1124 "Do NOT defer, descope, or mark a criterion out-of-scope, and do NOT\n" 

1125 "say a 'sibling story' will implement it. For a dual-draft pair no\n" 

1126 "such sibling is ever created, so anything you defer is built by\n" 

1127 "NOBODY and the story is then graded against it and blocked.\n" 

1128 "If a criterion is genuinely untestable as written, still IMPLEMENT\n" 

1129 "it and say why it is hard to observe — do not drop it.\n\n" 

1130 f"- title: {story.title}\n" 

1131 f"- slug: {story.slug}\n" 

1132 f"- scope: {story.scope}\n" 

1133 f"- target_path: {story.story_file_path}\n\n" 

1134 "Return the JSON object. No prose outside the JSON." 

1135 ) 

1136 model_id = route(persona) 

1137 result_any = text_run( 

1138 persona=persona, 

1139 prompt=full_prompt, 

1140 model_id=model_id, 

1141 schema=_SM_SCHEMA, 

1142 max_tokens=max_output_tokens_for(model_id), 

1143 story_id=story.id, 

1144 app=story.app, 

1145 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

1146 db_path=db, 

1147 ) 

1148 if not isinstance(result_any, dict): 

1149 return HandlerResult( 

1150 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

1151 error="sm returned non-dict", 

1152 ) 

1153 result = result_any 

1154 

1155 # Find the story entry that matches this StoryRecord. The DB slug is 

1156 # TRUNCATED (column cap) while the SM emits full slugs, so exact equality 

1157 # misses (e.g. "...llm-match-cont" vs "...llm-match-contract") — match by 

1158 # prefix in either direction. And NEVER fall back to "the first story": 

1159 # that silent default wrote the FIRST sibling's contract into 9 stories' 

1160 # files (D009/D010, found 2026-06-11) — dev faithfully re-built story 

1161 # 22's scope under story 23's title, the reviewer approved it against the 

1162 # same wrong file, and the duplicate PR conflicted with the real merged 

1163 # implementation. Writing the wrong contract is strictly worse than 

1164 # failing loudly. 

1165 stories_out = result.get("stories") or [] 

1166 matched: dict[str, Any] | None = None 

1167 for s in stories_out: 

1168 s_slug = str(s.get("slug") or "") 

1169 if s_slug == story.slug or ( 

1170 s_slug and (s_slug.startswith(story.slug) or story.slug.startswith(s_slug)) 

1171 ): 

1172 matched = s 

1173 break 

1174 

1175 if matched is None: 

1176 # Slug mismatch: do NOT advance. Advancing to SM_DONE without a 

1177 # written file poisons dispatch forever (dev dies on 

1178 # FileNotFoundError every tick — observed 2026-07-17 when dual-draft 

1179 # records met an SM that emitted per-child_story files). Reset to 

1180 # STORY_CREATED so the next tick re-runs SM against the (now 

1181 # single-story-explicit) prompt; the mismatch is loud in the story 

1182 # event log either way. 

1183 story.error = ( 

1184 f"sm output has no story matching slug {story.slug!r} " 

1185 f"(got: {[str(s.get('slug'))[:40] for s in stories_out[:6]]!r}); " 

1186 "refusing to write a sibling's contract into this story's file" 

1187 ) 

1188 story.state = StoryState.STORY_CREATED.value 

1189 story.sm_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

1190 log_story_event( 

1191 story.id, 

1192 "sm_slug_mismatch", 

1193 { 

1194 "expected_slug": story.slug, 

1195 "got_slugs": [str(s.get("slug"))[:60] for s in stories_out[:12]], 

1196 }, 

1197 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

1198 slug_hint=story.slug, 

1199 ) 

1200 persist_story(story, db) 

1201 return HandlerResult( 

1202 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

1203 payload=result, 

1204 error=story.error, 

1205 ) 

1206 

1207 # Resolve the on-disk target path. Prefer the SM's emitted target_path; if 

1208 # the filename leads with a numeric prefix (the SM's "<issue-number>" 

1209 # placeholder; ``0-`` in dry-run, but could be any digits a stale fixture 

1210 # carries) and we now know the real issue number, substitute it. Robust 

1211 # to any directory prefix (``stories/...``, ``apps/<x>/stories/...``). 

1212 target_path_rel = str(matched.get("target_path") or story.story_file_path) 

1213 target_path_rel = _substitute_issue_number_in_path( 

1214 target_path_rel, 

1215 issue_number=story.github_issue_number, 

1216 slug=story.slug, 

1217 ) 

1218 

1219 # A4: the mandate also fires for the ONLY story of an AC-carrying 

1220 # direction (gated on the same per-app flag as the spawn-time collapse). 

1221 # Fail direction on any lookup error is NO stamp — SM may then descope and 

1222 # the story blocks at the gate: a recoverable false-block, never a 

1223 # false-green. 

1224 ac_single_story = False 

1225 try: 

1226 if ( 

1227 app_config is not None 

1228 and app_config.gates.single_story_per_ac_direction 

1229 and direction is not None 

1230 ): 

1231 from factory.chain.acceptance import acceptance_expected_for 

1232 

1233 if acceptance_expected_for(app_config, direction): 

1234 from sqlmodel import Session, create_engine, select 

1235 

1236 eng = create_engine(f"sqlite:///{db}", echo=False) 

1237 with Session(eng) as session: 

1238 sibs = session.exec( 

1239 select(StoryRecord).where( 

1240 StoryRecord.direction_id == story.direction_id, 

1241 StoryRecord.app == story.app, 

1242 ) 

1243 ).all() 

1244 # "Only story" means only LIVE story: terminal rows 

1245 # (superseded losers, closed_by_operator, prior blocked 

1246 # attempts) do no further work, so their existence must not 

1247 # stop the stamp — else any direction with history never 

1248 # earns it again. The story must also actually be in the 

1249 # query result (an empty result proves nothing). 

1250 others_live = [ 

1251 s 

1252 for s in sibs 

1253 if s.id != story.id and not is_terminal(StoryState(s.state)) 

1254 ] 

1255 ac_single_story = ( 

1256 any(s.id == story.id for s in sibs) and not others_live 

1257 ) 

1258 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no stamp is the recoverable direction 

1259 ac_single_story = False 

1260 

1261 target_abs = software_factory_root / "apps" / story.app / target_path_rel 

1262 target_abs.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) 

1263 target_abs.write_text( 

1264 _with_full_coverage_mandate( 

1265 matched.get("file_content") or "", story, direction, ac_single_story=ac_single_story 

1266 ), 

1267 encoding="utf-8", 

1268 ) 

1269 story.story_file_path = target_path_rel 

1270 story.sm_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

1271 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_SM_DONE).value 

1272 persist_story(story, db) 

1273 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result) 

1274

1305def _read_persona_prompt(persona: str) -> str: 

1306 """Defer to the runner's reader to avoid duplicating the personas dir constant.""" 

1307 from factory.runner import _read_persona_prompt as _rpp 

1308 

1309 return _rpp(persona) 

1310 

1311 

1312def _finding_location_file(f: dict[str, Any]) -> str: 

1313 """Normalize a finding's location to its file path (drop :line, lowercase). 

1314 

1315 Line numbers shift as dev edits; the FILE is the stable identity of where 

1316 a defect lives. Findings without a location normalize to "" (excluded 

1317 from location-set comparisons). 

1318 """ 

1319 loc = str(f.get("location") or f.get("file") or "").strip().lower() 

1320 return loc.split(":", 1)[0].strip() 

1321 

1322 

1323def _extract_json_object(text: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: 

1324 """Best-effort parse of a JSON object from an LLM text response. 

1325 

1326 The reviewer is dispatched with ``schema=None`` (its output is large and we 

1327 don't want the runner's json_object mode / doubling ladder here), so the 

1328 raw model text can arrive fenced in ```json ... ``` or with a stray 

1329 sentence before/after the object. A bare ``json.loads`` silently fails on 

1330 those and the caller would degrade to an empty ``request_changes`` — losing 

1331 every finding and churning the loop. This recovers the object in three 

1332 escalating steps: (1) parse as-is; (2) strip a Markdown code fence; 

1333 (3) slice from the first ``{`` to the last ``}``. Returns ``None`` only 

1334 when no JSON object can be recovered — the caller MUST treat that as 

1335 ``request_changes`` (never a silent approve). 

1336 """ 

1337 if not isinstance(text, str): 

1338 return text if isinstance(text, dict) else None 

1339 

1340 def _as_obj(s: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None: 

1341 try: 

1342 parsed = json.loads(s) 

1343 except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): 

1344 return None 

1345 return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None 

1346 

1347 candidate = text.strip() 

1348 obj = _as_obj(candidate) 

1349 if obj is not None: 

1350 return obj 

1351 

1352 # Strip a fenced block: ```json\n{...}\n``` (or plain ```), keeping body. 

1353 if candidate.startswith("```"): 

1354 body = candidate[3:] 

1355 if body[:4].lower() == "json": 

1356 body = body[4:] 

1357 body = body.strip() 

1358 if body.endswith("```"): 

1359 body = body[:-3].strip() 

1360 obj = _as_obj(body) 

1361 if obj is not None: 

1362 return obj 

1363 

1364 # Last resort: slice the outermost brace span. 

1365 start = candidate.find("{") 

1366 end = candidate.rfind("}") 

1367 if start != -1 and end != -1 and end > start: 

1368 obj = _as_obj(candidate[start : end + 1]) 

1369 if obj is not None: 

1370 return obj 

1371 return None 

1372 

1373 

1374def _parse_tech_writer_result(result_any: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None: 

1375 """Parse + shape-check tech_writer output. Returns ``None`` on anything 

1376 that is not a usable result — the caller retries, then blocks fail-closed. 

1377 

1378 Deliberately STRICTER than the reviewer's ``_extract_json_object``: no 

1379 brace-slice. The tech_writer prompt embeds a complete example object, so 

1380 slicing the outermost ``{...}`` out of a prose response can capture the 

1381 prompt's own echoed example — one such shape (``context_updates: []`` with 

1382 ``no_updates_needed: false``) parks the story behind a docs-current gate 

1383 that can never pass, and another (``no_updates_needed: true``) is a FALSE 

1384 GREEN on a merged PR with stale context docs. Fence-stripping alone covers 

1385 the observed failure (story 177 attempt 1: a fully valid object inside a 

1386 ```json fence, rejected by the old bare ``json.loads``); everything 

1387 stranger stays a loud parse failure. 

1388 

1389 The shape check exists so a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped body 

1390 (e.g. ``context_updates`` as a list of strings) fails HERE — a retryable 

1391 parse failure — rather than as an uncaught ``TypeError`` in the 

1392 ``ContextUpdate`` build after the result was already persisted. 

1393 """ 

1394 candidate: dict[str, Any] | None = None 

1395 if isinstance(result_any, dict): 

1396 candidate = result_any 

1397 elif isinstance(result_any, str): 

1398 text = result_any.strip() 

1399 try: 

1400 parsed = json.loads(text) 

1401 except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): 

1402 parsed = None 

1403 if text.startswith("```"): 

1404 body = text[3:] 

1405 if body[:4].lower() == "json": 

1406 body = body[4:] 

1407 body = body.strip() 

1408 if body.endswith("```"): 

1409 body = body[:-3].strip() 

1410 try: 

1411 parsed = json.loads(body) 

1412 except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): 

1413 parsed = None 

1414 candidate = parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None 

1415 if candidate is None: 

1416 return None 

1417 

1418 updates = candidate.get("context_updates") 

1419 no_updates = bool(candidate.get("no_updates_needed")) 

1420 if updates is None: 

1421 return candidate if no_updates else None 

1422 if not isinstance(updates, list): 

1423 return None 

1424 for u in updates: 

1425 if not isinstance(u, dict) or not isinstance(u.get("path"), str) or not u["path"]: 

1426 return None 

1427 if not updates and not no_updates: 

1428 # "Docs are stale but here are zero updates" — the docs-current gate 

1429 # can never satisfy this; persisting it strands the story terminally. 

1430 return None 

1431 return candidate 

1432 

1433 

1434def _parse_reviewer_result(result_any: Any) -> dict[str, Any]: 

1435 """Normalize the reviewer's raw output into a review result dict. 

1436 

1437 The reviewer runs schema-free, so the raw text may be fenced or 

1438 prose-wrapped; ``_extract_json_object`` recovers the object (fence-strip / 

1439 brace-slice) before we give up. A genuine parse failure degrades to 

1440 ``request_changes`` WITH a synthetic rubric finding — never a silent 

1441 approve, and never an empty ``request_changes`` the dev can't act on. The 

1442 synthetic finding carries a rubric ``criterion`` so it flows through the 

1443 same signature / history / dev-findings plumbing as a real one. 

1444 """ 

1445 result = result_any if isinstance(result_any, dict) else _extract_json_object(result_any) 

1446 if isinstance(result, dict) and "verdict" in result: 

1447 return result 

1448 return { 

1449 "verdict": "request_changes", 

1450 "test_quality_score": 0.0, 

1451 "findings": [ 

1452 { 

1453 "severity": "high", 

1454 "criterion": "contract", 

1455 "location": "(reviewer output):0", 

1456 "what": ( 

1457 "Reviewer response was not valid rubric JSON; re-review " 

1458 "required (safe fallback — not an approval)." 

1459 ), 

1460 "fix_suggestion": ( 

1461 "No actionable code change parsed; the reviewer will " 

1462 "re-run. If this recurs, the reviewer model is not " 

1463 "emitting the JSON contract." 

1464 ), 

1465 } 

1466 ], 

1467 "test_quality_findings": [], 

1468 "summary": "reviewer JSON parse failed", 

1469 } 

1470 

1471 

1472# Fixed rubric axes the reviewer grades against. ``scope``/``style`` are 

1473# non-blocking by construction (the persona clamps them to ``low``); the rest 

1474# may be blocking. Kept here so the parse-fallback and the signature agree on 

1475# the vocabulary. An unknown/absent criterion normalizes to "" — it still 

1476# participates in the signature (via location + text) but carries no rubric 

1477# axis, which is the correct backward-compatible behavior for pre-rubric output. 

1478_RUBRIC_CRITERIA = frozenset({"correctness", "contract", "security", "tests", "scope", "style"}) 

1479 

1480 

1481def _finding_criterion(f: dict[str, Any]) -> str: 

1482 """Normalized rubric criterion for a finding ("" when absent/unknown).""" 

1483 crit = str(f.get("criterion") or "").strip().lower() 

1484 return crit if crit in _RUBRIC_CRITERIA else "" 

1485 

1486 

1487def _findings_signature(result: dict[str, Any]) -> str: 

1488 """Stable hash of a review's actionable findings (order-independent). 

1489 

1490 Keys on a NORMALIZED structured signature per finding: location FILE + 

1491 rubric ``criterion`` + ``what``/``issue`` text. Two cycles flagging the 

1492 same site on the same rubric axis count as "same" even when the reviewer 

1493 rewords the complaint (rewording defeated the text-only signature — 

1494 benchmark t3, 2026-07-17, six cycles with consecutive_same=1 throughout). 

1495 The criterion is part of the key so a genuinely different rubric objection 

1496 at the same file (e.g. a NEW ``security`` finding where cycle-1 raised 

1497 ``style``) reads as PROGRESS, not a stuck repeat. Line number is 

1498 deliberately excluded — it shifts as the dev edits, and file-grain identity 

1499 is what the 2026-07-17 fix established. Pre-rubric findings (no criterion) 

1500 normalize to "" and hash exactly as before, so the guard is unchanged for 

1501 legacy output. 

1502 """ 

1503 import hashlib 

1504 

1505 parts = [] 

1506 for f in (result.get("findings") or []) + (result.get("test_quality_findings") or []): 

1507 if isinstance(f, dict): 

1508 loc = _finding_location_file(f) 

1509 crit = _finding_criterion(f) 

1510 what = (f.get("what") or f.get("issue") or "").strip().lower()[:160] 

1511 key = "|".join(p for p in (loc, crit, what) if p) 

1512 parts.append(key) 

1513 digest = hashlib.sha256(" ".join(sorted(parts)).encode("utf-8", "replace")) 

1514 return digest.hexdigest()[:16] 

1515 

1516 

1517_REVIEWER_HISTORY_MAX_CYCLES = 4 

1518 

1519 

1520def _append_reviewer_history(story: StoryRecord, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None: 

1521 """Append this cycle's review to ``story.reviewer_history_json`` (capped). 

1522 

1523 Stores a digest, not the full result: enough for the reviewer to honor 

1524 finality (location + what + severity + regression flag) and for dev's 

1525 do-not-regress section, without unbounded prompt growth. 

1526 """ 

1527 

1528 def _digest(findings: Any, *, is_test: bool = False) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: 

1529 out = [] 

1530 for f in findings or []: 

1531 if not isinstance(f, dict): 

1532 continue 

1533 out.append( 

1534 { 

1535 "severity": f.get("severity", "medium" if not is_test else "low"), 

1536 "criterion": _finding_criterion(f) or ("tests" if is_test else ""), 

1537 "location": str(f.get("location") or f.get("test_name") or "")[:160], 

1538 "what": str(f.get("what") or f.get("issue") or "")[:200], 

1539 "regression": bool(f.get("regression")), 

1540 } 

1541 ) 

1542 return out 

1543 

1544 entry = { 

1545 "cycle": story.reviewer_cycles, 

1546 "verdict": result.get("verdict", "request_changes"), 

1547 "score": result.get("test_quality_score"), 

1548 "findings": _digest(result.get("findings")), 

1549 "test_quality_findings": _digest(result.get("test_quality_findings"), is_test=True), 

1550 } 

1551 try: 

1552 history = json.loads(story.reviewer_history_json or "[]") 

1553 if not isinstance(history, list): 

1554 history = [] 

1555 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

1556 history = [] 

1557 history.append(entry) 

1558 story.reviewer_history_json = json.dumps(history[-_REVIEWER_HISTORY_MAX_CYCLES:]) 

1559 

1560 

1561def _render_reviewer_history_section(story: StoryRecord) -> str: 

1562 """The "Your previous findings" prompt section for re-reviews. 

1563 

1564 Empty string on the first review. This is what makes the persona's 

1565 finality rule ENFORCEABLE — without it the reviewer has no memory of its 

1566 own prior verdicts and re-derives fresh objections every cycle. 

1567 """ 

1568 try: 

1569 history = json.loads(story.reviewer_history_json or "[]") 

1570 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

1571 history = [] 

1572 if not history: 

1573 return "" 

1574 lines = [ 

1575 "## Your previous findings (this is a RE-REVIEW — read before judging)", 

1576 "", 

1577 "You have reviewed this story before. Per the Review-finality rule, a", 

1578 "new `medium`/`high` finding is legitimate ONLY as (a) a regression", 

1579 'since your last review (mark `"regression": true`) or (b) one of', 

1580 "the findings below not actually addressed. Anything else is `low` /", 

1581 "`comments_to_post`. At cycle 3+ the chain clamps non-compliant", 

1582 "blocking findings to non-blocking.", 

1583 "", 

1584 ] 

1585 for entry in history: 

1586 lines.append(f"### Cycle {entry.get('cycle')} — verdict: {entry.get('verdict')}") 

1587 for f in (entry.get("findings") or []) + (entry.get("test_quality_findings") or []): 

1588 # Legacy history (written before _digest's isinstance guard) can 

1589 # contain a bare-string finding; skip it rather than crash the 

1590 # whole tick with "'str' object has no attribute 'get'". Mirrors 

1591 # the guards in _findings_signature and _append_reviewer_history. 

1592 if not isinstance(f, dict): 

1593 continue 

1594 reg = " (regression)" if f.get("regression") else "" 

1595 crit = f.get("criterion") 

1596 crit_tag = f"/{crit}" if crit else "" 

1597 lines.append( 

1598 f"- [{f.get('severity')}{crit_tag}] {f.get('location')}: {f.get('what')}{reg}" 

1599 ) 

1600 lines.append("") 

1601 return "\n".join(lines) 

1602 

1603 

1604# Pre-model sandbox infrastructure-error cap. A dev sandbox that fails BEFORE 

1605# any model work (``success=False`` with zero tokens/cost and tests never run) 

1606# is shared-infra breakage — a transient ``.venv`` relink from a concurrent 

1607# ``uv run``/``uv sync`` re-materialising site-packages mid-render 

1608# (``TemplateNotFound``), an SDK import failure, or a sandbox boot crash. This 

1609# is NOT a dev-code or test failure, so it must NOT consume the dev retry 

1610# budget; the story is bounced straight back to dev (most transients clear by 

1611# the next tick). Counted from *consecutive trailing* ``dev_sandbox_infra_error`` 

1612# events so a recovered story is never punished for an earlier blip; at the cap 

1613# a persistent infra fault escalates loudly via ``factory_needs_redesign`` 

1614# instead of looping forever. Capped at 3 per the "nothing loops >3" rule. 

1615_MAX_DEV_SANDBOX_INFRA_RETRIES = 3 

1616 

1617# Dev retry budget. A red dev run (tests not green) consumes one retry; at the 

1618# cap the story blocks with an explicit ``factory_needs_redesign`` event so the 

1619# operator sees the signal. 

1620# 

1621# 3 (operator decision 2026-08-01), lowered from 6. The 6 was itself 

1622# operator-approved on 2026-05-29 on the theory that informed extra attempts 

1623# (dev receives prior-attempt history + reviewer findings) improve convergence 

1624# on harder stories, but it contradicted the standing "nothing loops more than 

1625# ~3 times" guardrail in CLAUDE.md, and only ``_MAX_CI_FIX_CYCLES`` honoured 

1626# that. Four stories in the 14 days to 2026-08-01 reached 6 retries; those are 

1627# now cut off at 3 and block for a human instead of burning three more 

1628# attempts. Whether attempts 4-6 were producing PASSING work is unmeasured — 

1629# PLAN.md Phase 1.3's gate-precision number is what would settle it. 

1630# 

1631# It is now partly settled, and not in favour of more retries: the 2026-08-04 

1632# hidden-oracle grading put the chain's own green verdict at 40% precision, and 

1633# ImpossibleBench (arXiv 2510.20270) measured cheating rising 33% -> 38% when an 

1634# agent gets multiple submissions with feedback. Under Loop-4 the dev owns its 

1635# own tests, so an extra attempt is also an extra chance to make the check 

1636# agree with the code. Do not raise this cap as an "improvement" — see the 

1637# ``_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES`` note below for the same argument in full. 

1638# 

1639# RAISED TO 4 AND MADE CONFIGURABLE, 2026-08-09, by operator decision. Two 

1640# things changed since the argument above was written (2026-08-01): 

1641# 

1642# 1. THE ARGUMENT'S PREMISE WEAKENED. "An extra attempt is an extra chance to 

1643# make the check agree with the code" was true when the dev's own tests were 

1644# the only check. The acceptance oracle went live 2026-08-08: it is authored 

1645# from the spec before the dev starts, frozen, stored outside the dev 

1646# worktree, and run out of process. The dev cannot see or edit it. So an 

1647# extra dev attempt is no longer an extra chance to game the grader — the 

1648# grader is now independent of the dev. ImpossibleBench's own finding points 

1649# the same way: its most effective mitigation was denying the DEV access to 

1650# the tests, which is exactly what the oracle now does. 

1651# 2. THE COST OF THE CAP BECAME VISIBLE. Measured 2026-08-09 over 196 dev runs: 

1652# dev is 658 s average and 97% of all genuine work time in the factory. The 

1653# cap does not make anything faster — it converts a story that needed a 

1654# fourth attempt into a BLOCKED story that needs an operator, which measured 

1655# as hours of stall (story 172: 92.6% dead time). 

1656# 

1657# The "nothing loops more than 3" guardrail in CLAUDE.md still binds every OTHER 

1658# loop. This one is now an operator-tunable threshold with a hard invariant 

1659# enforced below, because the evidence that set it at 3 was specifically about 

1660# a grader the dev could reach, and that is no longer the arrangement. 

1661_DEFAULT_MAX_DEV_RETRIES = 4 

1662 

1663 

1664def _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root: Path | None = None) -> int: 

1665 """The dev-retry cap, from ``direction_defaults.max_dev_retries``. 

1666 

1667 Until 2026-08-09 this key existed in ``factory_settings.yaml`` and in 

1668 ``DirectionDefaults`` and **nothing read it** — the authoritative value was a 

1669 hardcoded constant here. An operator could set it to 6, restart, and observe 

1670 no change. That is the same defect class as the acceptance harness hint: a 

1671 configuration fact whose consumer cannot verify it, so it drifts silently. 

1672 

1673 INVARIANT (the CLAUDE.md guardrail this cap must not break): the 

1674 early-escalation guard ``_MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE`` must stay STRICTLY BELOW 

1675 the hard cap, or it becomes unreachable and two deliberately layered guards 

1676 silently collapse into one. A configured value at or below it is refused and 

1677 the floor is used instead — fail SAFE toward keeping both guards live. 

1678 """ 

1679 try: 

1680 from factory.settings.loader import load_settings 

1681 

1682 root = software_factory_root or Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent 

1683 configured = int( 

1684 getattr(load_settings(root).direction_defaults, "max_dev_retries", 0) or 0 

1685 ) 

1686 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - an unreadable settings file must not unbound the cap 

1687 return _DEFAULT_MAX_DEV_RETRIES 

1688 if configured <= _MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE: 

1689 # Would make the early-escalation guard unreachable. Refuse it. 

1690 return _MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE + 1 

1691 return configured 

1692 

1693 

1694# Module-level FALLBACK only — deliberately NOT the authoritative value. 

1695# ``orchestrator._prune_stale_in_progress`` imports this name; it now calls 

1696# ``_max_dev_retries()`` instead, so the value the orchestrator compares against 

1697# and the value the handler enforces come from one place and cannot disagree. 

1698# Resolving it at import time was rejected: it would do settings I/O during 

1699# module import and risk an import cycle. 

1700_MAX_DEV_RETRIES = _DEFAULT_MAX_DEV_RETRIES 

1701 

1702# Same-failure-signature fast-escalation cap. When consecutive dev runs fail 

1703# with the IDENTICAL normalized failure signature (the same assertions/errors, 

1704# volatile bits stripped) the model is stuck on something more attempts won't 

1705# fix — every retry re-discovers the same dead end while burning spend. Rather 

1706# than march to ``_MAX_DEV_RETRIES`` (+ the aggregate budget breaker) on no new 

1707# signal, block after this many identical failures. 3 per the "nothing loops 

1708# unproductively >3" operator rule. A CHANGING signature means the model IS 

1709# making progress and keeps its full retry budget. 

1710# 2, lowered from 3 when _MAX_DEV_RETRIES dropped 6 -> 3 (2026-08-01). This 

1711# guard exists to escalate EARLY — before the full retry budget is spent — so 

1712# it must stay strictly below _MAX_DEV_RETRIES. At 3 == 3 it would have had no 

1713# headroom left and the early-escalation layer would have become unreachable, 

1714# silently collapsing two deliberately layered guards into one. 

1715_MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE = 2 

1716 

1717# ImpossibleBench escape hatch (arXiv 2510.20270, ICLR 2026). The marker the 

1718# dev persona emits to declare a story unsatisfiable AS WRITTEN instead of 

1719# guessing or making its own tests agree with whatever it built. Measured 

1720# effect of offering the option at all: test-exploitation 54% -> 9% (GPT-5), 

1721# 49% -> 12% (o3). 

1722# 

1723# Line-anchored and upper-case so a discussion OF the mechanism ("I considered 

1724# declaring it underspecified but...") cannot trip it — the same 

1725# contract-literal collision that produced a structural non-convergence on 

1726# story 14 (see the persona_prompt_contract_collision memory). The persona 

1727# prompt must therefore never illustrate the marker at the start of a line. 

1728_UNDERSPECIFIED_MARKER = "UNDERSPECIFIED:" 

1729_UNDERSPECIFIED_REASON_CAP = 600 

1730 

1731 

1732def parse_underspecified_declaration(text: str) -> str | None: 

1733 """Return the dev's declared reason, or ``None`` if it did not declare. 

1734 

1735 Accepts the marker only at the START of a line (leading whitespace is 

1736 tolerated for indented final messages) and requires a non-empty reason: a 

1737 bare ``UNDERSPECIFIED:`` with nothing after it is not a declaration, it is 

1738 an unfinished sentence, and a blocked story with no reason is exactly the 

1739 useless escalation this repo has been burned by before. 

1740 """ 

1741 if not text: 

1742 return None 

1743 for raw in text.splitlines(): 

1744 line = raw.strip() 

1745 if not line.startswith(_UNDERSPECIFIED_MARKER): 

1746 continue 

1747 reason = line[len(_UNDERSPECIFIED_MARKER) :].strip() 

1748 if reason: 

1749 return reason[:_UNDERSPECIFIED_REASON_CAP] 

1750 return None 

1751 

1752 

1753def declared_underspecified(run_res: Any) -> str | None: 

1754 """The declared reason from a dev sandbox result, or ``None``. 

1755 

1756 Reads only the two places the DEV'S OWN WORDS land: its parsed 

1757 ``SELF_SUMMARY:`` block and its final assistant message. 

1758 ``_extract_self_summary`` already prefers the ``finish`` tool's message over 

1759 a plain trailing message, so a dev that declares via ``finish`` is covered. 

1760 

1761 ``run_res.summary`` is deliberately NOT read: it is the pytest output tail 

1762 (``factory/runner.py`` sets it from ``test_out``), which contains captured 

1763 stdout of arbitrary application code. That is a machine-generated, untrusted 

1764 channel, and this transition is terminal and not auto-recoverable — no such 

1765 channel gets to fire it. 

1766 """ 

1767 for field_name in ("self_summary", "last_assistant_message"): 

1768 reason = parse_underspecified_declaration(str(getattr(run_res, field_name, "") or "")) 

1769 if reason is not None: 

1770 return reason 

1771 return None 

1772 

1773 

1774def _block_underspecified( 

1775 story: StoryRecord, 

1776 reason: str, 

1777 *, 

1778 db: Path, 

1779 software_factory_root: Path, 

1780 tests_green: bool, 

1781 files_changed: list[str], 

1782) -> HandlerResult: 

1783 """Park ``story`` in the terminal BLOCKED_UNDERSPECIFIED sink. 

1784 

1785 ``story.dev_retries`` is deliberately NOT incremented: a declaration is not 

1786 a failed attempt, and charging a retry for it would price honesty the same 

1787 as failure — the opposite of what ImpossibleBench measured. 

1788 

1789 The declaration wins even when the run ended GREEN. A green run on a story 

1790 the dev itself calls unsatisfiable is the exact shape of the false-green 

1791 this closes (under Loop-4 the dev owns the tests that went green), so it 

1792 goes to a human rather than to the reviewer. ``tests_green`` is recorded so 

1793 the operator can see which case they are looking at. 

1794 """ 

1795 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_UNDERSPECIFIED).value 

1796 story.error = f"dev declared the story underspecified: {reason}" 

1797 persist_story(story, db) 

1798 log_story_event( 

1799 story.id, 

1800 "dev_declared_underspecified", 

1801 { 

1802 "reason": reason, 

1803 "tests_green_at_declaration": tests_green, 

1804 "files_changed": files_changed[:20], 

1805 # Proof the escape hatch is free: the operator can check that this 

1806 # is the same count the story carried before the declaration. 

1807 "dev_retries": story.dev_retries, 

1808 }, 

1809 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

1810 slug_hint=story.slug, 

1811 ) 

1812 return HandlerResult( 

1813 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

1814 payload={ 

1815 "test_run_passed": tests_green, 

1816 "underspecified": reason, 

1817 "files_changed": files_changed, 

1818 "summary": ( 

1819 "Dev declared the story underspecified rather than guessing: " 

1820 f"{reason}. Terminal, awaiting a human; no dev retry consumed." 

1821 ), 

1822 }, 

1823 error=story.error, 

1824 ) 

1825 

1826 

1827def _consecutive_same_dev_signature(prior_attempts: list[Any], current_sig: str) -> int: 

1828 """Count trailing dev attempts sharing ``current_sig`` (newest-first). 

1829 

1830 Walks ``prior_attempts`` (the ``dev_attempts_json`` list) from the end and 

1831 counts the unbroken run of red attempts whose ``failure_signature`` equals 

1832 ``current_sig``. A green attempt (``test_run_passed is True``) or a 

1833 different/absent signature breaks the run — a green in between or a changed 

1834 failure both mean genuine progress, so the stall counter resets. Returns 0 

1835 for an empty signature (no comparable evidence yet). 

1836 """ 

1837 if not current_sig: 

1838 return 0 

1839 count = 0 

1840 for a in reversed(prior_attempts): 

1841 if not isinstance(a, dict): 

1842 break 

1843 if a.get("test_run_passed") is True: 

1844 break 

1845 if a.get("failure_signature") == current_sig: 

1846 count += 1 

1847 else: 

1848 break 

1849 return count 

1850 

1851 

1852# Review convergence guard. Judged by finding STABILITY, not raw cycle count: a 

1853# cycle that surfaces DIFFERENT findings is making progress. We block only when 

1854# the reviewer returns the SAME findings _MAX_REVIEW_STUCK times in a row 

1855# (genuine churn — "nothing loops unproductively >3"), with a hard absolute 

1856# backstop (_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES) so a slowly-mutating loop can't run forever. 

1857# 

1858# Both lowered 2026-08-01 (operator decision) to honour the CLAUDE.md "nothing 

1859# loops more than ~3 times" guardrail, which previously only 

1860# ``_MAX_CI_FIX_CYCLES`` respected. The RATIO is preserved deliberately: 

1861# _MAX_REVIEW_STUCK must stay strictly below _MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES or the 

1862# stability guard becomes unreachable and "findings that CHANGE are progress" 

1863# — the whole reason this is judged by stability rather than raw count — 

1864# silently stops being true. 3/3 would have blocked a story making genuine 

1865# progress at the same point as one in pure churn. 

1866# 

1867# Review convergence is healthy at this cap: in the 14 days to 2026-08-01, 

1868# 101 of 122 stories used zero cycles, 18 used one, and the maximum was 5. 

1869# 

1870# DO NOT RAISE THESE AS AN "IMPROVEMENT". They are a stronger safety property 

1871# than "stop burning budget"; the external literature says more feedback rounds 

1872# buy gaming, not assurance: 

1873# * ImpossibleBench (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.20270) measured cheating rising 

1874# 33% -> 38% when agents get MULTIPLE submissions with feedback. More 

1875# cycles is the condition that produced more cheating. 

1876# * Self-refine/self-repair at MATCHED budget (arXiv 2306.09896) buys only 

1877# 3-10% — i.e. the same tokens spent on more independent attempts do about 

1878# as well, so extra cycles are not where the win is. 

1879# Under Loop-4 the dev owns the tests the reviewer's approve rule reads, so each 

1880# extra cycle is another chance to make the check agree with the code rather 

1881# than the code agree with the story. The 2026-08-04 hidden-oracle grading 

1882# measured the result: the chain's own green verdict was 40% precise. 

1883# 

1884# Lowering them, or replacing a cycle with an independent check that the dev 

1885# cannot author (a hidden oracle, a mutation score, execution output fed to the 

1886# reviewer), are the changes with evidence behind them. Raising them is not. 

1887_MAX_REVIEW_STUCK = 2 

1888_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES = 3 

1889 

1890 

1891def _is_premodel_infra_failure(run_res: Any) -> bool: 

1892 """True when a sandbox run failed before any model work began. 

1893
