1894 A genuine "dev ran but tests are still red" outcome has 

1895 ``test_run_passed is False`` and (almost always) non-zero token/cost 

1896 usage. A pre-model infrastructure failure — the OpenHands SDK import 

1897 blowing up, the agent prompt template failing to render, or the sandbox 

1898 boot crashing — returns ``success=False`` with ``test_run_passed`` never 

1899 set and zero tokens/cost. Distinguishing the two is what keeps an 

1900 environment blip from masquerading as a code failure and burning the dev 

1901 retry budget. 

1902 

1903 The runner now sets an EXPLICIT ``premodel_infra`` flag (True only for 

1904 genuine pre-model breakage; False when the model spent tokens and then 

1905 raised). Prefer it when present: the old zero-cost/None heuristic 

1906 misclassified a run that DID real model work but crashed afterwards (e.g. 

1907 during metrics extraction) as "infra", so the dev handler bounced it back 

1908 for free and NEVER incremented ``dev_retries`` — the story-88 loop where a 

1909 story was re-dispatched 12 times with ``dev_retries`` stuck at 1. A run 

1910 that actually evaluated tests (``test_run_passed is not None``) is a real 

1911 dev attempt and is NEVER infra, regardless of the flag. 

1912 """ 

1913 if run_res.test_run_passed is not None: 

1914 # The post-model gate ran (tests passed OR failed, including collection 

1915 # errors that exit pytest non-zero) — this is a genuine dev attempt, 

1916 # never infra. Also covers the runner's "model did real work then 

1917 # raised" path, which now reports test_run_passed=False. 

1918 return False 

1919 if getattr(run_res, "premodel_infra", False): 

1920 # Runner explicitly flagged genuine pre-model breakage. 

1921 return True 

1922 # Backward-compat heuristic for RunResults built without the explicit flag 

1923 # (e.g. legacy fixtures): no success, tests never ran, zero cost/tokens. 

1924 return bool( 

1925 not run_res.success 

1926 and run_res.test_run_passed is None 

1927 and (run_res.cost_usd or 0.0) == 0.0 

1928 and (run_res.tokens_out or 0) == 0 

1929 ) 

1930 

1931 

1932def _consecutive_trailing_infra_errors(story: StoryRecord, software_factory_root: Path) -> int: 

1933 """Count ``dev_sandbox_infra_error`` events with no real dev progress after. 

1934 

1935 Walks the per-story event log newest-first and counts the unbroken run of 

1936 trailing infra-error events. Any genuine dev event (retry, exhaustion, 

1937 green, clarification, or a fresh dev_started) resets the count — so a 

1938 story that hit one transient blip, recovered, and only much later hits 

1939 more is never blocked on a stale cumulative tally. 

1940 """ 

1941 from factory.chain.event_log import read_story_events 

1942 

1943 count = 0 

1944 for e in reversed( 

1945 read_story_events( 

1946 story.id, software_factory_root=software_factory_root, slug_hint=story.slug 

1947 ) 

1948 ): 

1949 ev = e.get("event") 

1950 if ev == "dev_sandbox_infra_error": 

1951 count += 1 

1952 elif ev in { 

1953 "dev_retry", 

1954 "dev_exhausted", 

1955 "dev_tests_green", 

1956 "tests_need_clarification", 

1957 }: 

1958 break 

1959 return count 

1960 

1961 

1962def _dry_run_dev(story: StoryRecord) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, Any]]: 

1963 """Deterministic dev result for dry-run mode. 

1964 

1965 Returns (tests_green, payload). Default happy path: tests green after 

1966 the first dev run. 

1967 """ 

1968 return True, { 

1969 "files_changed": [f"src/{story.slug.replace('-', '_')}.py"], 

1970 "test_run_passed": True, 

1971 "summary": "Dry-run dev pass: tests green on first attempt.", 

1972 } 

1973 

1974 

1975def _commit_green_dev_work( 

1976 story: StoryRecord, app_config: AppConfig, software_factory_root: Path 

1977) -> None: 

1978 """Deterministically ``git add -A && commit`` the dev's uncommitted worktree 

1979 changes on a GREEN outcome, so the reviewer's ``origin/base...HEAD`` diff is 

1980 never empty. The dev persona is only *asked* to self-commit; when it forgets 

1981 (story 106, 2026-07-21) the branch has no committed diff and dev<->review 

1982 churns on already-correct code. Idempotent (a clean tree — the agent already 

1983 committed — is a no-op) and best-effort (a git hiccup must never fail the 

1984 green advance; the work still lives in the reused worktree and PR-open 

1985 re-commits). Mirrors the dev-exhausted path's WIP-preservation commit. 

1986 """ 

1987 try: 

1988 from factory.chain.branch import _run_git as _git 

1989 

1990 repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

1991 _git(repo, "add", "-A") 

1992 if _git(repo, "status", "--porcelain").stdout.strip(): 

1993 _git(repo, "commit", "-m", f"dev: implement story {story.id} ({story.slug})") 

1994 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - commit is best-effort; never fail the green advance 

1995 pass 

1996 

1997 

1998def _try_resume_dev_from_checkpoint( 

1999 story: StoryRecord, 

2000 software_factory_root: Path, 

2001 *, 

2002 app_config: AppConfig, 

2003 db_path: Path | None = None, 

2004) -> HandlerResult | None: 

2005 """WS4.2 resume-from-checkpoint: skip re-running the dev LLM when a prior 

2006 sandbox already completed GREEN but the tick died before the DB advanced 

2007 out of ``dev_in_progress``. 

2008 

2009 Returns a ``HandlerResult`` (advanced to ``tests_green``) when a valid 

2010 green checkpoint is present, otherwise ``None`` (the caller proceeds with a 

2011 normal dev run). Correctness rests on two facts: (1) the dev sandbox writes 

2012 its changes into the per-story worktree, which is REUSED across ticks — so 

2013 the green code survives the interruption and re-running the LLM would only 

2014 reproduce it; (2) the checkpoint is written green then cleared within a 

2015 single ``handle_dev`` call, so a lingering one is unambiguous evidence of an 

2016 interruption (never the review-feedback re-entry path, which reaches dev 

2017 only after the checkpoint was already cleared). Idempotent: a second call 

2018 finds no checkpoint and returns ``None``. 

2019 """ 

2020 cp_raw = story.dev_step_checkpoint 

2021 if not cp_raw: 

2022 return None 

2023 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

2024 try: 

2025 cp = json.loads(cp_raw) 

2026 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2027 cp = None 

2028 if not isinstance(cp, dict) or cp.get("outcome") != "green": 

2029 # Malformed / non-green marker — clear it and fall through to a normal 

2030 # dev run. Never skip the LLM on an ambiguous checkpoint. 

2031 story.dev_step_checkpoint = None 

2032 persist_story(story, db) 

2033 return None 

2034 

2035 from_state = story.state 

2036 # Drive the pure state machine exactly as a real green run would: 

2037 # dispatch-state -> DEV_IN_PROGRESS -> TESTS_GREEN. ``advance`` is pure and 

2038 # validates the transition, so an unexpected dispatch state raises loudly 

2039 # rather than silently skipping into an illegal state. 

2040 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_STARTED).value 

2041 # Same deterministic commit as the live green path: a crash could have 

2042 # interrupted the original run BEFORE it committed, leaving the resumed 

2043 # green work uncommitted → empty-diff churn. Idempotent + best-effort. 

2044 _commit_green_dev_work(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

2045 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_TESTS_GREEN).value 

2046 story.dev_step_checkpoint = None 

2047 persist_story(story, db) 

2048 log_story_event( 

2049 story.id, 

2050 "dev_resume_from_checkpoint", 

2051 { 

2052 "from_state": from_state, 

2053 "to_state": story.state, 

2054 "checkpoint_attempt": cp.get("attempt"), 

2055 "checkpoint_ts": cp.get("ts"), 

2056 }, 

2057 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2058 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2059 ) 

2060 return HandlerResult( 

2061 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

2062 payload={"resumed_from_checkpoint": True, "test_run_passed": True}, 

2063 ) 

2064 

2065 

2066def handle_dev( 

2067 story: StoryRecord, 

2068 app_config: AppConfig, 

2069 software_factory_root: Path, 

2070 *, 

2071 dry_run: bool = False, 

2072 db_path: Path | None = None, 

2073 force_red: bool = False, 

2074) -> HandlerResult: 

2075 """Run the Dev persona; check tests; retry/escalate on failure. 

2076 

2077 With ``dev_convergence.enabled`` (factory_settings.yaml), a red run 

2078 retries IMMEDIATELY in this same invocation — fresh sandbox, prior- 

2079 attempts memory carried forward by ``_handle_dev_once``'s normal red 

2080 bookkeeping — instead of waiting for the next tick. The loop grants no 

2081 extra attempts (``_MAX_DEV_RETRIES`` stays authoritative); it only 

2082 removes the tick-cadence dead time between the same retries. Guards: 

2083 inner-attempt cap, one retry of headroom under the chain cap, per-story 

2084 wall-clock + budget, and a live re-check of the global hourly/daily 

2085 spend caps. Infra failures and content-filter escalations always exit 

2086 the loop into their existing across-ticks paths. 

2087 

2088 ``force_red`` is for testing the retry path: when True, the dry-run 

2089 branch returns tests_green=False so the handler exercises the retry + 

2090 escalation logic. 

2091 """ 

2092 import time as _time 

2093 

2094 from factory.settings.loader import load_settings 

2095 

2096 _settings = load_settings(software_factory_root) 

2097 

2098 # WS4.2 resume-from-checkpoint. Before spending anything, check whether a 

2099 # prior dev sandbox already completed GREEN and only the state advance was 

2100 # lost to an interruption. If so, resume from the persisted result WITHOUT 

2101 # re-running the expensive dev LLM (the green code already lives in the 

2102 # reused per-story worktree). Real-run only and gated by a default-on flag. 

2103 if not dry_run and getattr(_settings.dev_convergence, "resume_from_checkpoint", True): 

2104 _resumed = _try_resume_dev_from_checkpoint( 

2105 story, software_factory_root, app_config=app_config, db_path=db_path 

2106 ) 

2107 if _resumed is not None: 

2108 return _resumed 

2109 

2110 result = _handle_dev_once( 

2111 story, 

2112 app_config, 

2113 software_factory_root, 

2114 dry_run=dry_run, 

2115 db_path=db_path, 

2116 force_red=force_red, 

2117 ) 

2118 conv = _settings.dev_convergence 

2119 if dry_run or not conv.enabled: 

2120 return result 

2121 

2122 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

2123 loop_started_mono = _time.monotonic() 

2124 loop_started_ts = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() 

2125 inner_attempts = 1 

2126 

2127 while True: 

2128 stop_reason = _dev_inner_loop_stop_reason( 

2129 story=story, 

2130 result=result, 

2131 conv=conv, 

2132 inner_attempts=inner_attempts, 

2133 elapsed_s=_time.monotonic() - loop_started_mono, 

2134 since_ts=loop_started_ts, 

2135 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2136 db_path=db, 

2137 ) 

2138 if stop_reason == "continue": 

2139 inner_attempts += 1 

2140 log_story_event( 

2141 story.id, 

2142 "dev_inner_attempt", 

2143 {"inner_attempt": inner_attempts, "dev_retries": story.dev_retries}, 

2144 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2145 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2146 ) 

2147 result = _handle_dev_once( 

2148 story, 

2149 app_config, 

2150 software_factory_root, 

2151 dry_run=dry_run, 

2152 db_path=db_path, 

2153 force_red=force_red, 

2154 ) 

2155 continue 

2156 if stop_reason != "terminal": 

2157 # Stopped while the story is still retryable — record why so the 

2158 # FMS can distinguish "loop budget ran out" from "story done". 

2159 log_story_event( 

2160 story.id, 

2161 "dev_inner_loop_stopped", 

2162 { 

2163 "reason": stop_reason, 

2164 "inner_attempts": inner_attempts, 

2165 "dev_retries": story.dev_retries, 

2166 }, 

2167 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2168 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2169 ) 

2170 return result 

2171 

2172 

2173def _dev_inner_loop_stop_reason( 

2174 *, 

2175 story: StoryRecord, 

2176 result: HandlerResult, 

2177 conv: Any, 

2178 inner_attempts: int, 

2179 elapsed_s: float, 

2180 since_ts: str, 

2181 software_factory_root: Path, 

2182 db_path: Path, 

2183) -> str: 

2184 """Decide whether the dev convergence loop re-attempts now. 

2185 

2186 Returns ``"continue"`` to re-dispatch immediately, ``"terminal"`` when 

2187 the story left the retryable state (green, exhausted, blocked), or a 

2188 stop-reason label when the story IS retryable but a loop guard says to 

2189 fall back to the normal across-ticks path. 

2190 """ 

2191 if StoryState(story.state) is not StoryState.DEV_RETRY: 

2192 return "terminal" 

2193 payload = result.payload or {} 

2194 if payload.get("sandbox_infra_error"): 

2195 return "infra_failure" 

2196 if payload.get("content_filter_tier_escalation"): 

2197 return "content_filter" 

2198 if inner_attempts >= conv.max_inner_attempts: 

2199 return "attempts_cap" 

2200 # Leave the LAST chain retry to the normal tick path so exhaustion 

2201 # bookkeeping (WIP commit/push, factory_needs_redesign) never runs 

2202 # inside a tight loop iteration. 

2203 if story.dev_retries + 1 >= _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root): 

2204 return "retry_headroom" 

2205 if elapsed_s >= conv.per_story_wall_clock_s: 

2206 return "wall_clock" 

2207 story_cost = _story_spend_since(db_path, story.id, since_ts) 

2208 if story_cost >= conv.per_story_budget_usd: 

2209 return "budget" 

2210 # Live re-check of the global caps: the settings enforcer only gates 

2211 # dispatch, so a tight loop must re-verify mid-flight. 

2212 from factory.settings.loader import load_settings 

2213 from factory.settings.spend import hour_spend_usd, today_spend_usd 

2214 

2215 caps = load_settings(software_factory_root).caps 

2216 if hour_spend_usd(software_factory_root, db_path=db_path) >= caps.hourly_spend_usd: 

2217 return "hourly_cap" 

2218 if today_spend_usd(software_factory_root, db_path=db_path) >= caps.daily_spend_usd: 

2219 return "daily_cap" 

2220 return "continue" 

2221 

2222 

2223def _story_spend_since(db_path: Path, story_id: int | None, since_ts: str) -> float: 

2224 """Sum ``runs.cost_usd`` for ``story_id`` with ``ts >= since_ts`` (best-effort).""" 

2225 if story_id is None: 

2226 return 0.0 

2227 try: 

2228 from factory.runner import Run, _engine 

2229 

2230 total = 0.0 

2231 with Session(_engine(db_path)) as session: 

2232 rows = session.exec(select(Run).where(Run.story_id == story_id)).all() 

2233 for r in rows: 

2234 if (r.ts or "") >= since_ts: 

2235 total += float(r.cost_usd or 0.0) 

2236 return total 

2237 except Exception: 

2238 # A broken ledger must not stop the loop-guard decision; treat as 

2239 # budget-exhausted so the loop stops rather than spending blind. 

2240 return float("inf") 

2241 

2242 

2243def _handle_dev_once( 

2244 story: StoryRecord, 

2245 app_config: AppConfig, 

2246 software_factory_root: Path, 

2247 *, 

2248 dry_run: bool = False, 

2249 db_path: Path | None = None, 

2250 force_red: bool = False, 

2251) -> HandlerResult: 

2252 """Single dev attempt: dispatch sandbox, check tests, do retry/escalation 

2253 bookkeeping. See ``handle_dev`` for the convergence-loop wrapper. 

2254 """ 

2255 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

2256 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_STARTED).value 

2257 persist_story(story, db) 

2258 

2259 if dry_run: 

2260 tests_green = not force_red 

2261 _, payload = _dry_run_dev(story) 

2262 if force_red: 

2263 payload["test_run_passed"] = False 

2264 payload["summary"] = "Dry-run dev failure: tests still red." 

2265 else: 

2266 from factory.chain.branch import feature_branch_name 

2267 from factory.runner import LLMConfig, sandbox_run 

2268 

2269 # Dev runs in the same per-story worktree test_impl already created. 

2270 # If test_impl wasn't run yet (e.g. retry path entered directly), 

2271 # ``_writing_worktree`` will create it on demand. 

2272 target_repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

2273 repo_path = target_repo 

2274 story_file_path_obj = software_factory_root / "apps" / story.app / story.story_file_path 

2275 difficulty = story.current_model_tier 

2276 

2277 branch = feature_branch_name(story.github_issue_number, story.slug) 

2278 story.github_branch = branch 

2279 persist_story(story, db) 

2280 

2281 dev_direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

2282 from factory.directions.parser import get_direction_chain 

2283 

2284 dev_chain = ( 

2285 get_direction_chain(dev_direction, software_factory_root) 

2286 if dev_direction is not None 

2287 else None 

2288 ) 

2289 

2290 llm = LLMConfig(model=route("dev", difficulty=difficulty)) 

2291 import asyncio 

2292 

2293 # Carry prior attempts forward — the LLM gets to see what was tried 

2294 # and which assertions are still red, so retry N doesn't re-discover 

2295 # the same dead ends retries 1..N-1 already hit. 

2296 prior_attempts: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] 

2297 if story.dev_attempts_json: 

2298 try: 

2299 prior_attempts = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json) or [] 

2300 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2301 prior_attempts = [] 

2302 

2303 # When dev is re-dispatched after the reviewer requested changes, hand 

2304 # it the reviewer's actual findings. Tests are already green on this 

2305 # path, so without the findings the dev LLM has no signal about what to 

2306 # fix and the dev<->reviewer loop cannot converge. The most recent 

2307 # verdict carries the actionable items; earlier cycles ride along as a 

2308 # ``prior_cycles`` digest so already-fixed sites don't regress. 

2309 reviewer_findings: dict[str, Any] | None = None 

2310 if story.reviewer_result_json: 

2311 try: 

2312 parsed = json.loads(story.reviewer_result_json) 

2313 if isinstance(parsed, dict) and ( 

2314 parsed.get("findings") or parsed.get("test_quality_findings") 

2315 ): 

2316 reviewer_findings = parsed 

2317 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2318 reviewer_findings = None 

2319 if reviewer_findings is not None and story.reviewer_history_json: 

2320 try: 

2321 history = json.loads(story.reviewer_history_json) 

2322 # The final history entry is the latest review — already fully 

2323 # rendered as the actionable findings; only OLDER cycles go in 

2324 # the do-not-regress digest. 

2325 if isinstance(history, list) and len(history) > 1: 

2326 reviewer_findings["prior_cycles"] = history[:-1] 

2327 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2328 pass 

2329 

2330 from factory.settings.loader import load_settings as _load_settings 

2331 

2332 _dev_timeout_s = _load_settings(software_factory_root).dev_convergence.dev_sandbox_timeout_s 

2333 

2334 run_res = asyncio.run( 

2335 sandbox_run( 

2336 persona="dev", 

2337 story_path=story_file_path_obj, 

2338 repo_path=repo_path, 

2339 llm_config=llm, 

2340 difficulty=difficulty, 

2341 dry_run=False, 

2342 direction_chain=dev_chain, 

2343 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2344 test_command=app_config.gates.test_command, 

2345 prior_attempts=prior_attempts, 

2346 reviewer_findings=reviewer_findings, 

2347 story_id=story.id, 

2348 app=story.app, 

2349 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

2350 wall_clock_timeout_s=_dev_timeout_s, 

2351 db_path=db, 

2352 ) 

2353 ) 

2354 

2355 # Pre-model sandbox infrastructure guard. If the sandbox died before 

2356 # any model work (transient .venv relink → TemplateNotFound, SDK 

2357 # import failure, boot crash), this is shared-infra breakage, NOT a 

2358 # dev-code failure. Treating it as "tests red" below would burn a dev 

2359 # retry on a problem dev cannot fix and produce a $0/0.2s retry storm. 

2360 # Instead: do NOT count it as a dev retry, do NOT escalate the model 

2361 # tier; bounce straight back to dev (the transient usually clears by 

2362 # the next tick), bounded by a consecutive-error cap so a persistent 

2363 # fault escalates loudly rather than looping. 

2364 if not dry_run and _is_premodel_infra_failure(run_res): 

2365 # Provider content-filter blocks are NOT infrastructure: the same 

2366 # conversation deterministically re-trips the filter (observed 

2367 # 2026-06-11, Azure "ResponsibleAI" blocking deepseek's own 

2368 # completion 3/3 on story 32), so retrying the same model just 

2369 # marches to the breaker cap and terminally blocks the story. 

2370 # Escalate to the hard-tier model instead — a different model has 

2371 # a different filter profile. One-shot: if the hard tier also 

2372 # filters, fall through to the bounded infra path below. 

2373 if "content_filter" in (run_res.error or "") and story.current_model_tier != "hard": 

2374 story.current_model_tier = "hard" 

2375 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_TESTS_RED).value 

2376 story.error = None 

2377 persist_story(story, db) 

2378 log_story_event( 

2379 story.id, 

2380 "dev_content_filter_tier_escalation", 

2381 { 

2382 "to_tier": "hard", 

2383 "error": (run_res.error or "")[:300], 

2384 }, 

2385 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2386 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2387 ) 

2388 return HandlerResult( 

2389 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

2390 payload={ 

2391 "test_run_passed": False, 

2392 "content_filter_tier_escalation": True, 

2393 }, 

2394 error=None, 

2395 ) 

2396 prior_infra = _consecutive_trailing_infra_errors(story, software_factory_root) 

2397 infra_err = (run_res.error or "sandbox failed before model work")[:300] 

2398 if prior_infra < _MAX_DEV_SANDBOX_INFRA_RETRIES: 

2399 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_TESTS_RED).value 

2400 story.error = None 

2401 persist_story(story, db) 

2402 log_story_event( 

2403 story.id, 

2404 "dev_sandbox_infra_error", 

2405 { 

2406 "attempt": prior_infra + 1, 

2407 "cap": _MAX_DEV_SANDBOX_INFRA_RETRIES, 

2408 "error": infra_err, 

2409 "dev_retries_preserved": story.dev_retries, 

2410 }, 

2411 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2412 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2413 ) 

2414 return HandlerResult( 

2415 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

2416 payload={ 

2417 "test_run_passed": False, 

2418 "sandbox_infra_error": infra_err, 

2419 "summary": ( 

2420 "Sandbox infrastructure failure before any model " 

2421 f"work: {infra_err[:200]}. Re-dispatching dev " 

2422 f"(infra retry {prior_infra + 1}/" 

2423 f"{_MAX_DEV_SANDBOX_INFRA_RETRIES}); dev retry " 

2424 "budget untouched." 

2425 ), 

2426 }, 

2427 error=None, 

2428 ) 

2429 # Cap hit — a persistent sandbox/infra fault dev cannot fix. Block 

2430 # loudly so the operator/FMS sees genuine infra breakage rather 

2431 # than a story silently consuming retries. 

2432 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_EXHAUSTED).value 

2433 story.error = ( 

2434 f"sandbox infrastructure failure persisted across " 

2435 f"{_MAX_DEV_SANDBOX_INFRA_RETRIES} consecutive retries: {infra_err[:200]}" 

2436 ) 

2437 persist_story(story, db) 

2438 log_story_event( 

2439 story.id, 

2440 "factory_needs_redesign", 

2441 { 

2442 "kind": "sandbox_infra_persistent", 

2443 "infra_retries": prior_infra, 

2444 "error": infra_err, 

2445 "suggestions": [ 

2446 "The dev sandbox failed before any model work on every " 

2447 "attempt (e.g. TemplateNotFound / SDK import / boot " 

2448 "crash). This is environment breakage, not a code or " 

2449 "test problem dev can fix. Check for a concurrent " 

2450 "`uv run`/`uv sync` relinking the shared .venv, a " 

2451 "corrupt OpenHands install, or a missing prompt template.", 

2452 ], 

2453 }, 

2454 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2455 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2456 ) 

2457 return HandlerResult( 

2458 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

2459 payload={ 

2460 "test_run_passed": False, 

2461 "sandbox_infra_error": infra_err, 

2462 }, 

2463 error=story.error, 

2464 ) 

2465 

2466 # Loop-4 (dev-owns-tests): the dev persona writes BOTH production code 

2467 # and its tests, so there is no "tests are frozen" invariant to enforce 

2468 # and no Test-Designer to route a clarification back to. A failed run is 

2469 # simply a dev retry (below). Test *quality* (no slop, meaningful 

2470 # assertions) is gated downstream by the reviewer + programmatic slop 

2471 # detector, not here. 

2472 tests_green = bool(run_res.test_run_passed) 

2473 payload = { 

2474 "files_changed": run_res.files_changed, 

2475 "test_run_passed": tests_green, 

2476 "summary": run_res.summary[-2000:], 

2477 } 

2478 

2479 # ImpossibleBench escape hatch, checked BEFORE the green/red split and 

2480 # BEFORE any retry bookkeeping. See BLOCKED_UNDERSPECIFIED in 

2481 # state_machine.py for the measurement this implements. 

2482 declared = declared_underspecified(run_res) 

2483 if declared is not None: 

2484 return _block_underspecified( 

2485 story, 

2486 declared, 

2487 db=db, 

2488 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2489 tests_green=tests_green, 

2490 files_changed=list(run_res.files_changed or []), 

2491 ) 

2492 

2493 # Loop-4: a dev run that ends red — including one that made no code 

2494 # changes — is just a failed attempt and consumes a retry below. There 

2495 # is no longer a separate test author to route a "tests are wrong" 

2496 # signal back to: the dev owns the tests and fixes them on the next 

2497 # attempt. The no-change case still exhausts the budget quickly because 

2498 # ``_MAX_DEV_RETRIES`` caps total attempts. 

2499 

2500 if tests_green: 

2501 # Record the GREEN run's test output too. The reviewer's 

2502 # ``_fetch_latest_test_output`` prefers the last dev_attempts_json 

2503 # entry; when only red attempts were recorded, a story with any red 

2504 # history showed the reviewer stale failures forever — story 32 was 

2505 # rejected on 2026-06-11 over a "still 12 failing tests" tail that 

2506 # was ten days old. 

2507 if not dry_run: 

2508 green_record = { 

2509 "attempt": story.dev_retries, 

2510 "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(), 

2511 "test_run_passed": True, 

2512 "files_touched": (run_res.files_changed or [])[:20], 

2513 "test_output_tail": (run_res.summary or "")[-1800:], 

2514 "summary": "tests green", 

2515 "self_summary": (getattr(run_res, "self_summary", "") or "")[:2000], 

2516 } 

2517 try: 

2518 prior_green = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

2519 if not isinstance(prior_green, list): 

2520 prior_green = [] 

2521 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2522 prior_green = [] 

2523 prior_green.append(green_record) 

2524 story.dev_attempts_json = json.dumps(prior_green[-5:]) 

2525 # WS4.2 resume checkpoint: persist the completed green artifact + 

2526 # marker BEFORE the state advance. If the tick dies between here and 

2527 # the advance below, the next dev dispatch reads this marker and 

2528 # resumes to TESTS_GREEN without re-running the dev LLM (the green 

2529 # code already lives in the reused worktree). The advance below 

2530 # clears it, so it survives only a genuine interruption. 

2531 story.dev_step_checkpoint = json.dumps( 

2532 { 

2533 "outcome": "green", 

2534 "attempt": story.dev_retries, 

2535 "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(), 

2536 } 

2537 ) 

2538 persist_story(story, db) 

2539 # Deterministically COMMIT the dev's green work before review so the 

2540 # reviewer's origin/base...HEAD diff is never empty (see 

2541 # ``_commit_green_dev_work``). Fixes the dev<->review empty-diff 

2542 # churn observed on story 106 (2026-07-21). 

2543 _commit_green_dev_work(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

2544 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_TESTS_GREEN).value 

2545 story.dev_step_checkpoint = None 

2546 persist_story(story, db) 

2547 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload) 

2548 

2549 # Not green — bump retries AND record this attempt's diagnostic so the 

2550 # next retry sees what was tried and what failed. Dry-run has no 

2551 # ``run_res`` (synthetic payload only); skip the feed-forward record 

2552 # so the retry test fixture isn't tangled. 

2553 story.dev_retries += 1 

2554 # Record the retry in the replayable chain_step stream. Dev retries happen 

2555 # INSIDE a single handler invocation, so the orchestrator's two emit sites 

2556 # (which fire once per dispatch) never see them: the stream held 400 

2557 # ``advanced`` + 10 ``error`` rows and zero ``retried`` rows while 41 

2558 # stories carried a non-zero ``dev_retries``. A retry is not a state 

2559 # transition, so from_state == to_state deliberately. 

2560 # 

2561 # ``retry_attempt``/``retry_cap`` are named to avoid colliding with the 

2562 # payload's own ``attempt`` field (which carries ``story.total_attempts``); 

2563 # ``extra`` is merged last and would otherwise silently redefine it. 

2564 emit_chain_step( 

2565 story, 

2566 handler="dev", 

2567 from_state=story.state, 

2568 to_state=story.state, 

2569 outcome="retried", 

2570 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2571 extra={"retry_attempt": story.dev_retries, "retry_cap": _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root)}, 

2572 ) 

2573 if not dry_run: 

2574 # Capture rich cross-retry memory: the file diff + test tail are 

2575 # the "what failed" signal; ``self_summary`` + ``last_assistant_message`` 

2576 # + ``recent_tool_calls`` are the "what dev was thinking" signal. 

2577 # The next retry's _build_initial_message renders both layers into 

2578 # the prompt so the new conversation inherits the prior session's 

2579 # context, not just its stack trace. 

2580 attempt_record = { 

2581 "attempt": story.dev_retries, 

2582 "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(), 

2583 "test_run_passed": False, 

2584 "files_touched": (run_res.files_changed or [])[:20], 

2585 "test_output_tail": (run_res.summary or "")[-1800:], 

2586 "summary": (run_res.error or "tests not green after run")[:300], 

2587 "self_summary": (getattr(run_res, "self_summary", "") or "")[:2000], 

2588 "last_assistant_message": (getattr(run_res, "last_assistant_message", "") or "")[:2000], 

2589 "recent_tool_calls": list(getattr(run_res, "recent_tool_calls", []) or [])[-8:], 

2590 } 

2591 try: 

2592 prior = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

2593 if not isinstance(prior, list): 

2594 prior = [] 

2595 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2596 prior = [] 

2597 prior.append(attempt_record) 

2598 # R2: stamp this attempt with its normalized failure signature, reusing 

2599 # the SAME normalize+hash core the recovery / CI-fix loops use (via 

2600 # ``_story_failure_signature``) so "is this the same failure" means the 

2601 # same thing everywhere. Signed from the attempt's own ``test_output_tail`` 

2602 # (already in-memory) so we serialize dev_attempts_json exactly ONCE. 

2603 # Cap history to last 5 entries — beyond that the prompt bloat outweighs 

2604 # the signal, and we have the full chain in the per-story event log. 

2605 # Detection survives across ticks via the persisted field. 

2606 from factory.chain.orchestrator import _failure_signature_from_tail 

2607 

2608 attempt_record["failure_signature"] = _failure_signature_from_tail( 

2609 str(attempt_record["test_output_tail"]) 

2610 ) 

2611 story.dev_attempts_json = json.dumps(prior[-5:]) 

2612 

2613 # R2: if the last _MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE red runs all failed with the 

2614 # identical signature, the loop is unproductive — escalate now instead of 

2615 # burning the rest of the retry + per-story budget re-discovering the same 

2616 # dead end. Dry-run records no attempts, so this never fires there. 

2617 same_sig_count = 0 

2618 if not dry_run: 

2619 try: 

2620 _attempts_now = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

2621 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2622 _attempts_now = [] 

2623 _cur_sig = str(attempt_record.get("failure_signature", "") or "") 

2624 same_sig_count = _consecutive_same_dev_signature(_attempts_now, _cur_sig) 

2625 same_sig_stall = same_sig_count >= _MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE 

2626 

2627 if story.dev_retries >= _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root) or same_sig_stall: 

2628 # Preserve whatever dev produced so the work doesn't evaporate 

2629 # into a stash when the next story takes the working tree. Commit 

2630 # any uncommitted changes, push the branch to origin, and surface 

2631 # the failure with enough detail for a human (or follow-up persona 

2632 # run) to pick it up without forensic stash-archaeology. The 

2633 # story still terminates in BLOCKED_TESTS_NEED_CLARIFICATION but 

2634 # the branch exists at origin and any partial code is committed. 

2635 # 

2636 # Dry-run skips the commit/push entirely — there's no real work 

2637 # to preserve and ``_writing_worktree`` would try to ``git 

2638 # worktree add`` against a fixture repo that doesn't exist. 

2639 commit_pushed = False 

2640 commit_sha: str | None = None 

2641 if not dry_run: 

2642 from factory.chain.branch import _run_git as _git 

2643 

2644 target_repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

2645 try: 

2646 _git(target_repo, "add", "-A") 

2647 dirty = _git(target_repo, "status", "--porcelain").stdout.strip() 

2648 if dirty: 

2649 _git( 

2650 target_repo, 

2651 "commit", 

2652 "-m", 

2653 ( 

2654 f"wip(dev-exhausted): preserve partial work for story " 

2655 f"{story.id} ({story.slug})\n\n" 

2656 f"Dev exhausted {story.dev_retries} chain-level retries " 

2657 f"without reaching green. The chain commits this WIP so " 

2658 f"the work is recoverable from origin rather than living " 

2659 f"in a local stash. See ``factory why {story.id}`` for " 

2660 f"the per-attempt event log." 

2661 ), 

2662 ) 

2663 head_proc = _git(target_repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD") 

2664 commit_sha = head_proc.stdout.strip() or None 

2665 push_proc = _git( 

2666 target_repo, 

2667 "push", 

2668 "-u", 

2669 "origin", 

2670 story.github_branch or "HEAD", 

2671 check=False, 

2672 ) 

2673 commit_pushed = push_proc.returncode == 0 

2674 # Emit git signals — best-effort. 

2675 try: 

2676 from factory.manager.signals import write_git_event as _wge 

2677 

2678 if dirty: 

2679 _wge( 

2680 kind="commit", 

2681 story_id=story.id, 

2682 worktree_path=str(target_repo), 

2683 commit_sha=commit_sha, 

2684 result="ok", 

2685 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2686 ) 

2687 _wge( 

2688 kind="push", 

2689 story_id=story.id, 

2690 worktree_path=str(target_repo), 

2691 result="ok" if commit_pushed else "error", 

2692 error=None if commit_pushed else "push failed", 

2693 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2694 ) 

2695 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 

2696 pass 

2697 except Exception as commit_exc: 

2698 payload["dev_exhausted_commit_error"] = repr(commit_exc) 

2699 

2700 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_EXHAUSTED).value 

2701 _stall_note = ( 

2702 f"same failure signature {same_sig_count}x (>= {_MAX_DEV_SAME_SIGNATURE}); " 

2703 if same_sig_stall 

2704 else "" 

2705 ) 

2706 story.error = ( 

2707 f"dev exhausted retries ({story.dev_retries}); {_stall_note}" 

2708 f"partial work {'pushed to origin' if commit_pushed else 'committed locally'}" 

2709 f"{f' as {commit_sha[:12]}' if commit_sha else ''}" 

2710 ) 

2711 payload["dev_exhausted_commit_sha"] = commit_sha 

2712 payload["dev_exhausted_pushed"] = commit_pushed 

2713 if same_sig_stall: 

2714 payload["dev_same_signature_stall"] = same_sig_count 

2715 persist_story(story, db) 

2716 log_story_event( 

2717 story.id, 

2718 "dev_exhausted", 

2719 { 

2720 "retries": story.dev_retries, 

2721 "commit_sha": commit_sha, 

2722 "pushed": commit_pushed, 

2723 "files_changed": payload.get("files_changed", []), 

2724 # R2: distinguish "ran out of retry budget" from "same failure 

2725 # N times — escalated early on no new signal". 

2726 "reason": "same_failure_signature" if same_sig_stall else "max_retries", 

2727 "same_signature_count": same_sig_count if same_sig_stall else None, 

2728 }, 

2729 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2730 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2731 ) 

2732 # Exhausted retries with the new low cap + prior-attempts feed-forward 

2733 # is a strong signal something upstream of dev is wrong: tests are 

2734 # impossible, persona prompts need work, context docs lack 

2735 # information, or PM cut the story too broadly. Emit a structured 

2736 # "factory_needs_redesign" event with a recommendation so the 

2737 # operator (or a future improver persona) can act on it instead of 

2738 # just retrying more. 

2739 prior_attempts_summary = [] 

2740 try: 

2741 prior_attempts_summary = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

2742 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

2743 pass 

2744 

2745 # Heuristic suggestions based on what the diagnostic actually shows. 

2746 last_tail = "" 

2747 if prior_attempts_summary: 

2748 last_tail = prior_attempts_summary[-1].get("test_output_tail", "") 

2749 suggestions: list[str] = [] 

2750 if "ImportError" in last_tail or "ModuleNotFoundError" in last_tail: 

2751 suggestions.append( 

2752 "Test harness fails at import — check .env / DATABASE_URL " 

2753 "replication into the worktree, conftest dependencies, or " 

2754 "missing fixtures. Not a code issue dev can fix." 

2755 ) 

2756 if "TESTS_NEED_CLARIFICATION" in last_tail: 

2757 suggestions.append( 

2758 "Dev tried to escalate test-design — verify the escape " 

2759 "hatch wiring is firing and test_implementer re-ran with " 

2760 "the clarification." 

2761 ) 

2762 same_tails = ( 

2763 len(prior_attempts_summary) >= 2 

2764 and len({a.get("test_output_tail", "")[-300:] for a in prior_attempts_summary}) == 1 

2765 ) 

2766 if same_tails: 

2767 suggestions.append( 

2768 "All attempts hit the exact same failure tail — dev's LLM " 

2769 "is stuck on a problem code alone cannot fix. Re-prompt " 

2770 "test_implementer or revisit the story's acceptance criteria." 

2771 ) 

2772 if not suggestions: 

2773 suggestions.append( 

2774 "Investigate the per-story event log (``factory trace " 

2775 f"{story.id}``) and the partial commit on origin " 

2776 f"({commit_sha[:12] if commit_sha else 'no commit'}) — " 

2777 "the chain ran out of attempts but the cause isn't obvious " 

2778 "from the diagnostic." 

2779 ) 

2780 

2781 log_story_event( 

2782 story.id, 

2783 "factory_needs_redesign", 

2784 { 

2785 "kind": "dev_same_signature_stall" if same_sig_stall else "dev_exhausted", 

2786 "retries_used": story.dev_retries, 

2787 "max_retries": _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root), 

2788 "same_signature_count": same_sig_count if same_sig_stall else None, 

2789 "last_test_output_tail": last_tail[-600:], 

2790 "suggestions": suggestions, 

2791 "branch": story.github_branch, 

2792 "commit_sha": commit_sha, 

2793 }, 

2794 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2795 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2796 ) 

2797 

2798 # Post a comment on the direction's tracker issue (best-effort) so 

2799 # the signal is loud + persistent + linkable. 

2800 if not dry_run: 

2801 try: 

2802 _post_factory_needs_redesign_comment( 

2803 story=story, 

2804 app_config=app_config, 

2805 suggestions=suggestions, 

2806 last_tail=last_tail, 

2807 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2808 ) 

2809 except Exception as exc: # never let a comment failure mask the real return 

2810 log_story_event( 

2811 story.id, 

2812 "factory_needs_redesign_comment_failed", 

2813 {"error": repr(exc)}, 

2814 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2815 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2816 ) 

2817 

2818 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload, error=story.error) 

2819 

2820 # Escalate model tier on retry (standard -> hard). 

2821 if story.current_model_tier == "standard": 

2822 story.current_model_tier = "hard" 

2823 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DEV_TESTS_RED).value 

2824 persist_story(story, db) 

2825 log_story_event( 

2826 story.id, 

2827 "dev_retry", 

2828 { 

2829 "retries": story.dev_retries, 

2830 "model_tier": story.current_model_tier, 

2831 "files_changed": payload.get("files_changed", []), 

2832 "summary_tail": payload.get("summary", "")[-500:], 

2833 }, 

2834 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2835 ) 

2836 

2837 # Each retry IS a factory-improvement signal: under a healthy chain, 

2838 # most stories should land first-pass. A retry means something upstream 

2839 # of dev needs work — test_implementer wrote ambiguous tests, the persona 

2840 # prompts missed context, the harness was subtly off, etc. Emit a 

2841 # ``factory_needs_redesign`` event on EACH retry so it's visible early 

2842 # (via ``factory trace`` / the state event log) instead of waiting for 

2843 # exhaustion. ``kind: dev_retry_observed`` distinguishes this from the 

2844 # exhaustion event below. (Before 2026-08-07 this stream also fed the 

2845 # factory_improver persona; that consumer is gone, but the event is still 

2846 # the operator-visible early-warning signal.) 

2847 if not dry_run: 

2848 log_story_event( 

2849 story.id, 

2850 "factory_needs_redesign", 

2851 { 

2852 "kind": "dev_retry_observed", 

2853 "retries": story.dev_retries, 

2854 "max_retries": _max_dev_retries(software_factory_root), 

2855 "model_tier": story.current_model_tier, 

2856 "last_test_output_tail": (payload.get("summary") or "")[-600:], 

2857 "files_changed": payload.get("files_changed", [])[:10], 

2858 "branch": story.github_branch, 

2859 "suggestions": [ 

2860 "Inspect this story's dev retry — even a single retry is a " 

2861 "failure signal worth aggregating. Recurring retries on the " 

2862 "same persona / scope shape mean a prompt or harness gap." 

2863 ], 

2864 }, 

2865 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

2866 slug_hint=story.slug, 

2867 ) 

2868 

2869 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload) 

2870 

2871 

2872# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

2873# review 

2874# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

2875 

2876 

2877# Section caps for handle_review / handle_tech_writer prompt plumbing. Keep 

2878# these as module-level constants so the contract tests can import them. 

2879# Section caps for the assembled review/tech_writer prompts. These are 

2880# CHARACTER counts (str.__len__), not byte counts — Python's slicing 

2881# operates on characters, and ``len(s) <= N`` uses the same unit. The 

2882# ``_BYTES`` suffix is preserved for historical naming compatibility 

2883# (and because for ASCII-heavy persona output the two coincide); a future 

2884# refactor may rename them but the semantics are documented here so the 

2885# constant is not ambiguous. 

2886_STORY_CONTENT_CAP_BYTES = 32 * 1024 # characters; ~32KiB ASCII 

2887_TEST_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES = 8 * 1024 # characters; ~8KiB ASCII 

2888_PR_DIFF_CAP_BYTES = 64 * 1024 # characters; ~64KiB ASCII 

2889 

2890# Markers that indicate a prompt section was NOT populated with real data 

2891# (the literal placeholder strings that caused stories 5/15/16/18/19/22 to 

2892# cycle dev<->reviewer 5+ times). The sanity guard in handle_review raises 

2893# RuntimeError if any of these survive into the final prompt; the prompt 

2894# logger in factory.runner.text_run also scans for them so the watcher can 

2895# surface regressions before they burn another month of reviewer cycles. 

2896_BROKEN_PROMPT_MARKERS: tuple[str, ...] = ( 

2897 "(fetched from GitHub by the chain", 

2898 "placeholder for real-run", 

2899 # The literal "(see {" never appears when the f-string interpolates a 

2900 # real path — only when the f-string itself was removed and replaced 

2901 # by a bare string. We match the literal substring so a regressing 

2902 # author swapping the f-string out is caught. 

2903 "(see {", 

2904 # Diff-fetch failure text. ``_fetch_pr_diff_for_review`` used to be 

2905 # FAIL-OPEN: any ``gh pr diff`` / ``git diff`` failure returned the error 

2906 # text AS the diff, so the reviewer reviewed blind and produced "I cannot 

2907 # see the diff" blocking findings — a $0.008 reviewer decision triggering 

2908 # ~45x that in dev rework per cycle (2026-07-31 SWE-bench batch: rc=128 

2909 # on a missing ``origin/<base>`` ref poisoned EVERY review). The fetch now 

2910 # RAISES ``ReviewDiffUnavailableError`` instead (fail-closed, handled at 

2911 # both call sites before any prompt is built), so these strings must never 

2912 # reach a prompt again; the markers are the backstop that catches a 

2913 # regression to fail-open. 

2914 # 

2915 # Two rules keep the backstop from misfiring on LEGITIMATE prompt content 

2916 # (the diff section and test output embed arbitrary code/prose — a 

2917 # committed line like ``msg = f"command returned rc={rc}"`` crashed a real 

2918 # review when the marker was the bare ``"returned rc="``): 

2919 # * anchor on the parenthesized/format-specific prefixes only the OLD 

2920 # fail-open plumbing emitted, never on generic prose fragments; 

2921 # * build each marker by CONCATENATION so the contiguous literal never 

2922 # appears in this repo's own source — otherwise any loop-2 self-edit 

2923 # whose diff context includes this very tuple would trip the guard and 

2924 # crash-loop the review. 

2925 # old gh fail-open prefix: paren + command + "#" + PR number + rc text 

2926 "(gh pr diff " + "#", 

2927 # old git fail-open midsection: base ref ellipsis + HEAD + rc text 

2928 "...HEAD " + "returned rc=", 

2929 "(gh pr diff " + "failed", 

2930 "(git diff worktree " + "failed", 

2931 "(could not resolve " + "writing worktree", 

2932) 

2933 

2934 

2935def _read_story_file_content(story: StoryRecord, software_factory_root: Path) -> str: 

2936 """Return the story markdown content, capped, with a clear error fallback. 

2937 

2938 The reviewer / tech_writer prompts used to embed ``(see <path>)`` instead 

2939 of the actual file content — that meant the LLM was guessing about the 

2940 story's acceptance criteria and routinely demanded clarifications about 

2941 information that was already on disk. 

2942 """ 

2943 if not story.story_file_path: 

2944 return "(no story_file_path on record)" 

2945 story_path = software_factory_root / "apps" / story.app / story.story_file_path 

2946 try: 

2947 content = story_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") 

2948 except (OSError, FileNotFoundError) as exc: 

2949 return f"(story file unreadable at {story_path}: {exc!r})" 

2950 if len(content) > _STORY_CONTENT_CAP_BYTES: 

2951 content = content[:_STORY_CONTENT_CAP_BYTES] + "\n...[truncated at 32KB]" 

2952 return content 

2953 

2954 

2955def _fetch_latest_test_output( 

2956 story: StoryRecord, 

2957 software_factory_root: Path, 

2958) -> str: 

2959 """Return the most recent test output for ``story``. 

2960 

2961 Preference order (richest signal first): 

2962 

2963 1. The last entry of ``story.dev_attempts_json`` — dev writes a 

2964 ``test_output_tail`` (1800 char tail) here on every red retry. This 

2965 is the freshest signal when dev has run at least once. 

2966 2. The most recent ``harness_precheck`` event in the per-story log — 

2967 captures the output_tail of the one-shot pytest collect+exit that 

2968 the chain runs before dev. Useful when the story bounced back to 

2969 reviewer before dev produced an attempt of its own (e.g. tech_writer 

2970 failure routed to REVIEWER_REQUESTED_CHANGES). 

2971 3. ``"(no recent test run on record)"`` — explicit signal to the 

2972 reviewer that test output isn't available, instead of an empty 

2973 JSON object that looks indistinguishable from a passing run. 

2974 

2975 Output is capped at 8KB regardless of source. 

2976 """ 

2977 # 1. dev_attempts_json (preferred) 

2978 if story.dev_attempts_json: 

2979 try: 

2980 attempts = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json) 

2981 except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError): 

2982 attempts = None 

2983 if isinstance(attempts, list) and attempts: 

2984 last = attempts[-1] 

2985 tail = (last.get("test_output_tail") or "").strip() 

2986 if tail: 

2987 passed = last.get("test_run_passed") 

2988 verdict = "PASSED" if passed is True else "FAILED" if passed is False else "unknown" 

2989 header = ( 

2990 f"(from dev_attempts[-1]; " 

2991 f"attempt={last.get('attempt')!r} " 

2992 f"ts={last.get('ts')!r} " 

2993 f"run_verdict={verdict})\n" 

2994 ) 

2995 body = header + tail 

2996 if len(body) > _TEST_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES: 

2997 body = body[:_TEST_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES] + "\n...[truncated at 8KB]" 

2998 return body 

2999 

3000 # 2. harness_precheck event log 

3001 if story.id is not None: 

3002 try: 

3003 from factory.chain.event_log import read_story_events 

3004 

3005 events = read_story_events( 

3006 story.id, 

3007 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3008 slug_hint=story.slug, 

3009 ) 

3010 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 — log read must never break review 

3011 events = [] 

3012 for ev in reversed(events): 

3013 if ev.get("event") == "harness_precheck" and ev.get("output_tail"): 

3014 tail = str(ev.get("output_tail")).strip() 

3015 header = ( 

3016 f"(from harness_precheck event; " 

3017 f"exit_code={ev.get('exit_code')!r} " 

3018 f"passed={ev.get('passed')!r} " 

3019 f"ts={ev.get('ts')!r})\n" 

3020 ) 

3021 body = header + tail 

3022 if len(body) > _TEST_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES: 

3023 body = body[:_TEST_OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES] + "\n...[truncated at 8KB]" 

3024 return body 

3025 

3026 return "(no recent test run on record)" 

3027 

3028 

3029# Cap for the dev self-summary embedded in the reviewer prompt. Matches the 

3030# 2000-char cap ``_handle_dev_once`` applies when persisting the attempt. 

3031_SELF_SUMMARY_PROMPT_CAP = 2000 

3032 

3033 

3034def _fetch_latest_dev_self_summary(story: StoryRecord) -> str: 

3035 """Return the last dev attempt's ``self_summary``, or an explicit sentinel. 

3036 

3037 Same source as ``_fetch_latest_test_output`` preference 1: the trailing 

3038 entry of ``story.dev_attempts_json``. The reviewer needs this because the 

3039 dev's story-silent choices (invented literals, fixture shapes, data 

3040 sources) are only defensible via the precedent the dev cited here — the 

3041 2026-08-02 SWE-bench autopsies found every wrong patch was approved with 

3042 zero findings partly because the reviewer was never told which choices 

3043 were dev-invented versus story-mandated. 

3044 

3045 The sentinel for "no summary" is deliberate reviewable signal, never an 

3046 empty string: a dev that provided no self-summary skipped its own 

3047 output contract, and the reviewer should see that. 

3048 """ 

3049 sentinel = "(dev provided no self-summary)" 

3050 try: 

3051 attempts = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

3052 except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError): 

3053 return sentinel 

3054 if not isinstance(attempts, list) or not attempts: 

3055 return sentinel 

3056 last = attempts[-1] 

3057 if not isinstance(last, dict): 

3058 return sentinel 

3059 summary = str(last.get("self_summary") or "").strip() 

3060 if not summary: 

3061 return sentinel 

3062 return summary[:_SELF_SUMMARY_PROMPT_CAP] 

3063 

3064 

3065def _has_real_dev_attempt(story: StoryRecord) -> bool: 

3066 """True when at least one REAL (non-dry-run) dev attempt is on record. 

3067 

3068 ``dev_attempts_json`` is only ever appended to by ``_handle_dev_once`` 

3069 on a non-dry-run completion — both the green-run record and the 

3070 red-run/retry record are gated behind ``if not dry_run:`` (see 

3071 ``_handle_dev_once``). So a non-empty list here is proof a real dev 

3072 sandbox actually ran, which is the signal the empty-diff short-circuit 

3073 needs before it's allowed to fire — it must never trigger on a story 

3074 that hasn't given dev a real chance yet. 

3075 """ 

3076 try: 

3077 parsed = json.loads(story.dev_attempts_json or "[]") 

3078 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

3079 return False 

3080 return isinstance(parsed, list) and len(parsed) > 0 

3081 

3082 

3083def _dev_produced_empty_diff( 

3084 story: StoryRecord, 

3085 app_config: AppConfig, 

3086 software_factory_root: Path, 

3087) -> bool | None: 

3088 """Best-effort check: is the story's branch diff-empty against its base? 

3089 

3090 Returns ``True`` when the COMMITTED diff (``git diff --quiet 

3091 origin/<base>...HEAD``) AND the working tree are both empty — i.e. the 

3092 dev genuinely produced nothing at all — ``False`` when either a real 

3093 committed diff OR uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes exist, or 

3094 ``None`` when the check itself could not be performed (no worktree yet, 

3095 git error, unexpected exit code, neither ``origin/<base>`` nor a local 

3096 ``<base>`` ref resolving). ``None`` means "unknown" — callers MUST treat 

3097 it as "do not short-circuit" and fall back to the normal review path. 

3098 

3099 The working-tree check matters because the dev's "work happened" signal 

3100 is commit-agnostic: ``files_changed``/``test_run_passed`` come from the 

3101 on-disk working tree (``git status --porcelain`` / the pytest run 

3102 against it), but the dev agent is only INSTRUCTED to commit, not forced 

3103 to. An agent that produces real, test-passing work but never runs its 

3104 final ``git commit`` (e.g. it hit a turn/timeout limit) would otherwise 

3105 show an empty COMMITTED diff and get permanently blocked on its first 

3106 pass — worse than the review churn this check exists to prevent. So an 

3107 uncommitted/untracked change in the worktree is treated the same as a 

3108 committed one: NOT empty, fall back to the normal review path (which at 

3109 least gives dev more retries to land the commit). 

3110 """ 

3111 import subprocess 

3112 

3113 try: 

3114 worktree = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

3115 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - best-effort, fail open 

3116 return None 

3117 

3118 # Working-tree check FIRST: uncommitted/untracked changes mean dev did 

3119 # real work even if it never committed. Never short-circuit on that. 

3120 try: 

3121 status_proc = subprocess.run( 

3122 ["git", "status", "--porcelain"], 

3123 cwd=str(worktree), 

3124 capture_output=True, 

3125 text=True, 

3126 # Paths in status output are arbitrary bytes; tolerate rather 

3127 # than strict-decode-crash (UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, 

3128 # outside the OSError taxonomy below). 

3129 errors="replace", 

3130 check=False, 

3131 timeout=30, 

3132 ) 

3133 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError): 

3134 return None 

3135 if status_proc.returncode != 0: 

3136 return None 

3137 if status_proc.stdout.strip(): 

3138 return False 

3139 

3140 base = app_config.default_branch or "main" 

3141 # origin/<base> → local <base> fallback (see _resolve_diff_base): keeps 

3142 # this check consistent with _fetch_pr_diff_for_review in worktrees that 

3143 # have no ``origin`` remote, instead of degrading to "unknown" there. 

3144 base_ref = _resolve_diff_base(worktree, base) 

3145 if base_ref is None: 

3146 return None 

3147 try: 

3148 proc = subprocess.run( 

3149 ["git", "diff", "--quiet", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"], 

3150 cwd=str(worktree), 

3151 capture_output=True, 

3152 text=True, 

3153 errors="replace", 

3154 check=False, 

3155 timeout=30, 

3156 ) 

3157 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError): 

3158 return None 

3159 # ``git diff --quiet`` exits 0 (no diff), 1 (diff present), or >1 on a 

3160 # real error (e.g. bad/missing ref) — only 0/1 are meaningful signals. 

3161 if proc.returncode == 0: 

3162 return True 

3163 if proc.returncode == 1: 

3164 return False 

3165 return None 

3166 

3167 

3168class ReviewDiffUnavailableError(RuntimeError): 

3169 """The diff a persona must judge could not be fetched. 

3170 

3171 Raised by ``_fetch_pr_diff_for_review`` on ANY fetch failure (``gh pr 

3172 diff`` non-zero, git error, missing base ref, unresolvable worktree). 

3173 This is deliberately an exception, not an in-band error string: the old 

3174 fail-open behaviour returned the error text AS the diff, the reviewer 

3175 reviewed blind, and every cheap "I cannot see the diff" blocking finding 

3176 triggered a ~45x more expensive dev rework cycle (observed 2026-07-31: 

3177 a missing ``origin/<base>`` ref made ``git diff`` return rc=128 in every 

3178 review of every SWE-bench batch). Callers must treat this as a hard 

3179 precondition failure: no model call, no review-cycle burn, route the 

3180 story to a blocked state a human can see. 

3181 """ 

3182 

3183 def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None: 

3184 super().__init__(reason) 

3185 self.reason = reason 

3186 

3187 

3188def _resolve_diff_base(worktree: Path, base: str) -> str | None: 

3189 """Return the first base ref that resolves in ``worktree``, or ``None``. 

3190 

3191 Fallback chain: ``origin/<base>`` (the normal topology against a real 

3192 remote), then local ``<base>`` (worktrees cut from a repo with no 

3193 ``origin`` remote — e.g. a bench harness or a local-only app repo). 

3194 ``None`` means neither ref exists (or git itself failed) — callers must 

3195 fail CLOSED on it, never guess. 

3196 """ 

3197 import subprocess 

3198 

3199 for ref in (f"origin/{base}", base): 

3200 try: 

3201 proc = subprocess.run( 

3202 ["git", "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{ref}^{{commit}}"], 

3203 cwd=str(worktree), 

3204 capture_output=True, 

3205 text=True, 

3206 errors="replace", 

3207 check=False, 

3208 timeout=30, 

3209 ) 

3210 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError): 

3211 return None 

3212 if proc.returncode == 0: 

3213 return ref 

3214 return None 

3215 

3216 

3217def _fetch_pr_diff_for_review( 

3218 story: StoryRecord, 

3219 app_config: AppConfig, 

3220 software_factory_root: Path, 

3221) -> str: 

3222 """Return the diff the reviewer should look at. FAIL-CLOSED. 

3223 

3224 Two cases: 

3225 

3226 * ``story.github_pr_number`` is set → ``gh pr diff <num> -R <repo>``. 

3227 This is the source of truth once a PR exists. 

3228 * Otherwise → ``git diff <base>...HEAD`` inside the per-story worktree, 

3229 where ``<base>`` is resolved by ``_resolve_diff_base`` (``origin/<base>`` 

3230 first, then local ``<base>``). The chain creates a PR lazily; reviewer 

3231 can fire before that point, and we still want a real diff, not a 

3232 placeholder. 

3233 

3234 The result is capped at 64KB. A genuinely EMPTY diff is returned as ``""`` 

3235 — the call sites decide what an empty diff means for their persona (a 

3236 reviewer cannot approve zero commits). Any fetch FAILURE raises 

3237 ``ReviewDiffUnavailableError`` — this helper must never return error text 

3238 as if it were a diff (the fail-open bug that produced blind reviews). The 

3239 BROKEN_PROMPT_MARKERS guard downstream is the backstop that catches a 

3240 regression to fail-open. 

3241 """ 

3242 import subprocess 

3243 

3244 diff_text: str 

3245 

3246 pr_number = story.github_pr_number 

3247 if pr_number is not None: 

3248 try: 

3249 proc = subprocess.run( 

3250 ["gh", "pr", "diff", str(pr_number), "-R", app_config.repo], 

3251 capture_output=True, 

3252 text=True, 

3253 # Diffs are arbitrary bytes: repos legitimately contain 

3254 # non-UTF-8 source (latin-1 files in django et al.). Without 

3255 # this, ``text=True`` strict-decodes inside communicate() and 

3256 # a UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError — outside the OSError 

3257 # taxonomy) escapes the fail-closed contract entirely. A few 

3258 # U+FFFD replacement chars in an otherwise-real diff is far 

3259 # better than a crash-looping review. 

3260 errors="replace", 

3261 check=False, 

3262 timeout=30, 

3263 ) 

3264 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError) as exc: 

3265 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError(f"gh pr diff #{pr_number} failed: {exc!r}") from exc 

3266 if proc.returncode != 0: 

3267 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError( 

3268 f"gh pr diff #{pr_number} exited rc={proc.returncode}; " 

3269 f"stderr_tail={proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]!r}" 

3270 ) 

3271 diff_text = proc.stdout or "" 

3272 else: 

3273 # No PR yet — diff the worktree against the default branch. 

3274 try: 

3275 worktree = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

3276 except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 

3277 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError( 

3278 f"could not resolve writing worktree: {exc!r}" 

3279 ) from exc 

3280 base = app_config.default_branch or "main" 

3281 base_ref = _resolve_diff_base(worktree, base) 

3282 if base_ref is None: 

3283 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError( 

3284 f"no diff base ref: neither 'origin/{base}' nor '{base}' " 

3285 f"resolves in worktree {worktree}" 

3286 ) 

3287 try: 

3288 proc = subprocess.run( 

3289 ["git", "diff", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"], 

3290 cwd=str(worktree), 

3291 capture_output=True, 

3292 text=True, 

3293 # See the gh-path comment: diffs are arbitrary bytes; never 

3294 # let a non-UTF-8 hunk strict-decode into a crash. 

3295 errors="replace", 

3296 check=False, 

3297 timeout=30, 

3298 ) 

3299 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError) as exc: 

3300 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError(f"git diff in worktree failed: {exc!r}") from exc 

3301 if proc.returncode != 0: 

3302 raise ReviewDiffUnavailableError( 

3303 f"git diff {base_ref}...HEAD exited rc={proc.returncode}; " 

3304 f"stderr_tail={proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]!r}" 

3305 ) 

3306 diff_text = proc.stdout or "" 

3307 

3308 if not diff_text.strip(): 

3309 return "" 

3310 if len(diff_text) > _PR_DIFF_CAP_BYTES: 

3311 diff_text = diff_text[:_PR_DIFF_CAP_BYTES] + "\n...[truncated at 64KB]" 

3312 return diff_text 

3313 

3314 

3315def _changed_files_for_story( 

3316 story: StoryRecord, 

3317 app_config: AppConfig, 

3318 software_factory_root: Path, 

3319) -> list[str] | None: 

3320 """Return the branch's REAL changed-file list, or ``None`` if it cannot be 

3321 computed (worktree GC'd, git error, timeout). 

3322 

3323 Uses ``git diff --name-only <base_ref>...HEAD`` inside the per-story 

3324 worktree — the SAME merge-base semantics AND the same 

3325 ``origin/<base>`` → local ``<base>`` fallback (``_resolve_diff_base``) 

3326 ``_fetch_pr_diff_for_review`` uses on its pre-PR path — so the 

3327 docs-enforcer's vacuous-diff guard and the reviewer agree on what the 

3328 branch changed. The enforcer runs before PR creation in the 

3329 normal chain (pr_number is None), so they match in practice; once a PR 

3330 exists the reviewer switches to ``gh pr diff`` (the remote PR), which can 

3331 differ from the local worktree HEAD. 

3332 

3333 Returning ``None`` (never ``[]``) on failure lets the caller distinguish 

3334 "no diff available, fall back to declared paths" from "the branch genuinely 

3335 changed nothing" (``[]``, which the vacuous-diff guard blocks). 

3336 """ 

3337 import subprocess 

3338 

3339 try: 

3340 worktree = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

3341 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - any worktree resolution failure → fall back 

3342 return None 

3343 base = app_config.default_branch or "main" 

3344 # Same origin/<base> → local <base> fallback as _fetch_pr_diff_for_review, 

3345 # so the docs-enforcer and the reviewer keep agreeing on what changed even 

3346 # in a worktree with no ``origin`` remote. 

3347 base_ref = _resolve_diff_base(worktree, base) 

3348 if base_ref is None: 

3349 return None 

3350 try: 

3351 proc = subprocess.run( 

3352 ["git", "diff", "--name-only", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"], 

3353 cwd=str(worktree), 

3354 capture_output=True, 

3355 text=True, 

3356 # Filenames are arbitrary bytes too (git quotes non-UTF-8 paths, 

3357 # but never rely on it): tolerate, don't strict-decode-crash. 

3358 errors="replace", 

3359 check=False, 

3360 timeout=30, 

3361 ) 

3362 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError): 

3363 return None 

3364 if proc.returncode != 0: 

3365 return None 

3366 return [line.strip() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()] 

3367 

3368 

3369def _assert_no_broken_prompt_markers(full_prompt: str, *, where: str) -> None: 

3370 """Sanity guard — raise if a literal placeholder leaked into the prompt. 

3371 

3372 See ``_BROKEN_PROMPT_MARKERS`` for the list. Raised as ``RuntimeError`` 

3373 so the orchestrator's normal error handling captures + logs the failure 

3374 instead of silently feeding an inert prompt to the LLM. 

3375 """ 

3376 for marker in _BROKEN_PROMPT_MARKERS: 

3377 if marker in full_prompt: 

3378 raise RuntimeError( 

3379 f"{where} produced a prompt containing broken plumbing marker " 

3380 f"{marker!r}; check that PR diff and test output fetches " 

3381 f"actually executed." 

3382 ) 

3383 

3384 

3385def _empty_diff_review_result(story: StoryRecord) -> dict[str, Any]: 

3386 """Deterministic request_changes for a branch whose fetched diff is EMPTY. 

3387 

3388 A reviewer cannot approve zero commits, so we never spend a model call on 

3389 an empty diff (the old behaviour embedded "(diff is empty …)" as the 

3390 prompt's diff section — and the model could, and in mocked tests did, 

3391 APPROVE it). The confirmed-empty case (real dev attempt + clean worktree) 

3392 is blocked earlier by the ``_dev_produced_empty_diff`` short-circuit; what 

3393 reaches here is the "give dev another chance" remainder — most commonly 

3394 real, test-passing work left UNCOMMITTED in the worktree (the dev agent is 

3395 only INSTRUCTED to commit, not forced; see ``_dev_produced_empty_diff``). 

3396 The synthetic finding routes back to dev with an explicit instruction. 

3397 Deliberately bounded: the constant findings text gives an identical 

3398 ``_findings_signature`` and the frozen 0.0 score never improves, so the 

3399 stuck + non-improving guards block the story on the second occurrence — 

3400 this path can never churn to the hard cap. 

3401 """ 

3402 return { 

3403 "verdict": "request_changes", 

3404 "summary": ( 

3405 "empty diff: the branch has no committed changes beyond its base. " 

3406 "A reviewer cannot approve zero commits. If real work exists in " 

3407 "the worktree it was never committed — commit it." 

3408 ), 

3409 "findings": [ 

3410 { 

3411 "severity": "high", 

3412 "criterion": "completeness", 

3413 "location": "", 

3414 "what": ( 

3415 "empty diff: no committed changes on this branch beyond " 

3416 "its base — commit the work (uncommitted files do not ship)" 

3417 ), 

3418 } 

3419 ], 

3420 "test_quality_findings": [], 

3421 "test_quality_score": 0.0, 

3422 "comments_to_post": [], 

3423 "empty_diff_precondition": True, 

3424 } 

3425 

3426 

3427def _block_on_unavailable_diff( 

3428 story: StoryRecord, 

3429 app_config: AppConfig, 

3430 software_factory_root: Path, 

3431 *, 

3432 persona: str, 

3433 reason: str, 

3434 db: Path, 

3435 github_client: Any = None, 

3436) -> HandlerResult: 

3437 """Route a story whose diff could not be fetched to the blocked sink. 

3438 

3439 FAIL-CLOSED hard-precondition handling shared by ``handle_review`` and 

3440 ``handle_tech_writer``: the model is never called, ``reviewer_cycles`` is 

3441 never incremented (this is an infra failure, not a review verdict), and 

3442 the story lands in ``BLOCKED_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT`` — the same 

3443 human-visible sink the empty-diff short-circuit and the convergence guard 

3444 use. From there the bounded blocked-story auto-recovery 

3445 (``orchestrator._AUTO_RECOVERABLE_STATES``) re-enters the chain at 

3446 ``SM_DONE`` for transient causes (gh auth expiry, rate limit), and a 

3447 persistent cause surfaces to the operator (``last_rejection_reason`` puts 

3448 it in ``factory inbox``; the stalled-stories detector sees the state). 

3449 """ 

3450 full_reason = f"{persona} diff precondition failed (fail-closed): {reason}" 

3451 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT).value 

3452 story.error = full_reason 

3453 # Surfaces the story in the `factory inbox` "Needs human action" table, 

3454 # which keys off last_rejection_reason for states outside its small 

3455 # state allowlist. 

3456 story.last_rejection_reason = full_reason 

3457 result: dict[str, Any] = { 

3458 "verdict": "request_changes", 

3459 "summary": full_reason, 

3460 "findings": [], 

3461 "test_quality_findings": [], 

3462 "test_quality_score": 0.0, 

3463 "comments_to_post": [], 

3464 "review_diff_unavailable": True, 

3465 } 

3466 if persona == "reviewer": 

3467 # Keep the review record honest for dev plumbing. tech_writer must 

3468 # NOT overwrite reviewer_result_json — it holds the real approve. 

3469 # Deliberately NOT appended to reviewer_history_json: this is an 

3470 # infra failure, not a review verdict, and a synthetic 0.0-score 

3471 # history entry would make the next REAL rejection trivially count 

3472 # as "improving" in the non-improving-score guard (one wasted cycle). 

3473 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

3474 persist_story(story, db) 

3475 log_story_event( 

3476 story.id, 

3477 "review_diff_unavailable", 

3478 { 

3479 "persona": persona, 

3480 "reason": reason[:500], 

3481 "branch": story.github_branch, 

3482 "pr_number": story.github_pr_number, 

3483 "reviewer_cycles": story.reviewer_cycles, 

3484 }, 

3485 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3486 slug_hint=story.slug, 

3487 ) 

3488 if github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

3489 try: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3490 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

3491 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

3492 pr.add_to_labels("review-nonconvergent") 

3493 pr.create_issue_comment( 

3494 f"⚠️ Diff precondition failed for {persona}: {reason}. " 

3495 f"Failing CLOSED (no blind review) and routing to " 

3496 f"{StoryState.BLOCKED_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT.value}." 

3497 ) 

3498 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3499 pass 

3500 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result, error=story.error) 

3501 

3502 

3503def _dry_run_review(story: StoryRecord) -> dict[str, Any]: 

3504 return { 

3505 "verdict": "approve", 

3506 "findings": [], 

3507 "test_quality_score": 0.92, 

3508 "test_quality_findings": [], 

3509 "comments_to_post": [], 

3510 "summary": "Dry-run reviewer: approve.", 

3511 } 

3512 

3513 

3514def _slop_findings_for_story( 

3515 story: StoryRecord, app_config: AppConfig, software_factory_root: Path 

3516) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: 

3517 """Programmatically scan the dev-written test files for slop anti-patterns. 

3518 

3519 Loop-4 backstop for the dev-owns-tests model: scans the test files this 

3520 story's branch changed (relative to ``origin/main``) with the pure 

3521 ``slop_detector``. Returns a list of ``test_quality_findings``-shaped dicts 

3522 (empty when clean). Defensive: any git/IO failure returns ``[]`` so a 

3523 transient infra problem never blocks a review — the LLM reviewer remains 

3524 the primary judge; this only ADDS deterministic vetoes, never removes them. 

3525 """ 

3526 try: 

3527 from factory.chain.branch import find_test_files_in_diff 

3528 from factory.chain.slop_detector import scan_file 

3529 

3530 worktree = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

3531 base_ref = None 

3532 for candidate in ("origin/main", "main", "HEAD~1"): 

3533 try: 

3534 from factory.chain.branch import _run_git 

3535 

3536 _run_git(worktree, "rev-parse", "--verify", candidate) 

3537 base_ref = candidate 

3538 break 

3539 except Exception: 

3540 continue 

3541 if base_ref is None: 

3542 return [] 

3543 test_paths = find_test_files_in_diff(worktree, base_ref=base_ref) 

3544 findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] 

3545 for rel in test_paths: 

3546 for f in scan_file(worktree / rel): 

3547 findings.append( 

3548 { 

3549 "test_name": f"{f.path}:{f.line}", 

3550 "issue": f"slop: {f.kind} — {f.why_slop}", 

3551 "fix_suggestion": ( 

3552 "Replace this with an assertion on the real behavior " 

3553 "of the code under test. Make the test fail against an " 

3554 "absent/empty implementation first, then pass." 

3555 ), 

3556 "code_excerpt": f.code_excerpt, 

3557 } 

3558 ) 

3559 return findings 

3560 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - defensive; never block on infra 

3561 return [] 

3562 

3563 

3564def handle_review( 

3565 story: StoryRecord, 

3566 app_config: AppConfig, 

3567 software_factory_root: Path, 

3568 *, 

3569 dry_run: bool = False, 

3570 db_path: Path | None = None, 

3571 fixture: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

3572 github_client: Any = None, 

3573) -> HandlerResult: 

3574 """Run the Reviewer persona; post inline PR comments; transition state. 

3575 

3576 ``fixture`` lets tests inject a specific reviewer JSON (e.g. a 

3577 low-test-quality-score scenario). 

3578 """ 

3579 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

3580 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEWER_STARTED).value 

3581 persist_story(story, db) 

3582 

3583 # Empty-diff short-circuit. Real (non-fixture, non-dry-run) reviews only: 

3584 # fixture-driven and dry-run tests never touch git and must be 

3585 # completely unaffected. When a REAL dev attempt has already run 

3586 # (``_has_real_dev_attempt``) and the branch's diff against its base is 

3587 # CONFIRMED empty (``_dev_produced_empty_diff`` returns True, never on 

3588 # an unknown/error result), the dev produced no changes at all. 

3589 # Continuing into the normal review flow would waste an LLM call only to 

3590 # have the reviewer correctly reject it, then churn a full 

3591 # request_changes cycle, repeating up to ``_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES`` times 

3592 # before blocking (observed: D092/D094 each burned ~6 empty-diff cycles). 

3593 # Escalate straight to the terminal blocked state on the FIRST 

3594 # occurrence instead. 

3595 if fixture is None and not dry_run and _has_real_dev_attempt(story): 

3596 empty_diff = _dev_produced_empty_diff(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

3597 if empty_diff is True: 

3598 reason = ( 

3599 f"empty diff after dev attempt {story.dev_retries} — the dev " 

3600 "produced no changes; escalating instead of churning review " 

3601 "cycles; likely an un-doable-by-sandbox (runtime/operational) " 

3602 "task or a malformed story." 

3603 ) 

3604 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT).value 

3605 story.error = reason 

3606 result = { 

3607 "verdict": "request_changes", 

3608 "summary": reason, 

3609 "findings": [], 

3610 "test_quality_findings": [], 

3611 "test_quality_score": 0.0, 

3612 "empty_diff_short_circuit": True, 

3613 } 

3614 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

3615 _append_reviewer_history(story, result) 

3616 persist_story(story, db) 

3617 log_story_event( 

3618 story.id, 

3619 "factory_needs_redesign", 

3620 { 

3621 "kind": "empty_diff_short_circuit", 

3622 "dev_retries": story.dev_retries, 

3623 "reviewer_cycles": story.reviewer_cycles, 

3624 "branch": story.github_branch, 

3625 "suggestions": [ 

3626 "Dev produced an empty diff after a real attempt — " 

3627 "likely a task that isn't doable by a code sandbox " 

3628 "(a runtime/operational task) or a malformed story. " 

3629 "Investigate before re-dispatching; do not just " 

3630 "retry the same chain.", 

3631 ], 

3632 }, 

3633 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3634 slug_hint=story.slug, 

3635 ) 

3636 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

3637 try: 

3638 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

3639 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

3640 pr.add_to_labels("review-nonconvergent") 

3641 pr.create_issue_comment( 

3642 "⚠️ Empty-diff short-circuit: the dev produced no " 

3643 "changes on this branch. Routing directly to " 

3644 f"{StoryState.BLOCKED_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT.value} " 

3645 "instead of churning review cycles." 

3646 ) 

3647 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3648 pass 

3649 return HandlerResult( 

3650 next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result, error=story.error 

3651 ) 

3652 

3653 if fixture is not None: 

3654 result = fixture 

3655 elif dry_run: 

3656 result = _dry_run_review(story) 

3657 else: 

3658 # FAIL-CLOSED diff precondition. Fetched BEFORE any prompt assembly or 

3659 # model call: an unavailable diff must never be reviewed around (the 

3660 # old fail-open behaviour fed the fetch's error text to the model as 

3661 # the diff, and every blind "I cannot see the diff" rejection bought a 

3662 # ~45x more expensive dev rework cycle). 

3663 try: 

3664 pr_diff = _fetch_pr_diff_for_review(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

3665 except ReviewDiffUnavailableError as exc: 

3666 return _block_on_unavailable_diff( 

3667 story, 

3668 app_config, 

3669 software_factory_root, 

3670 persona="reviewer", 

3671 reason=exc.reason, 

3672 db=db, 

3673 github_client=github_client, 

3674 ) 

3675 if not pr_diff.strip(): 

3676 # Empty diff: never call the model — a reviewer cannot approve 

3677 # zero commits. Deterministic request_changes that flows through 

3678 # the normal verdict machinery below (cycle count, stuck + 

3679 # non-improving guards), so it stays bounded. 

3680 result = _empty_diff_review_result(story) 

3681 else: 

3682 from factory.app_config import resolve_app_repo_path 

3683 from factory.context.loader import compose_context_prelude 

3684 from factory.directions.parser import get_direction_chain 

3685 from factory.runner import text_run 

3686 

3687 persona = "reviewer" 

3688 persona_prompt = _read_persona_prompt(persona) 

3689 direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

3690 chain = ( 

3691 get_direction_chain(direction, software_factory_root) 

3692 if direction is not None 

3693 else None 

3694 ) 

3695 prelude = compose_context_prelude( 

3696 persona=persona, 

3697 app_repo_path=resolve_app_repo_path(app_config, software_factory_root), 

3698 task_scope=story.scope, 

3699 direction_chain=chain, 

3700 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3701 ) 

3702 story_content = _read_story_file_content(story, software_factory_root) 

3703 fresh_test_output = _fetch_latest_test_output(story, software_factory_root) 

3704 dev_self_summary = _fetch_latest_dev_self_summary(story) 

3705 rcaps = ( 

3706 "## App test capabilities (HONOR when judging test choices)\n\n" 

3707 f"* `e2e_harness_ready`: {str(app_config.gates.e2e_harness_ready).lower()}\n" 

3708 "* If false, this app has NO runnable Playwright/browser harness. Do " 

3709 "NOT require Playwright/E2E and do NOT flag a finding because a smoke/" 

3710 "flow test was written as pytest/httpx instead of Playwright — that " 

3711 "is the CORRECT choice here, and a backend test that covers the " 

3712 "behavior fully satisfies the acceptance criterion. Treat any stray " 

3713 "Playwright config/spec or 'playwright not wired' as NON-blocking " 

3714 "(`low`), never `medium`/`high`.\n\n" 

3715 ) 

3716 history_section = _render_reviewer_history_section(story) 

3717 full_prompt = ( 

3718 f"{persona_prompt.rstrip()}\n\n" 

3719 "---\n\n" 

3720 "## Context\n\n" 

3721 f"{prelude.rstrip()}\n\n" 

3722 f"{rcaps}" + (f"{history_section}\n\n" if history_section else "") + "## Story\n\n"
