3723 f"{story_content}\n\n" 

3724 "## Test plan\n\n" 

3725 f"{story.test_plan_json or '{}'}\n\n" 

3726 "## Latest test output\n\n" 

3727 f"{fresh_test_output}\n\n" 

3728 "## DEV SELF-SUMMARY (dev's own unverified claims, including " 

3729 "which precedent it followed)\n\n" 

3730 f"{dev_self_summary}\n\n" 

3731 "## PR diff\n\n" 

3732 f"{pr_diff}\n\n" 

3733 "Return the JSON object for the review. No prose outside the JSON." 

3734 ) 

3735 _assert_no_broken_prompt_markers(full_prompt, where="handle_review") 

3736 model_id = route(persona) 

3737 result_any = text_run( 

3738 persona=persona, 

3739 prompt=full_prompt, 

3740 model_id=model_id, 

3741 schema=None, # reviewer output is JSON but we don't enforce schema here 

3742 max_tokens=max_output_tokens_for(model_id), 

3743 story_id=story.id, 

3744 app=story.app, 

3745 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

3746 db_path=db, 

3747 ) 

3748 result = _parse_reviewer_result(result_any) 

3749 

3750 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

3751 

3752 # Post inline comments (real-run only). 

3753 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

3754 try: 

3755 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

3756 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

3757 for c in result.get("comments_to_post") or []: 

3758 # Inline comment requires commit_sha, path, position; we 

3759 # use a simpler issue comment in Phase 2 as fallback. 

3760 pr.create_issue_comment( 

3761 f"**Reviewer note** ({c.get('file')}:{c.get('line')}):\n\n{c.get('body')}" 

3762 ) 

3763 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3764 pass 

3765 

3766 verdict = result.get("verdict", "request_changes") 

3767 score = float(result.get("test_quality_score", 0.0)) 

3768 

3769 # Loop-4 programmatic slop gate. The dev now writes its own tests, so a 

3770 # deterministic scan of the changed test files is the backstop against the 

3771 # classic failure mode (tautological / assert-True / mock-only tests that 

3772 # pass before any real implementation). This runs BEFORE the approve check 

3773 # and can veto an LLM "approve": slop is a hard block routed back to dev. 

3774 # Runs on every real review (dry_run unit tests pass dry_run=True, and the 

3775 # helper returns [] defensively when there is no worktree to scan). 

3776 if not dry_run: 

3777 slop_findings = _slop_findings_for_story(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

3778 if slop_findings: 

3779 verdict = "request_changes" 

3780 score = min(score, 0.3) 

3781 result["verdict"] = "request_changes" 

3782 result["test_quality_score"] = score 

3783 result.setdefault("test_quality_findings", []) 

3784 result["test_quality_findings"].extend(slop_findings) 

3785 result["slop_detector_findings"] = slop_findings 

3786 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

3787 

3788 # Finality drift clamp. At cycle 3+, blocking findings that share NO file 

3789 # location with the previous cycle's findings AND are not marked 

3790 # ``regression: true`` violate the persona's finality rule (new objections 

3791 # to code that was already in front of the reviewer). Rotating fresh 

3792 # objections each cycle is exactly how benchmark t3/t8 burned 6 cycles 

3793 # without shipping. Clamp such findings to ``low`` (non-blocking); if 

3794 # nothing blocking remains and the score clears the bar, the verdict 

3795 # flips to approve. Slop-detector findings are never clamped (they are 

3796 # deterministic, not reviewer drift). 

3797 if verdict != "approve" and story.reviewer_cycles >= 2: 

3798 try: 

3799 history = json.loads(story.reviewer_history_json or "[]") 

3800 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

3801 history = [] 

3802 prev = history[-1] if history else None 

3803 if prev: 

3804 prev_locs = { 

3805 _finding_location_file(f) 

3806 for f in (prev.get("findings") or []) + (prev.get("test_quality_findings") or []) 

3807 } - {""} 

3808 slop_ids = {id(f) for f in (result.get("slop_detector_findings") or [])} 

3809 clamped: list[dict[str, Any]] = [] 

3810 for f in result.get("findings") or []: 

3811 if not isinstance(f, dict) or id(f) in slop_ids: 

3812 continue 

3813 blocking = f.get("severity") in ("medium", "high") 

3814 is_regression = bool(f.get("regression")) 

3815 known_site = _finding_location_file(f) in prev_locs 

3816 if blocking and not is_regression and not known_site: 

3817 f["severity"] = "low" 

3818 f["finality_clamped"] = True 

3819 clamped.append(f) 

3820 if clamped: 

3821 still_blocking = any( 

3822 isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("severity") in ("medium", "high") 

3823 for f in result.get("findings") or [] 

3824 ) or bool(result.get("slop_detector_findings")) 

3825 log_story_event( 

3826 story.id, 

3827 "reviewer_finality_clamped", 

3828 { 

3829 "cycle": story.reviewer_cycles + 1, 

3830 "clamped": [ 

3831 {"location": f.get("location"), "what": (f.get("what") or "")[:160]} 

3832 for f in clamped 

3833 ], 

3834 "approved_after_clamp": not still_blocking and score >= 0.7, 

3835 }, 

3836 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3837 slug_hint=story.slug, 

3838 ) 

3839 if not still_blocking and score >= 0.7: 

3840 verdict = "approve" 

3841 result["verdict"] = "approve" 

3842 result["finality_clamp_applied"] = True 

3843 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

3844 

3845 if verdict == "approve" and score >= 0.7: 

3846 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEWER_APPROVE).value 

3847 else: 

3848 # Convergence guard based on finding STABILITY. A cycle whose findings 

3849 # differ from the last is progress; only identical findings repeating 

3850 # _MAX_REVIEW_STUCK times is true churn. A hard backstop on total cycles 

3851 # prevents a slowly-mutating loop from running unbounded. 

3852 story.reviewer_cycles += 1 

3853 sig = _findings_signature(result) 

3854 from factory.chain.event_log import read_story_events 

3855 

3856 consecutive_same = 1 # this cycle 

3857 for e in reversed( 

3858 read_story_events( 

3859 story.id, software_factory_root=software_factory_root, slug_hint=story.slug 

3860 ) 

3861 ): 

3862 if e.get("event") != "reviewer_cycle": 

3863 continue 

3864 if e.get("sig") == sig: 

3865 consecutive_same += 1 

3866 else: 

3867 break 

3868 stuck = consecutive_same >= _MAX_REVIEW_STUCK 

3869 # Non-improving-score early exit. Review cycles are supposed to buy 

3870 # convergence; a score that fails to IMPROVE between consecutive 

3871 # rejecting cycles means more cycles are buying expensive wrong 

3872 # answers (2026-07-31 benchmark trajectories were flat/declining: 

3873 # 0.45→0.35→0.40). Compare against the PREVIOUS cycle's recorded 

3874 # score (reviewer_history_json — this cycle is appended later), and 

3875 # fire strictly BELOW the _MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES hard cap (at cycle 2, cap 

3876 # 3) or the guard would be unreachable. This lives inside the 

3877 # non-approve branch, so it can only ever route to the blocked sink — 

3878 # NEVER to approved. 

3879 prev_score: float | None = None 

3880 try: 

3881 _hist = json.loads(story.reviewer_history_json or "[]") 

3882 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): 

3883 _hist = [] 

3884 if _hist and isinstance(_hist[-1], dict): 

3885 _raw_prev = _hist[-1].get("score") 

3886 if isinstance(_raw_prev, (int, float)): 

3887 prev_score = float(_raw_prev) 

3888 non_improving = ( 

3889 story.reviewer_cycles >= 2 and prev_score is not None and score <= prev_score 

3890 ) 

3891 log_story_event( 

3892 story.id, 

3893 "reviewer_cycle", 

3894 { 

3895 "sig": sig, 

3896 "cycle": story.reviewer_cycles, 

3897 "consecutive_same": consecutive_same, 

3898 "score": score, 

3899 "prev_score": prev_score, 

3900 "non_improving": non_improving, 

3901 }, 

3902 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3903 slug_hint=story.slug, 

3904 ) 

3905 # Mirror the per-story event into the replayable chain_step stream — 

3906 # same reason as the dev-retry emit above: review cycles turn inside a 

3907 # single handler invocation and never reached ``emit_chain_step``. 

3908 # Emitted after the stability computation so the row carries the two 

3909 # facts that explain the cycle (``consecutive_same``, ``stuck``), not 

3910 # merely that one happened. 

3911 emit_chain_step( 

3912 story, 

3913 handler="review", 

3914 from_state=story.state, 

3915 to_state=story.state, 

3916 outcome="review_cycle", 

3917 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

3918 extra={ 

3919 "retry_attempt": story.reviewer_cycles, 

3920 "retry_cap": _MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES, 

3921 "consecutive_same": consecutive_same, 

3922 "stuck_cap": _MAX_REVIEW_STUCK, 

3923 "stuck": stuck, 

3924 "score": score, 

3925 "prev_score": prev_score, 

3926 "non_improving": non_improving, 

3927 }, 

3928 ) 

3929 if stuck or non_improving or story.reviewer_cycles >= _MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES: 

3930 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT).value 

3931 if stuck: 

3932 reason = f"same findings repeated {consecutive_same}x (stuck)" 

3933 elif non_improving: 

3934 reason = ( 

3935 f"review score did not improve between consecutive cycles " 

3936 f"({prev_score} -> {score})" 

3937 ) 

3938 else: 

3939 reason = f"hit hard cap of {_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES} cycles" 

3940 story.error = ( 

3941 f"Review did not converge ({reason}); routed to " 

3942 f"{StoryState.BLOCKED_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT.value} for human review." 

3943 ) 

3944 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

3945 try: 

3946 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

3947 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

3948 pr.add_to_labels("review-nonconvergent") 

3949 pr.create_issue_comment( 

3950 f"⚠️ Convergence guard: this PR has been through " 

3951 f"{story.reviewer_cycles} reviewer cycles without " 

3952 f"approval (max {_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES}). The dev↔reviewer " 

3953 f"loop is not converging; routing to human review " 

3954 f"instead of dispatching dev again." 

3955 ) 

3956 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3957 pass 

3958 else: 

3959 # Loop-4: dev owns BOTH code and tests, so every actionable 

3960 # rejection — code defects AND test-quality/slop findings — routes 

3961 # back to dev. There is no longer a separate test author to route a 

3962 # test-quality finding to. dev's prompt receives both ``findings`` 

3963 # and ``test_quality_findings`` (see handle_dev's reviewer_findings 

3964 # plumbing), so it knows what to fix in code and in tests. 

3965 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEWER_REQUEST_CHANGES).value 

3966 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

3967 try: 

3968 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

3969 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

3970 pr.add_to_labels("needs-changes") 

3971 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

3972 pass 

3973 

3974 # Record this cycle in the review history (post-clamp, so the next 

3975 # cycle's reviewer prompt and drift clamp see what was ACTUALLY ruled). 

3976 _append_reviewer_history(story, result) 

3977 persist_story(story, db) 

3978 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result) 

3979 

3980 

3981# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

3982# tech_writer 

3983# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

3984 

3985# S3 (019 fail-silent audit): a JSON parse failure used to persist 

3986# ``{"context_updates": [], "rationale": "tech_writer JSON parse failed"}`` — 

3987# a result the ``docs-current`` REQUIRED gate can never satisfy (that string 

3988# matches none of the gate's legacy literal phrases), permanently stranding 

3989# the story. Retry the model call INLINE (same handler invocation, no extra 

3990# tick) before giving up. Strictly below the hard cap of 3 chain-level 

3991# retries used elsewhere (``_MAX_DEV_RETRIES`` / ``_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES``). 

3992_MAX_TECH_WRITER_PARSE_RETRIES = 2 

3993 

3994 

3995def _dry_run_tech_writer(story: StoryRecord) -> dict[str, Any]: 

3996 """Deterministic tech_writer result for dry-run mode.""" 

3997 return { 

3998 "context_updates": [ 

3999 { 

4000 "path": f"context/modules/{story.scope}.md", 

4001 "action": "rewrite", 

4002 "content": ( 

4003 f"# {story.scope} module\n\nUpdated to reflect story `{story.slug}`.\n" 

4004 ), 

4005 } 

4006 ], 

4007 "rationale": "Dry-run tech_writer: minimal context refresh.", 

4008 } 

4009 

4010 

4011def handle_tech_writer( 

4012 story: StoryRecord, 

4013 app_config: AppConfig, 

4014 software_factory_root: Path, 

4015 *, 

4016 dry_run: bool = False, 

4017 db_path: Path | None = None, 

4018 fixture: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

4019) -> HandlerResult: 

4020 """Run the Tech-Writer persona; apply context updates to the app repo.""" 

4021 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

4022 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_TECH_WRITER_STARTED).value 

4023 persist_story(story, db) 

4024 

4025 if fixture is not None: 

4026 result = fixture 

4027 elif dry_run: 

4028 result = _dry_run_tech_writer(story) 

4029 else: 

4030 from factory.app_config import resolve_app_repo_path 

4031 from factory.context.loader import compose_context_prelude 

4032 from factory.directions.parser import get_direction_chain 

4033 from factory.runner import text_run 

4034 

4035 persona = "tech_writer" 

4036 persona_prompt = _read_persona_prompt(persona) 

4037 direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

4038 chain = ( 

4039 get_direction_chain(direction, software_factory_root) if direction is not None else None 

4040 ) 

4041 prelude = compose_context_prelude( 

4042 persona=persona, 

4043 app_repo_path=resolve_app_repo_path(app_config, software_factory_root), 

4044 task_scope=story.scope, 

4045 direction_chain=chain, 

4046 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4047 ) 

4048 story_content = _read_story_file_content(story, software_factory_root) 

4049 # FAIL-CLOSED diff precondition, same rationale as handle_review: a 

4050 # tech_writer that cannot see the diff would refresh context docs 

4051 # blind. An EMPTY diff is equally disqualifying HERE (unlike at 

4052 # review time, where it can mean "dev forgot to commit — retry"): 

4053 # tech_writer only runs after the reviewer approved a NON-empty diff, 

4054 # so an empty diff now means the worktree substrate changed under the 

4055 # chain (GC'd/rebuilt) — an infra fault, not a content verdict. 

4056 try: 

4057 pr_diff = _fetch_pr_diff_for_review(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

4058 except ReviewDiffUnavailableError as exc: 

4059 return _block_on_unavailable_diff( 

4060 story, 

4061 app_config, 

4062 software_factory_root, 

4063 persona="tech_writer", 

4064 reason=exc.reason, 

4065 db=db, 

4066 ) 

4067 if not pr_diff.strip(): 

4068 return _block_on_unavailable_diff( 

4069 story, 

4070 app_config, 

4071 software_factory_root, 

4072 persona="tech_writer", 

4073 reason=( 

4074 "diff is empty at tech_writer time, but the reviewer " 

4075 "approved a non-empty diff — the worktree no longer " 

4076 "matches what was reviewed" 

4077 ), 

4078 db=db, 

4079 ) 

4080 full_prompt = ( 

4081 f"{persona_prompt.rstrip()}\n\n" 

4082 "---\n\n" 

4083 "## Context\n\n" 

4084 f"{prelude.rstrip()}\n\n" 

4085 "## Story\n\n" 

4086 f"{story_content}\n\n" 

4087 "## PR diff\n\n" 

4088 f"{pr_diff}\n\n" 

4089 "Return the JSON object. No prose outside the JSON." 

4090 ) 

4091 _assert_no_broken_prompt_markers(full_prompt, where="handle_tech_writer") 

4092 model_id = route(persona) 

4093 parse_error: str | None = None 

4094 parsed: dict[str, Any] | None = None 

4095 for attempt in range(1, _MAX_TECH_WRITER_PARSE_RETRIES + 1): 

4096 result_any = text_run( 

4097 persona=persona, 

4098 prompt=full_prompt, 

4099 model_id=model_id, 

4100 schema=None, 

4101 # Per-model cap, NOT a small constant: routes.yaml documents 

4102 # tech_writer as "the largest JSON of any text persona", and a 

4103 # 2048 start burned all 4 of the runner's doubling retries 

4104 # (2048+4096+8192+16384 = story 177's exact tokens_out) before 

4105 # returning a still-truncated body as success. 

4106 max_tokens=max_output_tokens_for(model_id), 

4107 story_id=story.id, 

4108 app=story.app, 

4109 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

4110 db_path=db, 

4111 ) 

4112 # Fence-strip + shape-check, NOT the reviewer's brace-slice — see 

4113 # _parse_tech_writer_result for why leniency here is a false-green 

4114 # channel (story 177 attempt 1: a fully valid fenced object was 

4115 # rejected by the old bare json.loads; that case parses now). 

4116 candidate = _parse_tech_writer_result(result_any) 

4117 if isinstance(candidate, dict): 

4118 parsed = candidate 

4119 parse_error = None 

4120 break 

4121 parse_error = "tech_writer JSON parse failed" 

4122 log_story_event( 

4123 story.id, 

4124 "tech_writer_parse_retry", 

4125 {"attempt": attempt, "cap": _MAX_TECH_WRITER_PARSE_RETRIES}, 

4126 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4127 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4128 ) 

4129 if parsed is None: 

4130 # Exhausted retries. NEVER persist a result the docs-current gate 

4131 # can't satisfy — route to the same fail-closed blocked sink the 

4132 # diff-precondition checks above use, so a human sees this 

4133 # instead of a permanently-missing required label. 

4134 return _block_on_unavailable_diff( 

4135 story, 

4136 app_config, 

4137 software_factory_root, 

4138 persona="tech_writer", 

4139 reason=( 

4140 f"{parse_error} after {_MAX_TECH_WRITER_PARSE_RETRIES} attempts " 

4141 "(model never returned a parseable JSON object)" 

4142 ), 

4143 db=db, 

4144 ) 

4145 result = parsed 

4146 

4147 story.tech_writer_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

4148 

4149 # Apply context_updates to the app repo. In dry-run we use the factory's 

4150 # apps/<app>/ as a stand-in — but apply_context_updates would write files 

4151 # there. To keep dry-run truly dry (NO writes outside the factory state), 

4152 # we DO NOT call apply_context_updates in dry-run. Instead we record the 

4153 # updates that WOULD have been applied. 

4154 # 

4155 # IMPORTANT: We MUST do the write BEFORE advancing state to TECH_WRITER_DONE 

4156 # so a failed apply leaves the chain in a recoverable place. If the writer 

4157 # produced a forbidden path (or any other write failure), we transition to 

4158 # REVIEWER_REQUESTED_CHANGES so the chain routes back through the dev loop 

4159 # instead of pretending docs are current. 

4160 if not dry_run: 

4161 updates_raw = result.get("context_updates") or [] 

4162 updates = [ 

4163 ContextUpdate( 

4164 path=u["path"], action=u.get("action", "rewrite"), content=u.get("content", "") 

4165 ) 

4166 for u in updates_raw 

4167 ] 

4168 # Context lives in the per-story worktree so concurrent stories 

4169 # don't collide. Each worktree shares ``.git`` with the source 

4170 # repo so refs and history stay consistent. 

4171 repo_path = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

4172 try: 

4173 apply_context_updates(updates, repo_path) 

4174 except Exception as exc: 

4175 # Bounce back through reviewer_requested_changes: tech_writer 

4176 # produced an invalid context update; either the writer is 

4177 # confused (rare) or it tried to write to a forbidden path. The 

4178 # next dev cycle gets a clean shot. 

4179 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_REVIEWER_REQUEST_CHANGES).value 

4180 story.error = f"context update failed: {exc}" 

4181 persist_story(story, db) 

4182 return HandlerResult( 

4183 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

4184 payload=result, 

4185 error=story.error, 

4186 ) 

4187 

4188 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_TECH_WRITER_DONE).value 

4189 persist_story(story, db) 

4190 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result) 

4191 

4192 

4193# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4194# docs_sm — lightweight story-prep for the docs chain 

4195# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4196 

4197 

4198def _dry_run_docs_sm(story: StoryRecord) -> dict[str, Any]: 

4199 """Deterministic docs-SM result for dry-run mode. 

4200 

4201 Returns the minimum the downstream Onboarder handler needs: a story-file 

4202 body sketch and the list of canonical paths the Onboarder should produce. 

4203 The full BMAD story envelope isn't required — the docs path skips the 

4204 Test-Designer entirely. 

4205 """ 

4206 return { 

4207 "story_file_body": ( 

4208 f"# {story.title}\n\n" 

4209 f"## Goal\n\nProduce canonical documentation in the app repo.\n\n" 

4210 f"## Canonical paths\n\n" 

4211 f"- `context/project.md`\n" 

4212 f"- `context/current-state.md`\n" 

4213 f"- `context/navigation.md`\n" 

4214 f"- `context/glossary.md`\n" 

4215 f"- `context/architecture-diagrams.md`\n" 

4216 f"- `context/sprint-status.yaml`\n" 

4217 f"- `context/modules/<name>.md` per discovered module\n" 

4218 ), 

4219 "canonical_paths": [ 

4220 "context/project.md", 

4221 "context/current-state.md", 

4222 "context/navigation.md", 

4223 "context/glossary.md", 

4224 "context/architecture-diagrams.md", 

4225 "context/sprint-status.yaml", 

4226 ], 

4227 } 

4228 

4229 

4230def handle_docs_sm( 

4231 story: StoryRecord, 

4232 app_config: AppConfig, 

4233 software_factory_root: Path, 

4234 *, 

4235 dry_run: bool = False, 

4236 db_path: Path | None = None, 

4237) -> HandlerResult: 

4238 """Lightweight SM specialized for the docs chain. 

4239 

4240 Produces a story file under ``apps/<app>/stories/<issue>-<slug>.md`` that 

4241 enumerates which canonical paths the Onboarder should produce. NOT a full 

4242 BMAD story — the docs path skips test_design/test_impl/dev entirely. 

4243 

4244 In ``dry_run``, emits a deterministic fixture. In real-run, calls 

4245 ``text_run("sm", ...)`` with a docs-flavored prompt. The story file write 

4246 happens BEFORE advancing state so a crash mid-write leaves the chain 

4247 recoverable. 

4248 """ 

4249 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

4250 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_SM_STARTED).value 

4251 persist_story(story, db) 

4252 

4253 if dry_run: 

4254 result = _dry_run_docs_sm(story) 

4255 else: 

4256 # Real-run: text_run on a docs-flavored prompt. We re-use the SM 

4257 # persona file but prefix the prompt with a directive to emit a 

4258 # minimal docs story (skip test plans, dev notes, etc.). The SM prompt 

4259 # already knows about canonical paths from CANONICAL_CONTEXT_PATHS. 

4260 from factory.runner import text_run 

4261 

4262 persona_prompt = _read_persona_prompt("sm") 

4263 direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

4264 direction_title = direction.title if direction else story.title 

4265 direction_why = (direction.why if direction else "") or "" 

4266 

4267 docs_directive = ( 

4268 "You are running in DOCS-CHAIN mode for this story. The story's " 

4269 "deliverable is canonical documentation under the app's ``context/`` " 

4270 "tree — NO executable code, NO test plans, NO dev notes. Produce a " 

4271 "minimal story body listing the canonical paths the Onboarder must " 

4272 "write and the directive's acceptance criteria verbatim. Output " 

4273 "JSON ONLY with this shape:\n" 

4274 ' {"story_file_body": "<markdown body>", ' 

4275 '"canonical_paths": ["context/...", "context/..."]}' 

4276 ) 

4277 prompt = ( 

4278 f"{docs_directive}\n\n---\n\n" 

4279 f"{persona_prompt.rstrip()}\n\n---\n\n" 

4280 f"## Direction\n\n# {direction_title}\n\n{direction_why}\n" 

4281 ) 

4282 schema = { 

4283 "type": "object", 

4284 "properties": { 

4285 "story_file_body": {"type": "string"}, 

4286 "canonical_paths": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}, 

4287 }, 

4288 "required": ["story_file_body", "canonical_paths"], 

4289 } 

4290 result_any = text_run( 

4291 persona="sm", 

4292 prompt=prompt, 

4293 model_id=route("sm"), 

4294 schema=schema, 

4295 max_tokens=2048, 

4296 db_path=db, 

4297 story_id=story.id, 

4298 app=story.app, 

4299 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

4300 ) 

4301 result = result_any if isinstance(result_any, dict) else _dry_run_docs_sm(story) 

4302 

4303 # Persist the SM JSON before any filesystem write so a crash leaves the 

4304 # DB consistent with what the next handler will see. 

4305 story.sm_result_json = json.dumps(result) 

4306 

4307 # Write the story file under apps/<app>/stories/<issue>-<slug>.md. 

4308 story_path_abs = software_factory_root / "apps" / story.app / story.story_file_path 

4309 story_path_abs.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) 

4310 story_path_abs.write_text(result.get("story_file_body", "") + "\n", encoding="utf-8") 

4311 

4312 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_SM_DONE).value 

4313 persist_story(story, db) 

4314 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=result) 

4315 

4316 

4317# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4318# docs_onboarder — single-shot sandbox run that writes the canonical files 

4319# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4320 

4321 

4322def _dry_run_docs_onboarder(story: StoryRecord) -> dict[str, Any]: 

4323 """Dry-run fixture: pretend the Onboarder wrote a plausible canonical set.""" 

4324 return { 

4325 "files_changed": [ 

4326 "context/project.md", 

4327 "context/current-state.md", 

4328 "context/navigation.md", 

4329 "context/glossary.md", 

4330 "context/architecture-diagrams.md", 

4331 "context/sprint-status.yaml", 

4332 ], 

4333 "summary": "Dry-run docs_onboarder: canonical files would be produced.", 

4334 } 

4335 

4336 

4337def handle_docs_onboarder( 

4338 story: StoryRecord, 

4339 app_config: AppConfig, 

4340 software_factory_root: Path, 

4341 *, 

4342 dry_run: bool = False, 

4343 db_path: Path | None = None, 

4344) -> HandlerResult: 

4345 """Run the Onboarder persona via sandbox_run. 

4346 

4347 The Onboarder reads the app repo, infers the project + module map, and 

4348 writes the canonical context set on the feature branch. The single 

4349 sandbox pass replaces the entire test_impl/dev loop the TDD chain would 

4350 have driven. 

4351 

4352 Uses ``resolve_app_repo_path`` for the sandbox working directory (Bug A 

4353 fix) and ``ensure_feature_branch`` for the per-story branch (Fix 1). 

4354 Commits produced by the sandbox land on the feature branch in the real 

4355 app repo. 

4356 """ 

4357 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

4358 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ONBOARDER_STARTED).value 

4359 persist_story(story, db) 

4360 

4361 if dry_run: 

4362 payload = _dry_run_docs_onboarder(story) 

4363 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ONBOARDER_DONE).value 

4364 story.tech_writer_result_json = json.dumps( 

4365 { 

4366 "context_updates": [ 

4367 {"path": p, "action": "rewrite", "content": ""} 

4368 for p in payload["files_changed"] 

4369 ] 

4370 } 

4371 ) 

4372 persist_story(story, db) 

4373 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload) 

4374 

4375 from factory.chain.branch import feature_branch_name 

4376 from factory.runner import LLMConfig, sandbox_run 

4377 

4378 target_repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

4379 branch = feature_branch_name(story.github_issue_number, story.slug) 

4380 story.github_branch = branch 

4381 persist_story(story, db) 

4382 

4383 story_file_path_obj = software_factory_root / "apps" / story.app / story.story_file_path 

4384 llm = LLMConfig(model=route("onboarder")) 

4385 import asyncio 

4386 

4387 run_res = asyncio.run( 

4388 sandbox_run( 

4389 persona="onboarder", 

4390 story_path=story_file_path_obj, 

4391 repo_path=target_repo, 

4392 llm_config=llm, 

4393 dry_run=False, 

4394 story_id=story.id, 

4395 app=story.app, 

4396 direction_id=story.direction_id, 

4397 ) 

4398 ) 

4399 

4400 # Onboarder writes files via SDK tool calls. The factory then explicitly 

4401 # commits whatever's left untracked on the feature branch — the SDK 

4402 # doesn't always commit cleanly across the full set. 

4403 from factory.chain.branch import _run_git 

4404 

4405 try: 

4406 _run_git(target_repo, "add", "-A") 

4407 # Only commit if there's anything to commit; an empty commit would be 

4408 # a chain bug (Onboarder produced nothing) and we want to surface it. 

4409 status = _run_git(target_repo, "status", "--porcelain").stdout.strip() 

4410 if status: 

4411 _run_git( 

4412 target_repo, 

4413 "commit", 

4414 "-m", 

4415 f"docs(context): bootstrap canonical context for {story.app}\n\n" 

4416 f"Produced by Onboarder for story {story.id} ({story.slug}).", 

4417 ) 

4418 else: 

4419 # Nothing produced — Onboarder failed silently. Surface it. 

4420 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ONBOARDER_FAILED).value 

4421 story.error = "onboarder produced no files" 

4422 persist_story(story, db) 

4423 return HandlerResult( 

4424 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

4425 payload={"files_changed": [], "summary": run_res.summary[-1000:]}, 

4426 error=story.error, 

4427 ) 

4428 except Exception as exc: 

4429 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ONBOARDER_FAILED).value 

4430 story.error = f"docs_onboarder commit failed: {exc}" 

4431 persist_story(story, db) 

4432 return HandlerResult( 

4433 next_state=StoryState(story.state), 

4434 payload={"files_changed": run_res.files_changed, "summary": str(exc)}, 

4435 error=story.error, 

4436 ) 

4437 

4438 # Capture the diff between the feature branch and base for the enforcer. 

4439 diff_proc = _run_git( 

4440 target_repo, 

4441 "diff", 

4442 "--name-only", 

4443 f"{app_config.default_branch or 'main'}..HEAD", 

4444 ) 

4445 diff_files = [line.strip() for line in diff_proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()] 

4446 

4447 # Persist the file list under tech_writer_result_json so the existing 

4448 # ``handle_docs_enforcer`` can pick it up unchanged — the field name is 

4449 # legacy; semantically it's "list of files this story touched". 

4450 story.tech_writer_result_json = json.dumps( 

4451 {"context_updates": [{"path": p, "action": "rewrite", "content": ""} for p in diff_files]} 

4452 ) 

4453 

4454 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ONBOARDER_DONE).value 

4455 persist_story(story, db) 

4456 payload = { 

4457 "files_changed": diff_files, 

4458 "summary": run_res.summary[-2000:], 

4459 "tokens_in": run_res.tokens_in, 

4460 "tokens_out": run_res.tokens_out, 

4461 "cost_usd": run_res.cost_usd, 

4462 } 

4463 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload) 

4464 

4465 

4466# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4467# docs_enforcer 

4468# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 

4469 

4470# S4 (019 fail-silent audit): cap on consecutive ``gh pr create`` failures 

4471# before parking the story at BLOCKED_DEPLOY_FAILED instead of retrying 

4472# forever. Strictly below the hard cap of 3 used elsewhere 

4473# (``_MAX_DEV_RETRIES`` / ``_MAX_REVIEW_CYCLES``). 

4474_MAX_PR_CREATE_RETRIES = 2 

4475 

4476# Pre-PR lint bounce: how many times ONE story may be sent back to dev because 

4477# ruff is still red on its own changed .py files. Exactly one. The second red 

4478# opens the PR anyway and lets GitHub CI + the existing ci-fix / identical- 

4479# signature park be the backstop they already are. A repeating bounce would be 

4480# a new uncapped loop, which the guardrails forbid — and a dev that cannot 

4481# clear a concise ruff report it was handed verbatim will not clear it on 

4482# attempt three either. 

4483_MAX_LINT_BOUNCES = 1 

4484 

4485 

4486def _lint_bounces_so_far(story: StoryRecord, software_factory_root: Path) -> int: 

4487 """How many pre-PR lint bounces this story has already taken. 

4488 

4489 Derived from the story's OWN event stream (``lint_bounce`` records) rather 

4490 than a new counter column — the ``_gate_block_history`` precedent in 

4491 ``auto_merge``. Three reasons this is the cheapest option that actually 

4492 works: 

4493 

4494 * it survives a process restart for free (the events are on disk, hash- 

4495 chained, and already written for audit anyway); 

4496 * it needs no schema change and no migration of live rows; 

4497 * every field that LOOKED reusable is wrong. ``dev_retries`` / 

4498 ``reviewer_cycles`` are reset by the bounce itself (and by the CI-fix 

4499 re-dispatch); ``total_attempts`` is reset by the orchestrator's 

4500 advance-decay on forward progress; ``reviewer_result_json`` and 

4501 ``tech_writer_result_json`` are BOTH overwritten on the way back round 

4502 the loop the bounce sends the story on. A flag in any of them would be 

4503 erased before it was ever read. 

4504 

4505 Scoped after the most recent ``story_resumed`` for the same reason 

4506 ``_gate_block_history`` is: an operator resume is a deliberate "try this 

4507 again", and must not be silently overruled by history. 

4508 

4509 FAIL DIRECTION: an unreadable / unidentifiable log returns 

4510 ``_MAX_LINT_BOUNCES`` — "cap already reached", so the PR opens. This counter 

4511 is the ONLY thing bounding the bounce loop, and a read that fails 

4512 repeatedly (unreadable log, a story with no id, a wiped ``state/logs``) 

4513 would otherwise report 0 every single time and bounce the story forever. 

4514 Fail-safe HERE means "do not bounce": the un-bounced branch still meets 

4515 GitHub CI, which is the authoritative lint gate. An unbounded loop has no 

4516 such backstop. 

4517 """ 

4518 from factory.chain.event_log import read_story_events 

4519 

4520 if story.id is None: 

4521 # No id → no log path → nothing can ever be counted. Never bounce. 

4522 return _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES 

4523 try: 

4524 events = read_story_events( 

4525 story.id, software_factory_root=software_factory_root, slug_hint=story.slug or "" 

4526 ) 

4527 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - see FAIL DIRECTION above 

4528 _logger.warning( 

4529 "story %s: lint-bounce history unreadable; treating the cap as reached " 

4530 "so the bounce loop stays bounded", 

4531 story.id, 

4532 ) 

4533 return _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES 

4534 resume_idx = -1 

4535 for i, e in enumerate(events): 

4536 if e.get("event") == "story_resumed": 

4537 resume_idx = i 

4538 return sum(1 for e in events[resume_idx + 1 :] if e.get("event") == "lint_bounce") 

4539 

4540 

4541# Attempt headroom a story must still have before it is allowed to spend a 

4542# bounce. One bounce costs a dev dispatch + a review + a tech_writer + this 

4543# handler, so a story with less headroom than that would be sent round a loop it 

4544# cannot finish and would die at BLOCKED_BUDGET_EXCEEDED — with its branch 

4545# unpushed and no PR at all, which is strictly worse than the lint-red PR the 

4546# bounce was trying to avoid. 

4547_LINT_BOUNCE_ATTEMPT_HEADROOM = 4 

4548 

4549 

4550def _lint_bounce_budget_headroom( 

4551 story: StoryRecord, software_factory_root: Path 

4552) -> tuple[bool, int | None]: 

4553 """``(has enough attempt headroom for a bounce, remaining attempts)``. 

4554 

4555 Fails OPEN (``True``) when the caps can't be read or aren't configured: 

4556 an unreadable settings file must not silently disable the lint bounce, and 

4557 the bounce is capped at 1 either way. 

4558 """ 

4559 try: 

4560 from factory.settings.loader import load_settings as _load_settings 

4561 

4562 caps = _load_settings(software_factory_root).caps 

4563 per_story_attempts = int(getattr(caps, "per_story_attempts", 0) or 0) 

4564 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - unreadable settings must not disable the bounce 

4565 return True, None 

4566 if per_story_attempts <= 0: 

4567 return True, None 

4568 remaining = per_story_attempts - int(story.total_attempts or 0) 

4569 return remaining >= _LINT_BOUNCE_ATTEMPT_HEADROOM, remaining 

4570 

4571 

4572def _residual_lint_for_story( 

4573 story: StoryRecord, app_config: AppConfig, software_factory_root: Path 

4574) -> str | None: 

4575 """Autoformat the story's branch, then report what ruff still flags. 

4576 

4577 Autoformat runs FIRST and here (not only inside ``_open_pr_for_story``) so 

4578 the bounce is never spent on a nit the conservative autoformat fixes for 

4579 free — an I001 import-sort or a missing trailing newline must not cost a 

4580 whole dev cycle. It is idempotent, so the second call inside 

4581 ``_open_pr_for_story`` finds nothing to do and commits nothing. 

4582 

4583 Fail-open on any worktree-resolution problem: see 

4584 ``_residual_changed_py_lint``. 

4585 """ 

4586 try: 

4587 target_repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

4588 except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - no worktree → CI stays the backstop 

4589 _logger.warning("pre-PR lint check skipped (no worktree, fail-open): %s", exc) 

4590 return None 

4591 base = app_config.default_branch or "main" 

4592 _autoformat_changed_py_before_pr(target_repo, base, app_config) 

4593 return _residual_changed_py_lint(target_repo, base, app_config) 

4594 

4595 

4596def _push_fix_to_existing_pr( 

4597 story: StoryRecord, app_config: AppConfig, software_factory_root: Path 

4598) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: 

4599 """Push a post-PR fix cycle's new commits so the PR head actually MOVES. 

4600 

4601 Returns ``(pushed, error_reason)``. 

4602 

4603 THE BUG THIS CLOSES (sacrifice story 183, 2026-08-09 — live evidence, not 

4604 inference). The chain had exactly ONE push site for a story's work: 

4605 ``_open_pr_for_story``, which ``handle_docs_enforcer`` calls only under 

4606 ``story.github_pr_number is None``. The only other push in the codebase is 

4607 the dev-exhausted WIP-preservation path. So once a PR existed, NOTHING could 

4608 ever push again: 

4609 

4610 * CI goes red on PR #N; 

4611 * ``auto_merge._handle_ci_failure`` re-dispatches the story to dev with 

4612 the CI digest as a reviewer finding; 

4613 * dev DOES fix it — story 183's ``response_bodies.ndjson`` at 21:45:07 

4614 shows the F401s and the E712 corrected — and 

4615 ``_commit_green_dev_work`` commits it LOCALLY; 

4616 * the story walks back review → tech_writer → docs_enforcer, whose PR 

4617 block is skipped because ``github_pr_number`` is set; 

4618 * ``git.ndjson`` records exactly ONE push for the whole story: the 

4619 original. The remote head never moved, so GitHub never re-ran CI; 

4620 * the next evaluation re-reads the SAME stale head sha, sees the identical 

4621 failure signature, and terminally parks the story. 

4622 

4623 That silently swallowed EVERY post-PR fix, not just lint ones — the ci-fix 

4624 loop was writing fixes to a branch nobody shipped. The lint bounce added in 

4625 the previous commit only ever helped BEFORE a PR exists; this is the other 

4626 half. 

4627 

4628 Only pushes when the local branch is genuinely AHEAD of its remote. A cycle 

4629 that produced no new commit must NOT be given a fresh head sha it did not 

4630 earn: the identical-signature park is the correct outcome for a dev that 

4631 truly changed nothing, and manufacturing a new sha would defeat the one 

4632 guard that stops that loop. 

4633 

4634 Same ``--force-with-lease`` rationale as ``_open_pr_for_story``: story 

4635 branches are factory-owned and single-writer, origin may hold stale commits 

4636 from abandoned earlier attempts, and the lease still aborts if origin moved 

4637 unexpectedly since our fetch. 

4638 

4639 NOTE (deliberate asymmetry): the pre-push autoformat that 

4640 ``_open_pr_for_story`` runs is NOT run here. A post-PR cycle's commits come 

4641 from dev fixing concrete findings, and silently rewriting them on the way to 

4642 a PR whose CI is already contested would confuse the very signal being 

4643 adjudicated. If a fix cycle needs formatting help, that belongs in the dev 

4644 loop, where the findings already say so. 

4645 """ 

4646 import subprocess 

4647 

4648 branch = story.github_branch 

4649 if not branch: 

4650 return False, "no branch recorded on the story" 

4651 try: 

4652 target_repo = _writing_worktree(app_config, software_factory_root, story) 

4653 except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 

4654 return False, f"worktree unavailable: {exc}" 

4655 

4656 def _git(args: list[str], timeout: int = 120) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] | None: 

4657 try: 

4658 return subprocess.run( 

4659 ["git", *args], 

4660 cwd=str(target_repo), 

4661 capture_output=True, 

4662 text=True, 

4663 errors="replace", 

4664 check=False, 

4665 timeout=timeout, 

4666 ) 

4667 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError): 

4668 return None 

4669 

4670 # Refresh + PRUNE remote-tracking refs first: the ahead-check below reads 

4671 # ``origin/<branch>``, and --force-with-lease rejects with "stale info" 

4672 # against a tracking ref that was never updated (story 56, 2026-07-18). 

4673 _git(["fetch", "--prune", "origin"]) 

4674 

4675 # Gate on the SAME ref the push will act on — the local branch, not HEAD. 

4676 # ``git push origin <branch>`` sends ``refs/heads/<branch>``; deciding 

4677 # "is there anything new?" from HEAD instead would be a proxy for the real 

4678 # artifact, and the two can differ (detached HEAD, a worktree left on 

4679 # another branch). If the local branch ref is missing, rev-list fails and we 

4680 # report a push error rather than guessing. 

4681 remote_ref = f"origin/{branch}" 

4682 exists = _git(["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{remote_ref}^{{commit}}"], timeout=30) 

4683 if exists is not None and exists.returncode == 0: 

4684 ahead = _git(["rev-list", "--count", f"{remote_ref}..{branch}"], timeout=60) 

4685 if ahead is None: 

4686 return False, "could not compare the branch with its remote" 

4687 if ahead.returncode != 0: 

4688 return False, f"git rev-list failed: {(ahead.stderr or '').strip()[:300]}" 

4689 try: 

4690 ahead_n = int((ahead.stdout or "0").strip() or "0") 

4691 except ValueError: 

4692 return False, "unparseable git rev-list output" 

4693 if ahead_n == 0: 

4694 # Genuinely nothing new. Say so out loud and let the 

4695 # identical-signature guard do its (correct) job. 

4696 _logger.info( 

4697 "story %s: no new commits to push to PR #%s; the remote head is current", 

4698 story.id, 

4699 story.github_pr_number, 

4700 ) 

4701 log_story_event( 

4702 story.id, 

4703 "fix_push_skipped_no_commits", 

4704 { 

4705 "branch": branch, 

4706 "pr_number": story.github_pr_number, 

4707 "note": ( 

4708 "the fix cycle produced no commit; the PR head is unchanged on " 

4709 "purpose so the identical-signature guard can park it" 

4710 ), 

4711 }, 

4712 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4713 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4714 ) 

4715 return False, None 

4716 # A missing remote branch means "never pushed / deleted upstream" — push. 

4717 

4718 push = _git(["push", "--force-with-lease", "origin", str(branch)], timeout=120) 

4719 ok = push is not None and push.returncode == 0 

4720 # ``state/events/git.ndjson`` is the stream whose ONE push line exposed this 

4721 # bug in the first place; make sure a fix push is visible there too, with 

4722 # the PR it belongs to. 

4723 try: 

4724 from factory.manager.signals import write_git_event as _wge 

4725 

4726 _wge( 

4727 kind="push", 

4728 story_id=story.id, 

4729 worktree_path=str(target_repo), 

4730 pr_number=story.github_pr_number, 

4731 result="ok" if ok else "error", 

4732 error=None if ok else ((push.stderr or "").strip()[:300] if push else "push_failed"), 

4733 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4734 ) 

4735 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - signal emission is best-effort 

4736 pass 

4737 if ok: 

4738 log_story_event( 

4739 story.id, 

4740 "fix_push", 

4741 {"branch": branch, "pr_number": story.github_pr_number}, 

4742 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4743 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4744 ) 

4745 return True, None 

4746 detail = "git push timed out or could not run" if push is None else (push.stderr or "").strip() 

4747 return False, f"git push --force-with-lease failed: {detail[:300]}" 

4748 

4749 

4750def handle_docs_enforcer( 

4751 story: StoryRecord, 

4752 app_config: AppConfig, 

4753 software_factory_root: Path, 

4754 *, 

4755 dry_run: bool = False, 

4756 db_path: Path | None = None, 

4757 pr_files: list[str] | None = None, 

4758 github_client: Any = None, 

4759) -> HandlerResult: 

4760 """Run the canonical-paths enforcer over the PR's file list. 

4761 

4762 Violations → REVIEWER_REQUESTED_CHANGES + label + comment. 

4763 Clean → PR_OPEN. Opens the GitHub PR programmatically when reached via 

4764 the docs chain (TDD path leaves PR creation to a future webhook). 

4765 

4766 In dry-run mode without an explicit ``pr_files`` list, we derive a 

4767 plausible set from the tech_writer result (so the enforcer sees the 

4768 same paths the tech_writer claimed to write). Docs chain populates the 

4769 same JSON field with its diff file list. 

4770 """ 

4771 db = db_path or (software_factory_root / "state" / "factory.db") 

4772 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_CHECK).value 

4773 persist_story(story, db) 

4774 

4775 files = pr_files 

4776 if files is None: 

4777 # Real runs: the authoritative file list is the branch's ACTUAL diff 

4778 # against base — the SAME source the reviewer approves on (see 

4779 # ``_fetch_pr_diff_for_review``) — NOT the tech_writer's self-declared 

4780 # ``context_updates``. A tech_writer that declares only a story-file 

4781 # "update" (story 130 / D109, 2026-07-23) otherwise makes the 

4782 # vacuous-diff guard below misfire on a branch that genuinely contains 

4783 # the code fix: the reviewer approves the real diff, the enforcer sees 

4784 # only ``stories/*.md`` in the declared list, bounces the story to 

4785 # reviewer_requested_changes, and the dev<->enforcer loop churns every 

4786 # cycle until the per-story budget dies. Dry-run has no worktree to 

4787 # diff, so it keeps deriving from the tech_writer result (the enforcer 

4788 # still sees the paths the writer claimed). 

4789 real_files = ( 

4790 _changed_files_for_story(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

4791 if not dry_run 

4792 else None 

4793 ) 

4794 if real_files is not None: 

4795 files = real_files 

4796 else: 

4797 # Fallback (dry-run, or the git diff could not be computed — e.g. 

4798 # the worktree was GC'd): derive from the tech_writer result. 

4799 files = [] 

4800 tw_raw = story.tech_writer_result_json or "{}" 

4801 try: 

4802 tw = json.loads(tw_raw) 

4803 for u in tw.get("context_updates") or []: 

4804 files.append(str(u.get("path"))) 

4805 except json.JSONDecodeError: 

4806 pass 

4807 

4808 violations = scan_pr_diff(files) 

4809 payload: dict[str, Any] = {"violations": [v._asdict() for v in violations], "files": files} 

4810 

4811 # Vacuous-diff guard. A deliverable with no substantive file — no code, no 

4812 # context/, no prd.md — delivered nothing. Two shapes, both blocked back to 

4813 # the dev loop rather than opened as a PR: 

4814 # 

4815 # * only ``stories/*.md`` — the story file is the WORK ORDER, not the work. 

4816 # scan_pr_diff can't catch it (stories/*.md is a canonical path, so a 

4817 # story-file-only diff scans clean — exactly how benchmark t7 "passed" 

4818 # 2026-07-17 with a diff that only added the seeded story file). 

4819 # * empty (``files == []``) — the branch changed nothing at all. Now 

4820 # reachable since we key off the REAL diff: an in-handler base re-merge 

4821 # (``_writing_worktree``) can absorb a sibling's identical fix, leaving 

4822 # an empty ``origin/base...HEAD``. Opening a PR on an empty branch fails 

4823 # ``gh pr create`` and would strand the story at PR_OPEN with 

4824 # pr_number=None (auto-merge matches PRs by number → silent limbo), so 

4825 # bounce instead. NOTE the condition is ``not substantive`` (not the old 

4826 # ``files and not substantive``): with real-diff semantics the empty 

4827 # case is a genuine no-op, not the old story-only misfire. 

4828 substantive = [f for f in files if f and not str(f).startswith("stories/")] 

4829 if not substantive: 

4830 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_FAIL).value 

4831 empty = not files 

4832 story.error = ( 

4833 "vacuous diff: branch changed nothing — no deliverable content" 

4834 if empty 

4835 else "vacuous diff: only story files changed — no deliverable content" 

4836 ) 

4837 payload["vacuous_diff"] = True 

4838 payload["empty_diff"] = empty 

4839 persist_story(story, db) 

4840 log_story_event( 

4841 story.id, 

4842 "vacuous_diff", 

4843 {"files": files[:20], "empty_diff": empty}, 

4844 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4845 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4846 ) 

4847 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload, error=story.error) 

4848 

4849 if violations: 

4850 # Real-run: post the comment + label the PR. 

4851 if not dry_run and github_client is not None and story.github_pr_number is not None: 

4852 try: 

4853 repo = github_client.get_repo(app_config.repo) 

4854 pr = repo.get_pull(story.github_pr_number) 

4855 pr.create_issue_comment(format_violation_comment(violations)) 

4856 pr.add_to_labels("canonical-paths-violation") 

4857 except Exception: # pragma: no cover - real-run path 

4858 pass 

4859 

4860 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_FAIL).value 

4861 story.error = f"canonical-paths violations: {len(violations)}" 

4862 persist_story(story, db) 

4863 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload, error=story.error) 

4864 

4865 # Open the PR programmatically for BOTH chains. The "separate worker" 

4866 # the TDD path historically deferred to was removed with the test-first 

4867 # machinery in the Loop-4 cleanup — without this, TDD stories reached 

4868 # PR_OPEN with github_pr_number=None and auto-merge (which matches open 

4869 # PRs to stories by number) could never merge them. Observed live 

4870 # 2026-06-11 on story 5, the first Loop-4 story to complete the chain. 

4871 if not dry_run and story.github_pr_number is None and story.github_branch: 

4872 # Pre-PR lint bounce (sacrifice story 183, 2026-08-09). NOTHING in the 

4873 # chain runs lint: an app's ``lint_command`` / ``format_check_command`` 

4874 # are config the chain records but never executes, and the pre-PR 

4875 # autoformat is deliberately conservative — it only deletes imports the 

4876 # BRANCH ITSELF added. A dev that edits a PRE-EXISTING file and orphans 

4877 # an import there therefore passes every chain gate and opens a PR whose 

4878 # required lint check is already doomed. 

4879 # 

4880 # WHY THAT USED TO BE FATAL — and what it is NOT. Story 183's evidence 

4881 # is explicit that the dev was NOT the problem: it received the CI 

4882 # findings and FIXED them (``response_bodies.ndjson``, 21:45:07 — the 

4883 # F401s and the E712 corrected), and ``_commit_green_dev_work`` 

4884 # committed the fix locally. The defect was downstream: nothing ever 

4885 # PUSHED that commit, because the only push site sat behind 

4886 # ``github_pr_number is None``. The PR head never moved, CI never 

4887 # re-ran, and the identical-signature guard adjudicated a stale sha and 

4888 # parked the story. That is fixed below (``_push_fix_to_existing_pr``). 

4889 # 

4890 # This bounce is the cheaper half of the same story: catching lint while 

4891 # the loop is still pre-PR and non-destructive costs one dev cycle 

4892 # instead of a CI round-trip. Capped at ``_MAX_LINT_BOUNCES``. 

4893 lint_bounces = _lint_bounces_so_far(story, software_factory_root) 

4894 # The check runs even when the cap is spent — it costs one ruff pass and 

4895 # it is the difference between "we know this PR is going to fail CI lint" 

4896 # and inferring it from a closed PR the next morning. 

4897 residual_lint = _residual_lint_for_story(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

4898 # A bounce is only worth spending if the story can still AFFORD the loop 

4899 # it is being sent round. Below the headroom threshold it would die at 

4900 # BLOCKED_BUDGET_EXCEEDED with no PR at all — worse than the lint-red PR 

4901 # this is trying to prevent. 

4902 has_headroom, remaining_attempts = _lint_bounce_budget_headroom( 

4903 story, software_factory_root 

4904 ) 

4905 if residual_lint and lint_bounces < _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES and not has_headroom: 

4906 payload["residual_lint"] = residual_lint 

4907 payload["lint_bounce_skipped_budget"] = True 

4908 log_story_event( 

4909 story.id, 

4910 "lint_bounce_skipped_budget", 

4911 { 

4912 "branch": story.github_branch, 

4913 "remaining_attempts": remaining_attempts, 

4914 "headroom_required": _LINT_BOUNCE_ATTEMPT_HEADROOM, 

4915 "total_attempts": story.total_attempts, 

4916 "note": ( 

4917 "too little attempt budget left to survive a bounce; opening the " 

4918 "PR so the work reaches GitHub instead of dying unpushed" 

4919 ), 

4920 "ruff_output": residual_lint, 

4921 }, 

4922 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4923 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4924 ) 

4925 elif residual_lint and lint_bounces < _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES: 

4926 # Same destination REVIEWER_REQUESTED_CHANGES as the canonical-paths 

4927 # violation above, via the only event DOCS_ENFORCER_CHECK has a 

4928 # transition for. (The tech_writer path reaches the same state with 

4929 # EVENT_REVIEWER_REQUEST_CHANGES, but that pair is not in the 

4930 # transition table from here and would raise IllegalTransitionError.) 

4931 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_FAIL).value 

4932 # Reuse the reviewer-findings plumbing verbatim — the same channel 

4933 # ``auto_merge`` uses for CI failures and merge conflicts. A 

4934 # well-formed finding DICT, never a bare string: every downstream 

4935 # consumer (runner._build_initial_message, _findings_signature, 

4936 # _append_reviewer_history) indexes findings with ``f.get(...)``. 

4937 finding = { 

4938 "severity": "high", 

4939 "criterion": "lint", 

4940 "location": "ruff (changed .py files on this branch)", 

4941 "what": ( 

4942 "Lint is RED on this branch's own changed Python files. The " 

4943 "app's required GitHub CI lint check runs the same ruff and " 

4944 "will block the PR, so fix every violation listed below " 

4945 "before this can ship. Note these are NOT all on lines you " 

4946 "added — a violation you introduced on a MODIFIED line of a " 

4947 "pre-existing file counts, and the pre-PR autoformat " 

4948 "deliberately will not touch it for you:\n\n" 

4949 f"{residual_lint}" 

4950 ), 

4951 "fix_suggestion": ( 

4952 "Resolve each reported violation in the file it names " 

4953 "(delete the unused import, use the variable, or make the " 

4954 "line comply). Do not add per-file ruff ignores to silence " 

4955 "them. Keep the tests green." 

4956 ), 

4957 } 

4958 story.reviewer_result_json = json.dumps( 

4959 { 

4960 "findings": [finding], 

4961 "source": "pre_pr_lint", 

4962 "summary": "Ruff is red on this branch's changed .py files; fix the " 

4963 "violations listed.", 

4964 } 

4965 ) 

4966 # Reset BOTH per-loop counters, mirroring the CI-fix re-dispatch and 

4967 # for the identical reason: this story is already reviewer-APPROVED, 

4968 # so ``reviewer_cycles`` may sit at the cap, and the follow-up review 

4969 # pass would otherwise trip BLOCKED_REVIEW_NONCONVERGENT on its first 

4970 # non-approving verdict and mislabel a lint nit as non-convergence. 

4971 # Safe against loops: the bounce cap is counted from the EVENT 

4972 # stream, which these resets cannot touch. 

4973 story.dev_retries = 0 

4974 story.reviewer_cycles = 0 

4975 story.error = ( 

4976 "pre-PR lint is red on the branch's changed .py files; returned to dev " 

4977 "with the violations (one bounce only — the next pass opens the PR and " 

4978 "lets GitHub CI adjudicate)" 

4979 ) 

4980 payload["residual_lint"] = residual_lint 

4981 payload["lint_bounce"] = True 

4982 persist_story(story, db) 

4983 log_story_event( 

4984 story.id, 

4985 "lint_bounce", 

4986 { 

4987 "branch": story.github_branch, 

4988 "bounce": lint_bounces + 1, 

4989 "cap": _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES, 

4990 "ruff_output": residual_lint, 

4991 }, 

4992 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

4993 slug_hint=story.slug, 

4994 ) 

4995 return HandlerResult( 

4996 next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload, error=story.error 

4997 ) 

4998 elif residual_lint: 

4999 # Still red after its one bounce. Open the PR regardless and let the 

5000 # real CI rule — loudly, so a repeat offender is visible in the 

5001 # trace. The old path (CI red → ci-fix → identical signature → park) 

5002 # remains exactly the backstop it was; a second bounce would be a 

5003 # new uncapped loop. 

5004 payload["residual_lint"] = residual_lint 

5005 payload["lint_bounce_capped"] = True 

5006 log_story_event( 

5007 story.id, 

5008 "lint_bounce_capped", 

5009 { 

5010 "branch": story.github_branch, 

5011 "bounces": lint_bounces, 

5012 "cap": _MAX_LINT_BOUNCES, 

5013 "ruff_output": residual_lint, 

5014 "note": "opening the PR anyway; GitHub CI is the adjudicator", 

5015 }, 

5016 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

5017 slug_hint=story.slug, 

5018 ) 

5019 opened = _open_pr_for_story(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

5020 if opened is not None: 

5021 story.github_pr_number = opened 

5022 story.pr_create_retries = 0 

5023 story.error = None 

5024 story.last_rejection_reason = None 

5025 persist_story(story, db) 

5026 payload["pr_number"] = opened 

5027 else: 

5028 # S4 (019 fail-silent audit): this USED TO fall through to 

5029 # EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_PASS anyway — the story advanced to 

5030 # PR_OPEN with github_pr_number still None, a state with NO 

5031 # ``orchestrator._DISPATCH`` entry, so nothing ever drove it 

5032 # again. The only trace was a ``git_op result=error`` line in 

5033 # ``state/events/git.ndjson`` — absent from `factory inbox` and 

5034 # from GitHub. Refuse the transition instead: stay in 

5035 # DOCS_ENFORCER_CHECK (which DOES have a dispatch entry, so the 

5036 # next tick retries `_open_pr_for_story` for free — no LLM call, 

5037 # `github_pr_number` is still None) and surface the failure via 

5038 # `error`/`last_rejection_reason` so `factory inbox` lists it. 

5039 # Bounded by `_MAX_PR_CREATE_RETRIES` (strictly below the hard 

5040 # cap of 3) so a persistently broken `gh`/push doesn't retry 

5041 # forever; past that it parks at BLOCKED_DEPLOY_FAILED. 

5042 story.pr_create_retries += 1 

5043 reason = ( 

5044 f"gh pr create failed for branch {story.github_branch!r} " 

5045 f"(attempt {story.pr_create_retries}/{_MAX_PR_CREATE_RETRIES}); " 

5046 "see state/events/git.ndjson for the git_op error" 

5047 ) 

5048 payload["pr_create_failed"] = True 

5049 payload["pr_create_retries"] = story.pr_create_retries 

5050 if story.pr_create_retries >= _MAX_PR_CREATE_RETRIES: 

5051 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_PR_CREATE_EXHAUSTED).value 

5052 reason = f"{reason} — retries exhausted, parked for human action" 

5053 story.error = reason 

5054 story.last_rejection_reason = reason 

5055 persist_story(story, db) 

5056 log_story_event( 

5057 story.id, 

5058 "pr_create_failed", 

5059 { 

5060 "branch": story.github_branch, 

5061 "retries": story.pr_create_retries, 

5062 "exhausted": story.pr_create_retries >= _MAX_PR_CREATE_RETRIES, 

5063 }, 

5064 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

5065 slug_hint=story.slug, 

5066 ) 

5067 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload, error=reason) 

5068 

5069 elif not dry_run and story.github_pr_number is not None and story.github_branch: 

5070 # POST-PR FIX CYCLE — the story already has a PR and has just come back 

5071 # round through dev (CI failure, reviewer changes, or the lint bounce 

5072 # above). Its fix is committed in the worktree and, until this existed, 

5073 # was never pushed anywhere: the branch above is the ONLY place the 

5074 # chain pushed a story's work, and it is gated on 

5075 # ``github_pr_number is None``. See ``_push_fix_to_existing_pr`` for 

5076 # story 183's evidence. Push it, so the PR head moves and GitHub 

5077 # actually re-runs CI on the fix. 

5078 pushed, push_error = _push_fix_to_existing_pr(story, app_config, software_factory_root) 

5079 payload["fix_pushed"] = pushed 

5080 if push_error: 

5081 # Do NOT block the transition: PR_OPEN is where auto-merge can see 

5082 # the story, and refusing to advance would strand it. But the park 

5083 # that follows must NAME this — a failed push swallowed in silence 

5084 # is the exact failure class being fixed here, one level up. 

5085 payload["fix_push_error"] = push_error 

5086 story.error = ( 

5087 f"fix commits were NOT pushed to PR #{story.github_pr_number}: {push_error}. " 

5088 "The PR head is stale, so its CI verdict does not describe the current " 

5089 "work — re-push the branch by hand before trusting any red on it." 

5090 ) 

5091 _logger.error("story %s: %s", story.id, story.error) 

5092 log_story_event( 

5093 story.id, 

5094 "fix_push_failed", 

5095 { 

5096 "branch": story.github_branch, 

5097 "pr_number": story.github_pr_number, 

5098 "error": push_error, 

5099 }, 

5100 software_factory_root=software_factory_root, 

5101 slug_hint=story.slug, 

5102 ) 

5103 persist_story(story, db) 

5104 

5105 story.state = advance(story, EVENT_DOCS_ENFORCER_PASS).value 

5106 persist_story(story, db) 

5107 return HandlerResult(next_state=StoryState(story.state), payload=payload) 

5108 

5109 

5110def _post_factory_needs_redesign_comment( 

5111 *, 

5112 story: StoryRecord, 

5113 app_config: AppConfig, 

5114 suggestions: list[str], 

5115 last_tail: str, 

5116 software_factory_root: Path, 

5117) -> None: 

5118 """Post a 'factory needs redesign' comment on the direction's tracker issue. 

5119 

5120 Operator-loud signal that the chain ran out of dev retries on a small 

5121 story — likely the factory itself needs work (test_implementer wrote 

5122 impossible tests, persona prompt missing context, env/runtime gap, 

5123 etc.) rather than dev needing more chances. 

5124 

5125 Best-effort: silently no-ops when ``gh`` isn't on PATH, the direction 

5126 has no tracker_issue recorded, or the call fails. The structured 

5127 event log entry is the durable record; this comment is the surface. 

5128 """ 

5129 direction = find_direction_for_story(story, software_factory_root) 

5130 if direction is None: 

5131 return 

5132 tracker = direction.state.get("tracker_issue") if hasattr(direction, "state") else None 

5133 if not tracker: 

5134 return 

5135 repo = f"{app_config.repo_owner}/{app_config.repo_name}" 

5136 body_parts = [ 

5137 f"## :warning: factory_needs_redesign — story #{story.id} ({story.slug})", 

5138 "", 

5139 f"Dev exhausted **{story.dev_retries}/{_max_dev_retries(software_factory_root)}** chain-level " 

5140 f"retries with prior-attempt feed-forward enabled. That's a strong " 

5141 f"signal something upstream of dev needs work — not that dev needs more chances.", 

5142 "", 

5143 f"- Branch: `{story.github_branch}`", 

5144 f"- Story slug: `{story.slug}`", 

5145 f"- Direction: `{story.direction_id}`", 

5146 "", 

5147 "### Suggestions", 

5148 ] 

5149 for s in suggestions: 

5150 body_parts.append(f"- {s}") 

5151 if last_tail.strip(): 

5152 body_parts += [ 

5153 "", 

5154 "### Last test-output tail", 

5155 "```", 

5156 last_tail[-1500:], 

5157 "```", 

5158 ] 

5159 body_parts.append("") 

5160 body_parts.append(f"Inspect via `factory trace {story.id}` for the per-attempt event log.") 

5161 body = "\n".join(body_parts) 

5162 

5163 import subprocess 

5164 

5165 subprocess.run( 

5166 ["gh", "issue", "comment", str(tracker), "--repo", repo, "--body", body], 

5167 check=False, 

5168 timeout=30, 

5169 capture_output=True, 

5170 ) 

5171 

5172 

5173def _changed_py_lint_scope( 

5174 target_repo: Path, base: str, app_config: AppConfig | None = None 

5175) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], str] | None: 

5176 """``(changed .py files, ruff isolation flags, resolved base ref)``, or ``None``. 

5177 

5178 ``None`` means "there is nothing for ruff to do here": the repo/app does not 

5179 use ruff, the base ref could not be resolved, git failed, or the branch 

5180 changed no ``.py`` file. 

5181 

5182 Shared by :func:`_autoformat_changed_py_before_pr` (which FIXES what it 

5183 safely can) and :func:`_residual_changed_py_lint` (which REPORTS what is 

5184 left). They MUST agree on both halves or the residual check would grade the 

5185 branch under different rules than the autoformat just applied — and, worse, 

5186 under different rules than the app's own CI lint. Hence one function. 

5187 

5188 ``--isolated`` reproduces the app's CI exactly when the app has no ruff 

5189 config of its own: the per-story worktree is physically nested under the 

5190 factory repo, so a bare ``ruff check`` would walk up and pick the FACTORY's 

5191 ``[tool.ruff]`` (line-length 100) instead of the built-in defaults 

5192 (line-length 88) the app's ``ruff check .`` actually runs under. Ruff 

5193 resolves config by nearest ancestor, and the nearest ancestor here is the 

5194 wrong repo. 

5195 """ 

5196 import subprocess 

5197 

5198 # Only for repos/apps that actually use ruff — otherwise a ``ruff format`` 

5199 # would be meaningless / could touch code the repo's own CI does not lint. 

5200 # Detection: a ruff config file, ``[tool.ruff*]`` in pyproject, OR the app's 

5201 # configured lint/format gate command invokes ruff (sacrifice runs 

5202 # default-config ``ruff check .`` with NO ``[tool.ruff]`` table). 

5203 local_config = (target_repo / "ruff.toml").exists() or (target_repo / ".ruff.toml").exists() 

5204 if not local_config: 

5205 pyproject = target_repo / "pyproject.toml" 

5206 if pyproject.exists(): 

5207 try: 

5208 # Matches ``[tool.ruff]`` and any sub-table (``[tool.ruff.lint]``, 

5209 # ``[tool.ruff.format]``) — a repo may configure only a sub-table. 

5210 local_config = "[tool.ruff" in pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8") 

5211 except OSError: 

5212 local_config = False 

5213 has_ruff = local_config 

5214 if not has_ruff and app_config is not None: 

5215 gate_cmds = " ".join( 

5216 c 

5217 for c in ( 

5218 getattr(app_config.gates, "lint_command", None), 

5219 getattr(app_config.gates, "format_check_command", None), 

5220 ) 

5221 if c 

5222 ) 

5223 has_ruff = "ruff" in gate_cmds 

5224 if not has_ruff: 

5225 return None 

5226 

5227 iso = ["--isolated"] if not local_config else [] 

5228 

5229 # ``origin/<base>`` normally; local ``<base>`` when the worktree has no 

5230 # ``origin`` remote (bench harness / local-only app repo). Same fallback 

5231 # ``_changed_files_for_story`` and the reviewer's pre-PR diff use, so all 

5232 # three agree on "what this branch changed". In production topology this 

5233 # always resolves to ``origin/<base>`` — the fallback only fires where the 

5234 # old hard-coded ``origin/<base>`` silently did nothing at all. 

5235 base_ref = _resolve_diff_base(target_repo, base) 

5236 if base_ref is None: 

5237 return None 

5238 try: 

5239 diff = subprocess.run( 

5240 ["git", "diff", "--name-only", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"], 

5241 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5242 capture_output=True, 

5243 text=True, 

5244 errors="replace", 

5245 check=False, 

5246 timeout=60, 

5247 ) 

5248 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError): 

5249 return None 

5250 if diff.returncode != 0: 

5251 return None 

5252 py_files = [f for f in diff.stdout.split() if f.endswith(".py") and (target_repo / f).is_file()] 

5253 if not py_files: 

5254 return None 

5255 return py_files, iso, base_ref 

5256 

5257 

5258# Bound on how much ruff output rides along in the synthetic finding fed back to 

5259# dev. Concise format is one line per violation; 4000 chars is ~50 lines, far 

5260# more than a story's own changed files ever produce, while keeping the dev 

5261# prompt from being swamped by a pathological run. 

5262_RESIDUAL_LINT_MAX_CHARS = 4000 

5263 

5264 

5265def _residual_changed_py_lint( 

5266 target_repo: Path, base: str, app_config: AppConfig | None = None 

5267) -> str | None: 

5268 """Ruff findings still on the branch's changed ``.py`` files, or ``None``. 

5269 

5270 Run AFTER :func:`_autoformat_changed_py_before_pr`, so what comes back is 

5271 exactly what the conservative autoformat could NOT fix for itself — the 

5272 F401 on a MODIFIED line of a PRE-EXISTING file being the shape that opened 

5273 sacrifice story 183's PR lint-red (2026-08-09). The autoformat only ever 

5274 deletes imports the branch itself added; a dev that edits an old file and 

5275 orphans an import there sails past it and past every chain gate, because no 

5276 chain gate runs lint at all — an app's ``lint_command`` / 

5277 ``format_check_command`` are config the chain records but never executes. 

5278 

5279 BOTH CI lint commands are reproduced, because an app's CI runs two: 

5280 ``ruff check`` AND ``ruff format --check`` (see ``gates.lint_command`` / 

5281 ``gates.format_check_command`` in ``apps/*/config.yaml``; sacrifice and the 

5282 factory both configure the pair). Checking only the former would still ship 

5283 a PR doomed by a format-only red — the exact failure shape this function 

5284 exists to prevent, one command over. 

5285 

5286 VERSION SKEW CAVEAT: ``ruff format`` output is version-dependent, so the 

5287 locally-installed ruff and the app's CI ruff can legitimately disagree about 

5288 what "formatted" means. The consequences are both benign and bounded: a 

5289 local-only red costs at most ONE capped bounce (and the dev is handed the 

5290 concrete file list), and a CI-only red is exactly today's behavior. Do NOT 

5291 "harden" this into anything that can block the PR permanently. 

5292 

5293 Same scope and same ruff config as the autoformat (see 

5294 :func:`_changed_py_lint_scope`). 

5295 

5296 NEVER raises, and FAILS OPEN (returns ``None``) on anything that is not an 

5297 unambiguous finding report: missing ``uv``/``ruff``, a timeout, a ruff usage 

5298 error (exit 2), an empty report. GitHub CI is the authoritative lint 

5299 backstop; this check is an optimization that saves a doomed PR round-trip. 

5300 Blocking PR creation because the LOCAL ruff is broken would trade a bounded, 

5301 already-handled failure for a new unbounded one. 

5302 """ 

5303 import subprocess 

5304 

5305 scope = _changed_py_lint_scope(target_repo, base, app_config) 

5306 if scope is None: 

5307 return None 

5308 py_files, iso, _base_ref = scope 

5309 

5310 def _probe(args: list[str], label: str) -> str | None: 

5311 """Report text for one ruff command, or ``None`` (clean OR inconclusive).""" 

5312 try: 

5313 proc = subprocess.run( 

5314 args, 

5315 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5316 capture_output=True, 

5317 text=True, 

5318 errors="replace", 

5319 check=False, 

5320 timeout=180, 

5321 ) 

5322 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc: 

5323 _logger.warning( 

5324 "residual %s skipped (fail-open; GitHub CI remains the backstop): %s", label, exc 

5325 ) 

5326 return None 

5327 if proc.returncode == 0: 

5328 return None 

5329 out = (proc.stdout or "").strip() 

5330 if proc.returncode != 1 or not out: 

5331 # Exit 2 = ruff itself errored (bad config, unreadable file); exit 1 

5332 # with no stdout should not happen. Neither is evidence of a real 

5333 # finding, so do not bounce on it. 

5334 _logger.warning( 

5335 "residual %s inconclusive (rc=%s, fail-open): %s", 

5336 label, 

5337 proc.returncode, 

5338 (proc.stderr or "")[-500:], 

5339 ) 

5340 return None 

5341 return out 

5342 

5343 reports: list[str] = [] 

5344 check_out = _probe( 

5345 ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "--output-format", "concise", *iso, *py_files], 

5346 "lint check", 

5347 ) 

5348 if check_out: 

5349 reports.append(f"$ ruff check\n{check_out}") 

5350 format_out = _probe( 

5351 ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", "--check", *iso, *py_files], 

5352 "format check", 

5353 ) 

5354 if format_out: 

5355 reports.append(f"$ ruff format --check\n{format_out}") 

5356 if not reports: 

5357 return None 

5358 return "\n\n".join(reports)[:_RESIDUAL_LINT_MAX_CHARS] 

5359 

5360 

5361def _autoformat_changed_py_before_pr( 

5362 target_repo: Path, base: str, app_config: AppConfig | None = None 

5363) -> None: 

5364 """Best-effort: make the story's own changed ``.py`` files ruff-clean and 

5365 commit the result before the PR is opened. 

5366 

5367 Two scoped passes on the branch's OWN changed files (never a whole-repo 

5368 reformat): 

5369 1. ``ruff check --fix --select F401`` restricted to imports the BRANCH 

5370 ITSELF added — an unused import the dev just added is safe to delete; 

5371 a pre-existing (possibly side-effect) import is never touched (the file 

5372 is reverted if the fix would remove a line the branch didn't add). 

5373 2. ``ruff check --fix --select I`` (import-sort) + ``ruff format`` — the 

5374 non-semantic nits. 

5375 

5376 Rationale: a factory self-edit (PR #57) shipped with an ``I001`` unsorted 

5377 import; sacrifice PRs (#301/#293/#286/#275, 2026-07-21) sat lint-blocked on 

5378 ``F401`` unused imports the dev left in its own new/changed files. The 

5379 chain's pre-merge gates (tests-green / smoke / staging-clone) do NOT run 

5380 ``ruff``, so the nit only surfaced at GitHub's required lint check — blocking 

5381 the merge and, via auto-merge-enabled, stranding the story. Making the 

5382 pushed branch ruff-clean removes that class of false-block. 

5383 

5384 Safe: scoped to ``origin/<base>...HEAD`` changed files, F401 only ever 

5385 deletes branch-added imports, no-op when the repo/app doesn't use ruff, and 

5386 NEVER raises — a formatting hiccup must not block PR creation. 

5387 """ 

5388 import subprocess 

5389 

5390 # Which files, and under which ruff config — see ``_changed_py_lint_scope``. 

5391 # Shared with ``_residual_changed_py_lint`` so "what was fixed" and "what is 

5392 # left" are computed over the identical scope and rules. 

5393 scope = _changed_py_lint_scope(target_repo, base, app_config) 

5394 if scope is None: 

5395 return 

5396 py_files, iso, base_ref = scope 

5397 

5398 # Pass 1 — remove the auto-fixable pyflakes nits the dev leaves in its OWN 

5399 # new code, restricted to the branch's OWN added lines. A blanket ``ruff 

5400 # check --fix`` under the full ruleset (E/F/I/W/UP/B) could delete a 

5401 # PRE-EXISTING side-effect import or rewrite typing and, since the code is 

5402 # NOT re-tested after this step, break CI and re-create the strand. So a 

5403 # given rule is fixed in a file ONLY when EVERY violation of that rule sits 

5404 # on a line THIS branch added (decided from ruff's line numbers vs the diff 

5405 # hunks BEFORE fixing). Codes handled: F401 (unused import), F541 (f-string 

5406 # without placeholders), F841 (unused local variable) — exactly the F-class 

5407 # nits a human hand-fixed on #349/#351. A pre-existing violation of any of 

5408 # these is left for the dev loop / CI, never silently mutated here. 

5409 _strip_own_added_fixable_lint(target_repo, base_ref, py_files, iso) 

5410 

5411 try: 

5412 # Pass 2 — NON-SEMANTIC nits: import-sorting (``--select I``) plus 

5413 # ``ruff format`` (I001 unsorted imports, missing trailing newline, 

5414 # whitespace) — exactly PR #57's failure. These never change behavior. 

5415 subprocess.run( 

5416 ["uv", "run", "ruff", "check", "--fix", "--select", "I", *iso, *py_files], 

5417 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5418 check=False, 

5419 capture_output=True, 

5420 timeout=180, 

5421 ) 

5422 subprocess.run( 

5423 ["uv", "run", "ruff", "format", *iso, *py_files], 

5424 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5425 check=False, 

5426 capture_output=True, 

5427 timeout=180, 

5428 ) 

5429 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError): 

5430 return 

5431 

5432 # Commit only if ruff actually changed something. 

5433 try: 

5434 status = subprocess.run( 

5435 ["git", "status", "--porcelain", *py_files], 

5436 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5437 capture_output=True, 

5438 text=True, 

5439 check=False, 

5440 timeout=30, 

5441 ) 

5442 if status.returncode == 0 and status.stdout.strip(): 

5443 # Pathspec-scoped add+commit: only the story's own py files are 

5444 # committed, even if some earlier step left unrelated staged content 

5445 # in the index. The trailing ``-- <files>`` keeps the commit tight. 

5446 subprocess.run( 

5447 ["git", "add", "--", *py_files], 

5448 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5449 check=False, 

5450 capture_output=True, 

5451 timeout=30, 

5452 ) 

5453 subprocess.run( 

5454 [ 

5455 "git", 

5456 "commit", 

5457 "-m", 

5458 "style: ruff F401/F541/F841 (own added lines) + isort + format (pre-PR autoformat)", 

5459 "--", 

5460 *py_files, 

5461 ], 

5462 cwd=str(target_repo), 

5463 check=False, 

5464 capture_output=True, 

5465 timeout=60, 

5466 ) 

5467 except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError): 

5468 return 

5469 

5470 

5471def _added_line_numbers(diff_text: str) -> set[int]: 

5472 """New-file line numbers of the lines a unified diff ADDS. 

5473 

5474 Walks hunk headers (``@@ -a,b +c,d @@``) and counts ``+``/context lines in 

5475 the new-file coordinate system, so we can ask "was line N added by this 

5476 branch?" positionally — content matching alone is unsafe (a pre-existing 

5477 import can share text with an unrelated branch-added line). 

5478 """ 

5479 import re 

5480 

5481 added: set[int] = set() 

5482 new_ln = 0 

5483 for line in diff_text.splitlines(): 

5484 if line.startswith("@@"): 

5485 m = re.search(r"\+(\d+)", line) 

5486 new_ln = int(m.group(1)) if m else 0 

5487 continue 

5488 if line.startswith(("+++", "---")): 

5489 continue 

5490 if line.startswith("+"): 

5491 added.add(new_ln) 

5492 new_ln += 1 

5493 elif line.startswith("-"): 

5494 continue # old-only line — does not advance the new-file counter 

5495 else: 

5496 new_ln += 1 # context line 

5497 return added 

5498 

5499 

5500# The auto-fixable pyflakes nits stripped from the story's OWN added lines, 

5501# mapped to whether ruff classifies the fix as "unsafe" (needs ``--unsafe-fixes``). 

5502# F401 unused import — safe fix: delete the import. 

5503# F541 f-string, no placeholder — safe fix: drop the ``f`` prefix. 

5504# F841 unused local variable — UNSAFE fix: ruff rewrites ``x = call()`` to a 

5505# bare ``call()`` (the binding goes, the side-effecting RHS stays), so it 

5506# is behaviorally safe but ruff still gates it behind ``--unsafe-fixes``. 

5507# (E402 module-import-not-at-top is intentionally absent: ruff ships no autofix 

5508# for it, so nothing to do here — the dev loop / CI reorders those.) 

5509_OWN_LINE_FIXABLE_CODES: dict[str, bool] = {"F401": False, "F541": False, "F841": True} 

5510 

5511 

5512def _removed_line_numbers(diff_text: str) -> set[int]: 

5513 """OLD-file line numbers of the lines a unified diff REMOVES or ALTERS. 

5514
